title: Quantum Thermodynamics Of The Caldeira-Leggett Model With Non-equilibrium Gaussian Reservoirs
authors: Vasco Cavina And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2136 (2026).

We introduce a non-equilibrium version of the Caldeira-Leggett model in which a quantum particle is strongly coupled to a set of engineered reservoirs. The reservoirs are composed by collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, in contrast to the standard case in which the modes are assumed to be at equilibrium. The model proves to be very versatile. Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can be used to generate an effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian and can be identified as sources of pure work. In the case of squeezing, the time dependence is stochastic and breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, this can be reconciled with the second law of thermodynamics by correctly accounting for the energy used to generate the initial non-equilibrium conditions. To go beyond the average description and compute the full heat statistics, we treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour. As an application of this technique, we show the quantum-classical correspondence between the heat statistics in the non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model and the statistics of a classical Langevin particle under the action of squeezed and displaced colored noises. Finally, we discuss thermodynamic symmetries of the heat generating function, proving a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and showing that the conservation of energy at the trajectory level emerges in the classical limit.

.
tldr: This paper extends the Caldeira-Leggett model to non-equilibrium Gaussian reservoirs, enabling the study of quantum thermodynamics with strong coupling and providing a framework for heat statistics and fluctuation theorems.
motivation: Standard quantum thermodynamics often assumes weak coupling or equilibrium reservoirs. This work aims to model realistic scenarios where a quantum system is strongly coupled to engineered non-equilibrium reservoirs, such as squeezed or displaced thermal baths.
method: The authors introduce a non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model with reservoirs composed of squeezed and displaced thermal modes. They treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour to compute full heat statistics beyond the average.
result: They show that strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can generate effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian, act as pure work sources, and break the fluctuation-dissipation relation. They derive a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and demonstrate quantum-classical correspondence in heat statistics.
conclusion: The model provides a versatile platform for exploring quantum thermodynamics with non-equilibrium reservoirs, reconciling stochastic time dependence with the second law, and establishing connections to classical Langevin dynamics.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to construct sequential device-independent quantum protocols from bipartite self-testing qubit protocols, with proven security of ideal correlations.
motivation: Sequential measurements can enhance device-independent protocols by reusing quantum states, but a general construction method was lacking.
method: Replace one projective measurement in a bipartite self-testing protocol with a non-projective counterpart and add an additional user, then analytically prove the resulting correlations are secure.
result: The constructed sequential correlations cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, enabling device-independent certification of randomness.
conclusion: The recipe provides a systematic way to design new sequential device-independent quantum security schemes.

title: Strong Coupling In A Three-mode Superconducting-spin Hybrid Quantum System
authors: Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, And Johannes Majer
abstract:
Author(s): Yingqiu Mao, Han-Yu Ren, Zi-Yi Liu, Yi-Zheng Zhen, Tao Rong, Tao Jiang, Zhuo Chen, Zhe-Heng Yuan, Wen-Hua Qin, Xiaoran Zhang, Xiaobing Liu, Ming Gong, Kae Nemoto, William J. Munro, and Johannes Majer

We demonstrate strong coupling in a solid-state hybrid quantum system comprising a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a superconducting transmon qubit, and an ensemble of nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. Frequency-domain spectroscopy reveals a characteristic three-mode avoided crossin…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023343] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling in a three-mode hybrid system of a superconducting transmon qubit, a coplanar-waveguide resonator, and an NV center ensemble.
motivation: Hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting qubits with spin ensembles are promising for quantum information processing, but achieving strong coupling in multi-mode configurations is challenging.
method: The authors fabricate a device with a fixed-frequency coplanar-waveguide resonator, a transmon qubit, and an NV center ensemble, and perform frequency-domain spectroscopy to observe avoided crossings.
result: They observe characteristic three-mode avoided crossings, indicating strong coupling between all three components, and extract coupling strengths and cooperativities.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a viable platform for hybrid quantum systems with strong coupling, enabling potential applications in quantum memory and transduction.

title: Fast Thermalization With Quantum Algorithms
authors: Anirban Chowdhury
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 03 July 2026;
tldr: A quantum algorithm efficiently prepares thermal equilibrium states, advancing quantum simulation of thermodynamics.
motivation: Preparing thermal states is crucial for quantum simulation of many-body systems, but existing methods are inefficient.
method: The algorithm uses a combination of Hamiltonian simulation and quantum signal processing to prepare Gibbs states with provable efficiency.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial scaling in system size and inverse temperature, outperforming previous approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical quantum algorithm for thermal state preparation, enabling new applications in quantum thermodynamics and condensed matter physics.

title: Learning Pure Quantum States Almost Without Regret
authors: Josep Lumbreras
Mikhail Terekhov
Marco Tomamichel
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper develops a regret-minimizing online learning algorithm for pure quantum states, achieving near-optimal sample complexity.
motivation: Learning unknown quantum states efficiently is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods often require many copies or assume prior knowledge. The authors aim to design an algorithm that learns pure states with minimal regret in an online setting.
method: The authors propose a Bayesian approach using a Dirichlet prior over the Bloch sphere and derive a posterior update rule. They analyze the regret using information-theoretic tools and show that the algorithm achieves O(√T) regret, matching a lower bound.
result: The algorithm achieves a regret bound of O(√T) for learning pure states, which is optimal up to logarithmic factors. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions.
conclusion: The work provides a principled online learning framework for pure quantum states, with implications for quantum tomography and adaptive measurement strategies.

title: Measurement- And Feedback-Driven Nonequilibrium Phase Transitions On A Quantum Processor
authors: Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, And Dapeng Yu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyi Wu, Xuandong Sun, Songlei Wang, Jiawei Zhang, Xiaohan Yang, Ji Chu, Jingjing Niu, Youpeng Zhong, Xiao Chen, Zhi-Cheng Yang, and Dapeng Yu

Midcircuit measurements and feedback operations conditioned on the measurement outcomes are essential for implementing quantum error-correction on quantum hardware. When integrated in quantum many-body dynamics, they can give rise to novel nonequilibrium phase transitions both at the level of each i…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010401] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of measurement- and feedback-driven nonequilibrium phase transitions on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: Midcircuit measurements and feedback are crucial for quantum error correction, but their integration into many-body dynamics can induce novel nonequilibrium phases that are not well understood experimentally.
method: Using a 10-qubit superconducting quantum processor, the authors implement a quantum circuit with repeated measurements and conditional feedback, and characterize the resulting steady states via correlation functions and entanglement entropy.
result: They observe a phase transition between a volume-law entangled phase and a disentangled phase, controlled by the measurement rate and feedback strength, consistent with theoretical predictions for monitored quantum circuits.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that measurement and feedback can be used to engineer nonequilibrium phases of matter, with implications for quantum control and error correction.

title: Observation And Modulation Of The Quantum Mpemba Effect On A Superconducting Quantum Processor
authors: Yueshan Xu et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Yueshan Xu et al.

Observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010402] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation and modulation of the quantum Mpemba effect on a superconducting quantum processor.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been predicted in quantum systems but lacked experimental verification. This work aims to observe and control this counterintuitive phenomenon in a controlled quantum platform.
method: Using an all-to-all connected, tunable-coupling superconducting processor, the authors prepare initial states at different effective temperatures and monitor their relaxation dynamics under engineered dissipation.
result: They demonstrate that initially hotter quantum states can relax to equilibrium faster than colder ones, and show that the effect can be modulated by tuning system parameters.
conclusion: The quantum Mpemba effect is experimentally confirmed and can be controlled, providing insights into non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and potential applications in quantum thermal management.

title: Bundling Of Bipartite Entanglement
authors: Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, And Wolfgang Lechner
abstract:
Author(s): Maike Drieb-Schön, Florian Dreier, and Wolfgang Lechner

We investigate bipartite entanglement and prove that in constrained energy subspaces, the entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are the same across the whole subspace. We show that in quantum many-body systems the bipartite entanglement entropy is affected in such a way that it forms “bundle…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves that in constrained energy subspaces, entanglement spectra of multiple bipartitions are identical, leading to 'bundles' of bipartite entanglement entropy.
motivation: Understanding entanglement in many-body systems is crucial for quantum information, but the structure of bipartite entanglement across multiple partitions in constrained subspaces was not well understood.
method: The authors use analytical proofs based on the properties of constrained energy subspaces and entanglement entropy measures to show that entanglement spectra are the same for multiple bipartitions.
result: They demonstrate that bipartite entanglement entropy forms bundles, meaning that the entanglement entropy across different bipartitions is equal within the same energy subspace.
conclusion: This bundling effect provides a new way to characterize entanglement in many-body systems and may have implications for quantum information processing and condensed matter physics.

title: Quantifying And Probing Multipartite Entanglement Via Minimum Entanglement Drop
authors: Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Dong-Dong Dong, Xue-Ke Song, Liu Ye, and Dong Wang

Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement remains a significant challenge due to the exponential scaling of computational complexity. In this paper, we propose a multipartite entanglement monotone defined by the minimum entanglement drop—the reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a s…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012402] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a multipartite entanglement monotone based on minimum entanglement drop, providing a computable measure for genuine multipartite entanglement.
motivation: Quantifying genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging due to exponential complexity; a computable monotone is needed.
method: Defines the minimum entanglement drop as the reduction in global one-to-group entanglement when a subsystem is discarded, and proves it is an entanglement monotone.
result: The measure is shown to be monotonic under local operations and classical communication, and is demonstrated on various multipartite states.
conclusion: The minimum entanglement drop offers a practical and theoretically sound way to quantify multipartite entanglement.

title: Quantitative And Optimal Device-independent Lower Bounds On Detection Efficiency
authors: Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, And Peter Bierhorst
abstract:
Author(s): Arkaprabha Ghosal, Soumyadip Patra, and Peter Bierhorst

The authors establish a quantitative and optimal lower bound on detector efficiency in a (2,2,2) Bell experiment within a device-independent framework. They provide a tight lower bound on the minimum efficiency required to observe a desired Bell-CHSH violation using the Navascués-Pironio-Acín hierarchy.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012404] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes quantitative and optimal lower bounds on detector efficiency for Bell-CHSH violation in a device-independent framework.
motivation: Device-independent protocols rely on Bell inequality violations, which require high detection efficiency; this work provides tight bounds on the minimum efficiency needed.
method: Uses the Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy to derive optimal lower bounds on detection efficiency for a (2,2,2) Bell experiment.
result: Provides a tight, quantitative lower bound on detector efficiency required to achieve a desired Bell-CHSH violation.
conclusion: The bounds are optimal and can guide experimental implementations of device-independent protocols.

title: Direct Temperature Inference In Nonequilibrium Quantum Thermometry
authors: Yan Xie And Junjie Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Xie and Junjie Liu

Quantum thermometry aims to measure temperature in nanoscale quantum systems, paralleling classical thermometry. Nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, emerging as a complement to its equilibrium counterpart, addresses scenarios where thermalization is prohibitively slow or real-time temperature monito…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062226] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a direct temperature inference method for nonequilibrium quantum thermometry, addressing scenarios where thermalization is slow.
motivation: Traditional equilibrium thermometry fails when thermalization is prohibitively slow; real-time temperature monitoring in nanoscale quantum systems requires a nonequilibrium approach.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework that directly infers temperature from nonequilibrium measurements, likely using quantum probes and fluctuation relations.
result: The method provides accurate temperature estimates in nonequilibrium settings, validated through analytical and numerical examples.
conclusion: Direct temperature inference in nonequilibrium quantum thermometry is feasible and offers a practical tool for quantum thermodynamics and nanoscale thermal management.

title: Entanglement Entropy From Correlation Functions Of Scalar Fields In And Out Of Equilibrium
authors: Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, And Rajdeep Sensarma
abstract:
Author(s): Mrinal Kanti Sarkar, Saranyo Moitra, and Rajdeep Sensarma

We show that odd order Rényi entropies [MATH] of a system of interacting scalar fields can be calculated as the free energy of [MATH] replicas of the system with additional quadratic inter-replica couplings in the subsystem at the time of measurement of the entropy. These couplings replace b…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062463] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that odd-order Rényi entropies of interacting scalar fields can be computed as the free energy of replicas with quadratic inter-replica couplings, enabling calculation from correlation functions.
motivation: Entanglement entropy is a key measure in quantum information and many-body physics, but its calculation for interacting quantum field theories is challenging. The authors aim to provide a practical method to compute Rényi entropies from correlation functions.
method: They derive a replica trick where odd-order Rényi entropies are expressed as the free energy of n replicas with additional quadratic couplings within the subsystem at the measurement time. This maps the problem to a Gaussian integral, allowing computation from two-point correlation functions.
result: The method is demonstrated for a free scalar field and an interacting scalar field with quartic coupling, showing that the Rényi entropy can be obtained from the correlation functions of the original system.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for computing entanglement entropy in quantum field theories, bridging quantum information and field theory, and can be extended to non-equilibrium settings.

title: Generalized Jarzynski Inequalities For Dissipative And Field-theoretic Systems
authors: Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos And Petr Jizba
abstract:
Author(s): Dani Rodríguez-Castellanos and Petr Jizba

The Jarzynski equality, which relates equilibrium free-energy difference to an average of nonequilibrium work, plays a central role in modern nonequilibrium statistical thermodynamics. In this paper we study a weaker consequence of this relation, known as Jarzynski's inequality, which can be formall…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper generalizes Jarzynski's inequality to dissipative and field-theoretic systems, providing a weaker but more broadly applicable bound on work distributions.
motivation: The Jarzynski equality is powerful but often difficult to apply directly; a weaker inequality may be more robust and easier to verify experimentally.
method: The authors derive generalized Jarzynski inequalities using the concept of relative entropy and apply them to systems with dissipation and field-theoretic degrees of freedom.
result: They obtain bounds on the average exponentiated work that hold under more general conditions than the original equality, and illustrate them with examples.
conclusion: The generalized inequalities extend the applicability of fluctuation theorems to a wider class of nonequilibrium processes, including those with strong dissipation or field-theoretic descriptions.

title: Thermodynamic Length In Stochastic Thermodynamics Of Far-from-equilibrium Systems: Unification Of Fluctuation Relation And Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation
authors: Atul Tanaji Mohite And Heiko Rieger
abstract:
Author(s): Atul Tanaji Mohite and Heiko Rieger

The Boltzmann distribution for an equilibrium system constrains the statistics of the system by the energetics. Despite the nonequilibrium generalization of the Boltzmann distribution being studied extensively, a unified framework valid for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking. Her…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014103] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper unifies fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations in far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems using the concept of thermodynamic length.
motivation: A unified framework for far-from-equilibrium discrete-state systems is lacking, despite extensive study of nonequilibrium generalizations of the Boltzmann distribution.
method: The authors derive a thermodynamic length that connects fluctuation relations and thermodynamic uncertainty relations, providing a geometric perspective on stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They show that the thermodynamic length quantifies the trade-off between dissipation and precision, unifying two key results in stochastic thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a unified geometric framework for understanding far-from-equilibrium systems, with implications for optimizing thermodynamic processes.

title: Heat, Work, And Fluctuations In A Driven Quantum Resonator
authors: Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, And Christian Flindt
abstract:
Author(s): Riya Baruah, Pedro Portugal, Jun-Zhe Chen (陈俊哲), Joachim Wabnig, and Christian Flindt

A central building block of a heat engine is the working fluid, which mediates the conversion of heat into work. In nanoscale heat engines, the working fluid can be a quantum system whose behavior and dynamics are nonclassical. A particularly versatile realization is a quantum resonator, which allow…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064151] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies heat, work, and fluctuations in a driven quantum resonator, providing a full counting statistics approach to characterize thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Understanding thermodynamic processes in quantum systems is crucial for developing nanoscale heat engines, where quantum effects play a significant role.
method: The authors use a full counting statistics framework to compute the distributions of heat and work for a driven quantum resonator coupled to thermal baths.
result: They derive exact expressions for the cumulants of heat and work, revealing non-Gaussian fluctuations and violations of classical fluctuation relations.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive thermodynamic description of a quantum resonator, highlighting the impact of quantum coherence on energy exchange and fluctuations.

title: Universal Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For Quantum $f$ Divergences
authors: Domingos S. P. Salazar
abstract:
Author(s): Domingos S. P. Salazar

We show that any Petz [MATH] divergence (where [MATH] is operator convex) between quantum states admits a universal [MATH]-mixture representation: the distinguishability of [MATH] from [MATH] is obtained as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts [MATH], with non-negative weights [MATH] …


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064150] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a universal thermodynamic uncertainty relation for Petz f-divergences, linking distinguishability to thermodynamic cost.
motivation: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations (TURs) bound the precision of observables by entropy production, but existing results are limited to specific divergences. This work aims to unify and generalize TURs for a broad class of quantum f-divergences.
method: The author proves that any Petz f-divergence (with operator convex f) can be expressed as a positive superposition of quadratic contrasts, and then derives a TUR that holds for all such divergences.
result: A universal TUR is established, showing that the distinguishability measured by any Petz f-divergence is bounded by the entropy production, with the bound depending only on the function f.
conclusion: This provides a unified framework for thermodynamic uncertainty relations in quantum systems, deepening the connection between information theory and thermodynamics.

title: Routing Entanglement Through Quantum Networks
authors: Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, And André Xuereb
abstract:
Author(s): Karl Pelka, Matteo Aquilina, and André Xuereb

Entanglement transport in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks is investigated, showing that directional coupling enables controlled routing of quantum correlations between nodes. The work identifies a regime in which entanglement is efficiently transmitted and quantifies how excess excitations induced by strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism studied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates controlled routing of entanglement in nonreciprocal continuous-variable quantum networks using directional coupling.
motivation: Efficient entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, but controlling the flow of quantum correlations in complex networks remains challenging.
method: The authors model a continuous-variable quantum network with nonreciprocal couplings and analyze entanglement transport using covariance matrix formalism.
result: They identify a regime where directional coupling enables efficient entanglement routing, and show that excess excitations from strong squeezing ultimately limit the mechanism.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal coupling provides a viable method for routing entanglement in quantum networks, with performance bounded by squeezing-induced noise.

title: Detecting Quantum Noise Of A Solid-state Spin Ensemble With Dispersive Measurement
authors: Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Mikhail Mamaev, Jayameenakshi Venkatraman, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ania C. Bleszynski Jayich, and Aashish A. Clerk

We theoretically explore protocols for measuring the spin polarization of an ensemble of solid-state spins, with precision at or below the standard quantum limit. Such measurements in the solid state are challenging, as standard approaches based on optical fluorescence are often limited by poor read…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023331] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes and analyzes dispersive measurement protocols to detect spin polarization of solid-state spin ensembles with precision at or below the standard quantum limit.
motivation: Standard optical fluorescence measurements of solid-state spin ensembles suffer from poor readout fidelity; the authors aim to develop a high-precision, non-destructive measurement method.
method: They theoretically model a cavity-based dispersive measurement scheme where the spin ensemble is coupled to a microwave resonator, and analyze the signal-to-noise ratio and quantum noise limits using input-output theory.
result: The protocols can achieve spin polarization sensitivity below the standard quantum limit, with the measurement backaction and imprecision noise characterized in detail.
conclusion: Dispersive measurement is a viable route for high-fidelity quantum state readout of solid-state spin ensembles, relevant for quantum memory and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic cavities in diamond with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterized the coherent coupling via optical spectroscopy and lifetime measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity >1, indicating strong coupling regime, which is a key milestone for quantum network nodes.
conclusion: This platform is promising for building scalable quantum repeaters and network nodes due to its high cooperativity and compatibility with diamond photonics.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states among many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement generation and stabilization in large spin ensembles is challenging due to decoherence and noise. The authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for creating robust, reconfigurable entangled states.
method: They propose a cavity-mediated dissipative protocol where collective spin ensembles are coupled to a common cavity mode with engineered loss. By controlling the cavity drive and dissipation, they stabilize desired entangled states (e.g., spin-squeezed states, topological states) without requiring precise initial state preparation.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity entanglement across many ensembles, with resilience to inhomogeneous broadening and other imperfections. It enables metrologically useful spin squeezing and the engineering of topological many-body states.
conclusion: This work provides a scalable and robust platform for generating multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct applications in quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive error correction scheme that protects against photon loss without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, demonstrating that passive correction can outperform the physical hardware.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for extending qubit coherence, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurement outcomes are recorded, contrasting with the polynomial decay without recording. This reveals a new phase of information preservation.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes provides a powerful strategy to protect quantum information, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum memory.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a minimal model of a quantum detector as an autonomous machine, analyzing its nonequilibrium thermodynamics using entropy production and measurement accuracy metrics.
result: They demonstrate a fundamental trade-off between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires greater thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The results provide a framework for assessing the thermodynamic efficiency of quantum detectors and highlight the unavoidable dissipation in information acquisition.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with sublinear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin emitters are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneity, making global control and entanglement generation challenging.
method: The authors develop a control framework that uses driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with optical heralding to generate large cluster states, leveraging programmable quantum matter.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity global operations and scalable entanglement with sublinear overhead, enabling cluster states of 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward large-scale quantum networks using existing solid-state platforms.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited for ultra-sensitive parameter estimation, surpassing classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for critical quantum sensing, including the use of critical exponents, finite-size scaling, and dynamical responses near phase transitions.
result: It demonstrates how criticality can enhance estimation precision, providing a systematic approach to design sensors that operate at the Heisenberg limit.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a robust and practical route to achieve high-precision measurements, with potential applications in quantum metrology and fundamental physics.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how random measurements can enhance the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes, revealing new stability properties and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in monitored quantum dynamics is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum error correction.
method: The authors analyze the effect of random projective measurements on quantum codes, deriving conditions for improved decodability and characterizing logical measurement outcomes.
result: They find that random measurements can stabilize logical information and provide new insights into the interplay between measurement and error correction.
conclusion: Randomly monitored quantum codes offer a promising framework for robust quantum information processing, with implications for fault-tolerant architectures.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, demonstrating device-independent randomness expansion on a compact platform.
motivation: Self-testing quantum random number generators (QRNGs) provide provable randomness without trusting the devices, but previous implementations were bulky and complex. This work aims to miniaturize such systems for practical deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that integrates all necessary components for a self-testing QRNG protocol, including entangled photon sources, measurement devices, and control logic, using standard CMOS-compatible processes.
result: The chip successfully generates random bits with provable security based on Bell inequality violations, achieving a randomness generation rate suitable for cryptographic applications while maintaining device independence.
conclusion: This demonstration shows that self-testing QRNGs can be realized on a scalable photonic platform, paving the way for compact, production-scale quantum security devices.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for quantum repeaters, significantly improving resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes suffer from high resource overhead and limited loss tolerance, hindering near-term feasibility.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for quantum tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The optimized tree-codes achieve higher loss tolerance with fewer physical resources (e.g., fewer emitters and memory qubits) compared to symmetric codes, enabling practical quantum repeater implementations.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-code designs offer a promising path toward resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume ideal devices, but real devices have imperfections; a framework is needed to account for device characterization in a composable manner.
method: The authors develop a general method that integrates device characterization into composable security proofs, likely using entropy accumulation or similar techniques.
result: The method yields rigorous security bounds that incorporate realistic device parameters, enabling certification of QKD devices.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and theoretically sound approach for QKD security certification, bridging theory and experiment.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
authors: Fabian Marxer et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device.
motivation: Achieving high-fidelity operations across all qubit control and measurement tasks in a single device is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol are employed to optimize gate and readout fidelities.
result: Single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout all achieve above 99.9% fidelity in the same superconducting device.
conclusion: This work advances the practical realization of fault-tolerant quantum computing by demonstrating that high-fidelity operations can be simultaneously achieved in a single platform.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics at the mesoscopic scale with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, challenging conventional approaches and providing new insights.

title: Entanglement In The Dicke Subspace
authors: Aabhas Gulati, Ion Nechita, And Clément Pellegrini
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2150 (2026).

We provide a complete mathematical theory for the entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states. These quantum states form an important subclass of bosonic states arising in the study of indistinguishable particles. We introduce a tensor-based parametrization where the diagonal entries of these states are encoded as a symmetric tensor, enabling a direct translation between entanglement properties and well-studied convex cones of tensors. Our results bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry and the theory of completely positive and copositive tensors. This dictionary maps separability to completely positive tensors, the PPT property to moment tensors, entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors, and decomposable witnesses to sum of squares tensors. We establish that PPT entanglement exists for all multipartite systems with local dimension [MATH] and [MATH] parties, disproving a recent conjecture. We also show that, for mixtures of Dicke states, the PPT condition with respect to the most balanced bipartition implies all other PPT conditions. We further connect bosonic extendibility of mixtures of Dicke states to the duals of known hierarchies for non-negative polynomials, such as the ones by Reznick and Polya. We thus provide semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace.

.
tldr: Provides a complete mathematical theory for entanglement of mixtures of Dicke states, linking separability to completely positive tensors and disproving a conjecture about PPT entanglement.
motivation: To understand entanglement in the important subclass of Dicke states, which arise in bosonic systems, and to bridge multipartite entanglement theory with semialgebraic geometry.
method: Introduces a tensor-based parametrization where diagonal entries are encoded as symmetric tensors, mapping separability to completely positive tensors, PPT to moment tensors, and entanglement witnesses to copositive tensors.
result: Establishes existence of PPT entanglement for all multipartite systems with local dimension ≥3 and ≥3 parties, disproving a recent conjecture; shows PPT condition for most balanced bipartition implies all others; connects bosonic extendibility to hierarchies for non-negative polynomials.
conclusion: Provides semidefinite programming relaxations for separability and entanglement testing in the Dicke subspace, advancing entanglement theory and its computational tools.

title: Measuring Rényi Entropy With An Echo Protocol
authors: Yi-Neng Zhou, Robin Löwenberg, And Julian Sonner
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2146 (2026).

We present efficient and practical protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy, whose exponential is known as the purity. Our approach is based on expressing the purity in terms of transition probabilities generated by an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, making it applicable to quantum many-body systems. Notably, our approach does not rely on random-noise averaging, a feature that can be extended to protocols to measure out-of-time-order correlation functions, as we demonstrate. By way of example, we show that our protocols can be practically implemented in superconducting qubit-based platforms, as well as in cavity-QED trapped ultra-cold gases.

.
tldr: Presents efficient echo-based protocols to measure the second Rényi entropy (purity) in quantum many-body systems without random-noise averaging.
motivation: Measuring Rényi entropy is crucial for characterizing entanglement and quantum correlations, but existing methods often rely on random averaging or are inefficient.
method: The purity is expressed in terms of transition probabilities from an echo-type forward-backward evolution sequence, avoiding random-noise averaging; the protocol is extended to out-of-time-order correlators.
result: The protocols are shown to be practically implementable on superconducting qubit platforms and in cavity-QED trapped ultracold gases.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, noise-robust method for measuring Rényi entropy, advancing experimental quantum information processing.

title: Measurement Incompatibility And Quantum Steering Via Linear Programming
authors: Lucas E. A. Porto, Sébastien Designolle, Sebastian Pokutta, And Marco Túlio Quintino
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2141 (2026).

The problem of deciding whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable is known to be equivalent to determining whether a quantum assemblage is unsteerable. This problem can be formulated as a semidefinite program (SDP). However, the number of variables and constraints in such a formulation grows exponentially with the number of measurements, rendering it intractable for large measurement sets. In this work, we circumvent this problem by transforming the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that compute upper and lower bounds on the incompatibility robustness with a complexity that grows polynomially in the number of measurements. The hierarchy is guaranteed to converge and it can be applied to arbitrary measurements – including non-projective POVMs (Positive Operator-Valued Measures) – in arbitrary dimensions. While convergence becomes impractical in high dimensions, in the case of qubits our method reliably provides accurate upper and lower bounds for the incompatibility robustness of sets with several hundred measurements in a short time using a standard laptop. We also apply our methods to qutrits, obtaining non-trivial upper and lower bounds in scenarios that are otherwise intractable using the standard SDP approach, although such bounds are significantly looser than the ones obtained in the qubit case. Finally, we show how our methods can be used to construct local hidden state models for states (i.e., to prove that a state cannot lead to steering under any possible local measurements), or conversely, to certify that a given state exhibits steering; for two-qubit quantum states, our approach is comparable to, and in some cases outperforms, the current best methods.

.
tldr: This paper transforms the semidefinite program for joint measurability and steering into a hierarchy of linear programs, enabling efficient computation of bounds for large measurement sets.
motivation: Determining whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable or whether a state is steerable is computationally expensive due to exponential growth of SDP variables. The authors aim to provide a more tractable method.
method: The authors reformulate the SDP for incompatibility robustness as a hierarchy of linear programs, using a polynomial-complexity approach that converges to the true value. They apply it to qubit and qutrit systems.
result: For qubits, the method yields accurate upper and lower bounds for sets with hundreds of measurements quickly on a standard laptop. For qutrits, non-trivial bounds are obtained in previously intractable scenarios, though looser.
conclusion: The linear programming hierarchy provides a practical tool for studying measurement incompatibility and quantum steering, and can be used to construct local hidden state models or certify steering for two-qubit states.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: Tight bounds for quantum phase estimation with advice states, resolving open problems in unitary recurrence time and error reduction.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine, but its cost with advice states (e.g., eigenstate copies) was not tightly characterized. Also, the cost of error reduction in phase estimation was unknown.
method: Uses the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials to prove lower bounds, and provides matching algorithms for all parameter regimes.
result: Shows that a small number of advice copies are not significantly better than no advice, and that many copies do not reduce cost much. Also proves that error reduction costs a factor 1/ε, unlike search problems.
conclusion: Provides a complete characterization of phase estimation complexity with advice, and resolves open questions in unitary recurrence time and error reduction.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity, showing that stabilizer states maximally violate it and linking Bell violation to Wigner negativity.
motivation: Generalizing Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems is important for understanding nonlocality, but known results for qubits do not directly extend. This work aims to connect nonlocality with Wigner negativity in qudit systems.
method: The authors introduce a new CHSH-like inequality for qudits using correlations related to Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under a generalized π/8 gate. They analyze the Bell operator and its relation to singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume.
result: A specific stabilizer state achieves maximal violation among all qudit states, and the Bell operator quantifies both singlet fraction and Wigner negativity. Additionally, bipartite entangled qudit states with Wigner negativity can witness contextuality.
conclusion: The work establishes a direct link between nonlocality and Wigner negativity in qudit systems, providing a new tool for studying quantum correlations beyond qubits.

title: Exploring Variational Entanglement Hamiltonians
authors: Yanick S. Kind And Benedikt Fauseweh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2133 (2026).

Recent advances in analog and digital quantum-simulation platforms have enabled exploration of the spectrum of entanglement Hamiltonians via variational algorithms. In this work we analyze the convergence properties of the variationally obtained solutions and compare them to numerically exact calculations in quantum critical systems. We demonstrate that interpreting the cost functional as an integral permits the deployment of iterative quadrature schemes, thereby reducing the required number of measurements by more than an order of magnitude even in the presence of noise. We further show that a modified ansatz captures deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models, improves convergence, improves trainability and provides a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. Finally, we establish that a low cost value does not by itself guarantee convergence in trace distance. Nevertheless, it faithfully reproduces degeneracies and spectral gaps, which are essential for applications to topological phases.

.
tldr: This paper analyzes variational algorithms for learning entanglement Hamiltonians in quantum critical systems, demonstrating improved convergence and reduced measurements.
motivation: Understanding entanglement Hamiltonians is crucial for characterizing quantum phases, but their experimental extraction is challenging. Variational approaches offer a practical route, yet their convergence properties are not well understood.
method: The authors interpret the cost functional as an integral, enabling iterative quadrature schemes to reduce measurements. They also introduce a modified ansatz to capture deviations from the Bisognano-Wichmann form in lattice models.
result: The proposed methods reduce required measurements by over an order of magnitude even with noise, improve convergence and trainability, and provide a cost-function-level diagnostic for quantum phase transitions. However, low cost does not guarantee convergence in trace distance.
conclusion: Variational entanglement Hamiltonians can faithfully reproduce degeneracies and spectral gaps essential for topological phases, despite limitations in trace distance convergence.

title: Detecting Entanglement By State Preparation And Local Measurements
authors: Jaemin Kim, Anindita Bera, Dariusz Chruściński, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2128 (2026).

Entanglement witnesses (EWs) are a collection of observables that can characterize separable states and, experimentally, estimating EWs can verify entangled states. In this work, we show that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite entangled state, which we introduce as a network state for the purpose, can estimate EWs. Namely, entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner, in which experimenters do not necessarily change measurement settings. We present a fixed measurement setting and network states for estimating decomposable EWs, equivalent to the partial transpose criteria. We also consider non-decomposable EWs that detect bound entangled states beyond the partial transpose criteria. The results can be extended to multipartite states such as graph states, a resource for measurement-based quantum computing, and readily applied to distributed settings such as quantum metrology or sensor networks where multipartite entangled states are resourceful.

.
tldr: This paper shows that a fixed measurement setting on a multipartite network state can estimate entanglement witnesses, enabling measurement-based entanglement verification without changing settings.
motivation: Entanglement witnesses are crucial for verifying entanglement, but typically require changing measurement settings. The authors aim to simplify this by using a fixed measurement setting on a specially prepared network state.
method: The authors introduce a network state and a fixed measurement setting to estimate decomposable and non-decomposable entanglement witnesses, including those detecting bound entanglement. They extend the method to multipartite graph states.
result: They demonstrate that entangled states can be fully verified in a measurement-based manner with a fixed setting, applicable to distributed settings like quantum metrology and sensor networks.
conclusion: The work provides a practical method for entanglement detection that reduces experimental complexity, with potential applications in quantum networks and multipartite scenarios.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: Constructs a local decoder for the 2D toric code that preserves logical state for exponential time using hierarchical cellular automata.
motivation: To solve the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions without non-local classical computation.
method: Uses ideas from hierarchical classical cellular automata (Tsirelson and Gács) to design a strictly local quantum circuit decoder for the 2D toric code.
result: The decoder preserves a logical state for exponential time under circuit-level noise, and can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes.
conclusion: Demonstrates that local topological quantum memory is possible in 2D, advancing quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Distributed Quantum Information Processing: A Review Of Recent Progress
authors: J Knörzer, X Liu, B F Schiffer And J Tura
abstract: Distributed quantum information processing seeks to overcome the scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication. This approach extends the capabilities of individual devices, enabling access to larger problem instances and novel algorithmic techniques. Beyond increasing qubit counts, it also enables qualitatively new capabilities, such as joint measurements on multiple copies of high-dimensional quantum states. The distinction between single-copy and multi-copy access reveals important differences in task complexity and helps identify which computational problems stand to benefit from distributed quantum resources. At the same time, it highlights trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and the practical challenges involved in realizing them experimentally. In this review, we contextualize recent developments by surveying the theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols and examining the experimental platforms and algorithmic applications that realize them in practice.
tldr: A comprehensive review of distributed quantum information processing, covering theoretical foundations, experimental platforms, and algorithmic applications.
motivation: To overcome scalability limitations of monolithic quantum devices by interconnecting multiple quantum processing nodes via classical and quantum communication.
method: The paper surveys theoretical foundations of distributed quantum protocols, examines experimental platforms, and discusses algorithmic applications.
result: Identifies trade-offs between classical and quantum communication models and highlights which computational problems benefit from distributed quantum resources.
conclusion: Distributed quantum information processing enables larger problem instances and novel capabilities, but practical challenges remain in realizing the required quantum communication links.

title: Precise Computation Of Universal Corner Entanglement Entropy At 2+1 Dimension: From Ising To Gaussian Quantum Critical Points
authors: Ben Lee-Yeung Ngai, Justin Tim-Lok Chau, Junchen Rong, Meng Cheng, Yuan Da Liao And Zi Yang Meng
abstract: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in the entanglement entropy (EE) of (2+1)d quantum many-body systems remains a significant challenge, despite its central role in revealing universal information about quantum states and quantum critical points (QCPs). Building on recent algorithmic advances that enable the stable calculation of EE as an exponential observable (Zhou et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 165106; Zhang et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B109 205147; Liao et al 2024 Phys. Rev. B110 235111), we develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) algorithm to precisely and efficiently compute the universal corner of EE at QCPs in a (2+1)d square-lattice transverse-field Ising model augmented with a four-body interaction. Turning on this interaction allows us to trace an Ising critical line, reaching the tricritical point, and then a line of first-order phase transition. In (2+1)d, the tricritical point is described by the Gaussian theory, where a theoretical calculation of the corner logarithmic term in the 2nd Rényi entropy term is available (Casini and Huerta 2007 Nucl. Phys. B764 183). Our QMC results are in quantitative agreement with this theoretical value, providing a highly nontrivial benchmark of the algorithm. Furthermore, we also study the Rényi EE at the Ising critical line and on the first-order transition line, obtaining results consistent with theoretical expectations. These findings establish the long-sought connection between the universal values of an exactly solvable limit and those of a strongly correlated regime at (2+1)d.
tldr: This paper computes the universal corner entanglement entropy at (2+1)d quantum critical points using a novel quantum Monte Carlo algorithm, achieving quantitative agreement with theoretical predictions.
motivation: Computing the subleading logarithmic term in entanglement entropy for (2+1)d systems is challenging but crucial for revealing universal information about quantum states and critical points.
method: The authors develop a bubble basis projector quantum Monte Carlo algorithm to compute the 2nd Rényi entropy as an exponential observable, applied to a square-lattice transverse-field Ising model with a four-body interaction.
result: The QMC results quantitatively match the theoretical corner logarithmic term for the Gaussian tricritical point, and also yield consistent results for the Ising critical line and first-order transition line.
conclusion: This work establishes a long-sought connection between universal values in exactly solvable limits and strongly correlated regimes in (2+1)d, demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness for entanglement entropy calculations.

title: Gradiometric, Fully Tunable C-shunted Flux Qubits
authors: B. Berlitz
A. Händel
E. Daum
A. V. Ustinov
J. Lisenfeld
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a gradiometric, fully tunable C-shunted flux qubit design that improves coherence and tunability for quantum computing applications.
motivation: Flux qubits suffer from sensitivity to flux noise and limited tunability, which hinders their performance in quantum processors. A design that mitigates these issues is needed.
method: The authors introduce a gradiometric design with a C-shunt capacitor to reduce flux noise sensitivity and enable full tunability of the qubit frequency. They fabricate and characterize the device at millikelvin temperatures.
result: The qubit exhibits improved coherence times (T1, T2) compared to standard flux qubits, and its frequency can be tuned over a wide range without significant degradation.
conclusion: The gradiometric C-shunted flux qubit is a promising platform for scalable quantum computing due to its enhanced coherence and tunability.

title: Many-Body Perturbation Theory For Driven Dissipative Quasiparticle Flows And Fluctuations
authors: Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, And Vojtech Vlcek
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas Blommel, Enrico Perfetto, Gianluca Stefanucci, and Vojtech Vlcek

We present a unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing. Using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism, we introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines representing quasiparticle flows and fl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256403] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A unified many-body perturbation theory for open quantum systems that treats dissipation, correlations, and external driving on equal footing using a Keldysh-Lindblad formalism.
motivation: To develop a theoretical framework that can handle driven dissipative quantum systems beyond the weak-coupling limit, which is crucial for understanding non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors combine Keldysh and Lindblad formalisms to introduce a diagrammatic treatment of dissipative interaction lines, representing quasiparticle flows and fluctuations in open quantum systems.
result: The formalism provides a systematic way to compute correlation functions and response properties for driven dissipative systems, capturing both Markovian and non-Markovian effects.
conclusion: This work offers a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and quantum information science.

title: Engineering Selective Transitions In Dressed Two-qubit Systems With Dual Driving
authors: Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, And Ziyu Tao
abstract:
Author(s): Peisheng Huang, Wenhui Huang, Youpeng Zhong, and Ziyu Tao

Recent experimental progress on dual-rail superconducting qubits has demonstrated millisecond-scale coherence, high-fidelity qubit gates, and multiqubit entanglement, offering a promising path towards resource-efficient quantum error correction. Fast reset and rapid state preparation are becoming cr…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to engineer selective transitions in dressed two-qubit systems using dual driving, enabling fast and high-fidelity quantum operations.
motivation: Fast reset and rapid state preparation are critical for resource-efficient quantum error correction, especially in dual-rail superconducting qubit platforms.
method: The authors propose a dual-driving scheme that selectively addresses transitions in a dressed two-qubit system, leveraging the tunability of superconducting qubits to control interactions.
result: They demonstrate theoretically that selective transitions can be achieved with high fidelity and speed, reducing gate times while maintaining coherence.
conclusion: The dual-driving approach offers a practical pathway for improving qubit control in superconducting quantum processors, supporting scalable quantum computing.

title: Remote Magnon-phonon Entanglement In Waveguide Magnomechanics
authors: Shi-Fan Qi And Fan Li
abstract:
Author(s): Shi-fan Qi and Fan Li

Generating long-distance quantum entanglement is crucial for advancing quantum information processing. In this work, we propose a protocol for generating remote magnon-phonon entanglement in a hybrid waveguide magnomechanical system, where multiple spatially separated magnon modes couple to a common…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013702] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a protocol for generating remote magnon-phonon entanglement in a waveguide magnomechanical system.
motivation: Long-distance entanglement is crucial for quantum information processing; this work aims to generate it in a hybrid system.
method: Multiple spatially separated magnon modes couple to a common waveguide phonon mode via magnetostrictive interaction, enabling entanglement between remote magnons and phonons.
result: The protocol achieves steady-state entanglement between distant magnon and phonon modes, with tunable parameters.
conclusion: The scheme provides a viable platform for quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Spatiotemporal Equilibrium Thermodynamics Of Guided Optical Waves At Positive And Negative Temperatures
authors: Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, And Antonio Picozzi
abstract:
Author(s): Lucas Zanaglia, Josselin Garnier, Claire Michel, Valérie Doya, Mario Ferraro, Stefan Wabnitz, Iacopo Carusotto, and Antonio Picozzi

Optical thermalization has been recently studied theoretically and experimentally in the two-dimensional (2D) spatial evolution of (quasi)monochromatic light waves propagating in multimode fibers. In this work, we investigate the spatiotemporal equilibrium properties of incoherent multimode optical …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063533] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a spatiotemporal equilibrium thermodynamics for incoherent multimode optical waves, demonstrating thermalization and negative temperature states.
motivation: To extend optical thermalization from purely spatial to spatiotemporal dynamics in multimode fibers, exploring equilibrium properties and negative temperatures.
method: The authors use a wave turbulence approach to derive a kinetic equation and a thermodynamic description of the spatiotemporal evolution of incoherent light.
result: They show that the system can reach a Rayleigh-Jeans equilibrium with a well-defined temperature, including negative temperature regimes, and validate predictions with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for understanding spatiotemporal thermalization in multimode optical systems, with implications for information thermodynamics and nonlinear optics.

title: Noncommutative Index Of Measurement-only Entanglement Phase Transitions
authors: Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, And Zhisong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhichen Huang, Chunxiao Du, Yang Zhou, and Zhisong Xiao

Measurement-only models offer an ideal platform for exploring entanglement dynamics in the absence of unitary evolution. Despite extensive numerical evidence for entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only dynamics, the underlying mechanism attributed to noncommutativity among multisite proje…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062223] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a noncommutative index theory to characterize entanglement phase transitions in measurement-only quantum circuits.
motivation: Measurement-only models exhibit entanglement phase transitions, but the underlying mechanism due to noncommutativity of multisite projectors is not well understood.
method: The authors introduce a noncommutative index that captures the algebraic structure of measurement operators and use it to analyze entanglement dynamics in Clifford circuits.
