result: They show that the noncommutative index distinguishes different phases and predicts critical points, providing a rigorous framework for understanding measurement-induced entanglement transitions.
conclusion: The noncommutative index offers a powerful tool for classifying entanglement phases in measurement-only dynamics, advancing the theory of quantum information in many-body systems.

title: Dynamical Irreversibility And Local Decoherence In Quantum Many-body Chaos
authors: Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, And Carlos Diaz-Mejia
abstract:
Author(s): Jose Alfredo de Leon, Miguel Gonzalez, and Carlos Diaz-Mejia

Typical dynamical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent (e.g., local observables or purities) and thus may fail to capture typical decoherent behavior one expects of a subsystem. Quantum channels fully capture the reduced dynamics of a subsystem. Here, we investigate the purity of the Cho…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062224] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical irreversibility and local decoherence in quantum many-body chaotic systems using the purity of the Choi matrix as a probe.
motivation: Typical quantum chaos probes are initial-state dependent and may not capture typical decoherent behavior of a subsystem; the authors aim to use quantum channels to fully capture reduced dynamics.
method: The authors investigate the purity of the Choi matrix of the reduced dynamics (quantum channel) for a subsystem in a chaotic many-body system, comparing it to initial-state dependent measures.
result: The Choi purity provides a more robust and typical measure of decoherence and irreversibility in quantum chaotic systems, capturing features missed by state-dependent probes.
conclusion: The Choi matrix purity is a valuable tool for characterizing quantum chaos and decoherence, offering a state-independent perspective on dynamical irreversibility.

title: Quantum Implementation Of Higher-order Power Method For Estimating Geometric Entanglement Of Pure States
authors: Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, And Elena Blokhina
abstract:
Author(s): Andrii Semenov, Niall Murphy, Simone Patscheider, Alessandra Bernardi, and Elena Blokhina

Entanglement is one of the fundamental properties of a quantum state and is a crucial differentiator between classical and quantum computation. There are many ways to define entanglement and its measure, depending on the problem or application under consideration. Each of these measures may be compu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062459] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum algorithm for estimating geometric entanglement of pure states using a higher-order power method.
motivation: Geometric entanglement is a key measure of multipartite entanglement, but its computation is classically hard. A quantum algorithm could provide a speedup.
method: The authors design a quantum circuit implementing the higher-order power method to find the closest separable state and compute the geometric measure of entanglement.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on small systems and show that it can estimate geometric entanglement with high accuracy.
conclusion: The quantum algorithm offers a viable approach for estimating geometric entanglement, potentially useful for benchmarking quantum devices.

title: Scalable Quantum Resources With Short-range Interacting Spin-1/2 Chains
authors: Marcin Płodzień And Jan Chwedeńczuk
abstract:
Author(s): Marcin Płodzień and Jan Chwedeńczuk

The dynamical generation of quantum resources, such as many-body entanglement, Bell correlations, or spin squeezing, can be achieved via one-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics, which require all-to-all couplings. However, current digital and analog quantum simulation platforms natively provide short-range…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062220] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that short-range interacting spin-1/2 chains can generate scalable quantum resources like many-body entanglement and Bell correlations via one-axis twisting dynamics, using a staggered field to mimic all-to-all interactions.
motivation: One-axis twisting (OAT) dynamics generate useful quantum resources but require all-to-all couplings, which are not native to many quantum simulation platforms. The authors aim to achieve OAT-like dynamics with short-range interactions.
method: They consider a spin-1/2 chain with nearest-neighbor XX interactions and a staggered transverse field, which effectively produces a collective spin squeezing Hamiltonian. They analyze the dynamics using exact diagonalization and analytical approximations.
result: The staggered field enables OAT-like dynamics, generating scalable spin squeezing and Bell correlations that grow with system size, comparable to the ideal all-to-all case.
conclusion: Short-range interacting spin chains can serve as scalable quantum resources for metrology and quantum information tasks, bridging the gap between realistic platforms and ideal OAT models.

title: Accelerated Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Quantum Memory Via Shortcuts To Adiabaticity
authors: Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, And X. Q. Shao
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Wei, Changcheng Li, Y. M. Liu, Yuechun Jiao, Weibin Li, and X. Q. Shao

Electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) enables coherent light-matter storage, forming the basis of photonic quantum memories that are essential for scalable quantum networks and distributed quantum computing. However, accelerating the storage process violates the adiabatic condition, resulti…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062453] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper accelerates Rydberg EIT quantum memory using shortcuts to adiabaticity, achieving faster storage with high efficiency.
motivation: Standard EIT quantum memory requires slow adiabatic processes to avoid loss, limiting its speed. Faster storage is needed for practical quantum networks.
method: The authors apply counter-diabatic driving (shortcuts to adiabaticity) to the Rydberg EIT system, designing control pulses that suppress non-adiabatic losses.
result: They demonstrate that the accelerated protocol achieves near-unity storage efficiency and fidelity while significantly reducing storage time compared to the adiabatic limit.
conclusion: Shortcuts to adiabaticity provide a viable route to high-speed, high-fidelity quantum memory in Rydberg systems, advancing hybrid quantum network components.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology exploits quantum phase transitions for enhanced precision, but critical slowing down limits achievable precision within finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the quantum Fisher information per unit time using the Lieb-Robinson bound and the energy gap scaling near criticality.
result: The precision scales as T^{-1/2} for a d-dimensional system with dynamical critical exponent z, independent of system size, revealing a trade-off between precision and evolution time.
conclusion: The bound is fundamental and cannot be overcome by any adaptive or feedback scheme, setting a universal limit for critical quantum metrology.

title: Protocol For Purifying Noisy Preparation And Measurements Of Qubits
authors: Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, And Joonwoo Bae
abstract:
Author(s): Jaemin Kim, Seungchan Seo, Jiyoung Yun, Benjamin Lienhard, and Joonwoo Bae

Noise affecting qubit preparation and measurements accounts for a significant fraction of errors in quantum information processing. This is especially critical in tasks like variational quantum algorithms, quantum error correction, and entanglement distribution through repeaters. In this work, we pr…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023347] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A protocol to purify noisy qubit preparation and measurement devices using only trusted state preparation and measurement, enabling high-fidelity quantum information processing.
motivation: Noise in qubit preparation and measurement is a major error source in quantum computing and communication, limiting performance in tasks like variational algorithms and quantum error correction.
method: The protocol uses a trusted state preparation and measurement device to characterize and then purify noisy devices via iterative error mitigation, without requiring full tomography.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity purified states and measurements, significantly reducing errors from preparation and measurement noise.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method to mitigate preparation and measurement noise, enhancing the reliability of quantum information processing tasks.

title: Surface Code Stabilizer Measurements For Rydberg Atoms
authors: Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, And Guido Pupillo
abstract:
Author(s): Sven Jandura, Laura Pecorari, and Guido Pupillo

Optimizing quantum gates for logical errors—rather than solely focusing on physical fidelity—is found to improve surface code performance in neutral-atom arrays. Novel Rydberg leakage propagation mechanisms are presented and laser-pulse protocols to suppress them are introduced, paving the way for efficient and fault-tolerant quantum error correction.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022059] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Optimizing Rydberg gate pulses for logical error suppression improves surface code performance and mitigates leakage propagation.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing with Rydberg interactions is a promising platform, but leakage errors degrade surface code performance. Existing gate optimization focuses on physical fidelity, not logical errors.
method: The authors model Rydberg atom surface code stabilizer measurements, identify novel leakage propagation mechanisms, and design laser-pulse protocols to suppress them, optimizing gates for logical error rate.
result: The optimized protocols significantly reduce logical error rates and improve surface code threshold, demonstrating the importance of logical-error-aware optimization.
conclusion: Rydberg atom arrays can achieve efficient fault-tolerant quantum error correction with tailored gate designs that address leakage, advancing neutral-atom quantum computing.

title: High-sensitivity Optical Detection Of Electron-nuclear Spin Clusters In Diamond
authors: L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, And G. Hétet
abstract:
Author(s): L. Chambard, A. Durand, J. Voisin, M. Perdriat, V. Jacques, and G. Hétet

We perform sensitive nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) with spin ensembles that are polarized by nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond at room temperature. Using stabilized lasers, a balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field, we resolve sharp NMR features arising from multiple spin c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023337] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: High-sensitivity NMR detection of electron-nuclear spin clusters in diamond using NV centers.
motivation: To achieve sensitive NMR with spin ensembles polarized by NV centers at room temperature, resolving sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters.
method: Using stabilized lasers, balanced detection, and a highly uniform magnetic field to perform NMR on NV-polarized spin ensembles.
result: Resolved sharp NMR features from multiple spin clusters, demonstrating high sensitivity.
conclusion: The technique enables high-sensitivity detection of nuclear spin clusters, relevant for quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Parastatistics And A Secret Communication Challenge
authors: Zhiyuan Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiyuan Wang

A secret-communication challenge is proposed that demonstrates a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles in topological phases of matter. The work shows how exchanging emergent paraparticles can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance that is achievable only in topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022056] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a secret-communication challenge using emergent paraparticles in topological phases to transmit information without local traces.
motivation: To demonstrate a distinctive physical consequence of paraparticles and their potential for secure communication.
method: Theoretical analysis of exchanging emergent paraparticles in topological phases of matter, showing robust information transmission without locally detectable traces.
result: Paraparticle exchange can robustly transmit information without leaving locally detectable traces, a performance unique to topological phases hosting emergent paraparticles.
conclusion: The work provides a new secret-communication challenge that highlights the unique properties of paraparticles in topological phases.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a quantum computational advantage using an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To provide experimental evidence of a utilizable quantum computational advantage in a programmable quantum processor, moving beyond proof-of-principle demonstrations.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the dynamics of a driven many-body system, benchmarking against classical simulations and quantifying the advantage via entanglement measures.
result: The processor achieves a quantum computational advantage that is both verifiable and utilizable, with entanglement generation exceeding classical simulability thresholds.
conclusion: Ultracold-atom processors can serve as viable platforms for demonstrating practical quantum advantage in simulating many-body physics.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, undermining quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They identify a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, posing a challenge for error correction.
conclusion: Correlated phase error bursts from ionizing radiation must be addressed to achieve fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. The symplectic rank fills this gap by providing an operationally meaningful resource measure.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank as the minimum number of Gaussian unitaries needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and they develop tools to compute it for various classes of states, including Fock states and cat states.
result: The symplectic rank is shown to be additive under tensor products and to provide tight lower bounds on the number of non-Gaussian operations required for state preparation and measurement.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a powerful and practical measure of non-Gaussianity with direct implications for resource estimation in continuous-variable quantum information processing.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral diffusion and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters in silicon are promising for quantum networks, but spectral instability limits their performance. Understanding and mitigating these instabilities is crucial for practical quantum repeaters and memories.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on single erbium ions coupled to silicon photonic crystal cavities, measuring spectral diffusion and linewidths under various conditions (temperature, laser power, etc.).
result: They identify charge fluctuations in the silicon host as the main cause of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that cavity enhancement reduces the impact, achieving near-transform-limited linewidths.
conclusion: Cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon can achieve the spectral stability required for quantum networking, with identified mechanisms guiding further improvement.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, which combine cavity QED and Rydberg atoms, is of fundamental interest for quantum simulation and many-body physics.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays using analytical and numerical methods, focusing on kinetic constraints arising from long-range interactions.
result: They find that kinetic constraints lead to blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating novel non-equilibrium phases.
conclusion: The work provides a new platform for exploring constrained dynamics and non-thermal states in hybrid quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence time and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are promising for scalable quantum technologies, but suitable spin defects with long coherence and high readout fidelity have been lacking.
method: The authors characterize a deep-level defect in ZnO using experimental and theoretical methods, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity.
result: They find an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity suitable for single-shot readout.
conclusion: ZnO deep spin defects are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, particularly for quantum sensing and quantum networking applications.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often lack accuracy.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and use computer algebra to optimize the control fields.
result: The proposed method achieves higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in numerical simulations.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise. The authors aim to design device-tailored sequences that are both effective and scalable.
method: The paper maps the problem of designing dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging error-correcting code principles to cancel k-local noise. The resulting sequences are derived from code parity checks.
result: The proposed sequences achieve decoupling from spatially correlated noise with a length that does not scale with the number of qubits, offering a significant advantage over conventional approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable method for dynamical decoupling in multi-qubit systems, with potential applications in quantum error mitigation and quantum computing.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Energy relaxation errors are a major obstacle for superconducting qubits; converting them into erasures can significantly enhance error correction efficiency.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby flagging relaxation events as erasures.
result: The erasure conversion scheme boosts effective coherence times by converting dominant relaxation errors into detectable erasures.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to improved error correction by turning relaxation errors into erasures, which are easier to handle in fault-tolerant protocols.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroups, providing a unified framework for symmetry-learning tasks.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and complexity.

title: Maximizing The Nondemolition Nature Of A Quantum Measurement Via An Adaptive Readout Protocol
authors: Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, And Andrea Morello
abstract:
Author(s): Arjen Vaartjes, Rocky Yue Su, Laura A. O’Neill, Paul Steinacker, Gauri Goenka, Mark R. van Blankenstein, Xi Yu, Benjamin Wilhelm, Alexander M. Jakob, Fay E. Hudson, Kohei M. Itoh, Chih Hwan Yang, Andrew S. Dzurak, David N. Jamieson, Martin Nurizzo, Danielle Holmes, Arne Laucht, and Andrea Morello

Adaptive subspace-switching readout improves nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems, boosting qudit readout fidelity to 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across platforms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020330] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: An adaptive readout protocol improves nondemolition measurement fidelity in multilevel quantum systems, demonstrated on a silicon spin qudit.
motivation: Nondemolition measurements in multilevel quantum systems are limited by measurement-induced errors and long readout times; improving fidelity and speed is crucial for quantum computing.
method: The authors implement an adaptive subspace-switching readout protocol that dynamically adjusts the measurement basis to reduce backaction and enhance readout fidelity.
result: The protocol achieves a readout fidelity of 99.61% while reducing measurement time and mitigating measurement-induced errors across different platforms.
conclusion: Adaptive readout is a practical technique to enhance nondemolition measurements, applicable to various qudit platforms and beneficial for quantum error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and non-decodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random quantum codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using statistical physics methods, mapping the decoding problem to a statistical mechanics model and studying its phase transitions.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and non-decodable phases as a function of noise strength, with the transition point determined by the code's spectral properties.
conclusion: The work provides a simple mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical quantum error-correcting codes.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and high-rate key distribution. This review consolidates the state of the art to guide future research.
method: The paper surveys CV quantum communication protocols including CV-QKD, measurement-device-independent CV-QKD, and continuous-variable quantum networks, discussing security proofs, finite-size effects, and experimental implementations.
result: CV quantum communication has reached maturity with record key rates over metropolitan distances, and security proofs have been tightened. Challenges remain in long-distance transmission and integration with quantum repeaters.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and competitive technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing work needed to extend range and improve performance.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive classification and security analysis of quantum cryptographic protocols beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a structured overview.
method: The paper reviews and categorizes quantum cryptographic primitives, explains their security guarantees and limitations, and discusses experimental implementations using photonic platforms.
result: It presents a taxonomy of quantum cryptographic protocols and highlights the current experimental capabilities and challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant limitations that need to be addressed.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to testing whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical and conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and proposed tabletop experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several feasible experiments are analyzed, showing that entanglement generation can serve as a witness for non-classical gravity.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide concrete experimental tests for the quantum nature of gravity, with near-term feasibility.

title: A Complexity Theory For Non-local Quantum Computation
authors: Andreas Bluhm, Simon Höfer, Alex May, Mikka Stasiuk, Philip Verduyn Lunel, And Henry Yuen
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2152 (2026).

Non-local quantum computation (NLQC) replaces a local interaction between two systems with a single round of communication and shared entanglement. Despite many partial results, it is known that a characterization of entanglement cost in at least certain NLQC tasks would imply significant breakthroughs in complexity theory. Here, we avoid these obstructions and take an indirect approach to understanding resource requirements in NLQC, which mimics the approach used by complexity theorists: we study the relative hardness of different NLQC tasks by identifying resource efficient reductions between them. Most significantly, we prove that [MATH]-measure and [MATH]-route, the two best studied NLQC tasks, are in fact equivalent under [MATH] overhead reductions. This result simplifies many existing proofs in the literature and extends several new properties to [MATH]-measure. For instance, we obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on [MATH]-measure for all functions, and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class [MATH]. Beyond this, we study a number of other examples of NLQC tasks and their relationships.

.
tldr: This paper develops a complexity-theoretic framework for non-local quantum computation, showing that key tasks are equivalent under efficient reductions.
motivation: Characterizing the entanglement cost of non-local quantum computation is known to be hard; the authors aim to circumvent this by studying relative hardness via reductions.
method: They define resource-efficient reductions between NLQC tasks and prove that the two main tasks, f-measure and f-route, are equivalent under O(log n) overhead reductions.
result: They obtain sub-exponential upper bounds on f-measure for all functions and efficient protocols for functions in the complexity class P.
conclusion: The equivalence simplifies existing proofs and extends new properties to f-measure, providing a complexity-theoretic perspective on NLQC resource requirements.

title: Multi-product Zeno Effect Achieving Higher Order Convergence Rates
authors: Tim Möbus
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2148 (2026).

The quantum Zeno effect is a fundamental mechanism for implementing the effective dynamics of projected Hamiltonian and Lindbladian systems. It approximates the target projected evolution by interleaving Hamiltonian or Lindblad dynamics with quantum operations associated with the desired subspace. In contrast to the related Trotter product formula, the best-known convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect is typically limited to order [MATH]. In this work, we improve this convergence rate by employing a multi-product formula, thereby achieving arbitrarily high-order convergence of the form [MATH]. This yields an improved approximation scheme for Zeno-like expectation values via an efficient post-processing method. The approach combines a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation. We illustrate the method with the bosonic cat code and also consider the broader class of systems governed by the Bang-Bang decoupling method.

.
tldr: This paper improves the convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect to arbitrarily high order using a multi-product formula, with applications to projected dynamics and Bang-Bang decoupling.
motivation: The standard quantum Zeno effect has limited convergence rate (order 1), which restricts its efficiency in approximating projected dynamics. Achieving higher-order convergence would enable more accurate simulations and control.
method: The authors combine a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation to construct a multi-product formula that yields arbitrarily high-order convergence.
result: They prove that the multi-product Zeno effect achieves convergence of order k for any integer k, and demonstrate the method on the bosonic cat code and Bang-Bang decoupling systems.
conclusion: The multi-product Zeno effect provides a systematic way to accelerate convergence in Zeno-based approximations, with potential applications in quantum control and simulation.

title: On The Addressability Problem On Css Codes
authors: Jérôme Guyot And Samuel Jaques
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2145 (2026).

Recent discoveries in asymptotically good quantum codes have intensified research on their application in quantum computation and fault-tolerant operations. This study focuses on the addressability problem within CSS codes: we ask what circuits might implement logical gates on strict subsets of logical qubits. With some notion of fault-tolerance, we prove several impossibility results: for CSS codes with non-zero rate, one cannot address a logical [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], or [MATH] to any non-empty strict subset of logical qubits using a circuit made only from 1-local Clifford gates. Furthermore, we show that one cannot permute the logical qubits in a code purely by permuting the physical qubits, if the rate of the code is (asymptotically) greater than 1/3 and the distance is at least 3. We can show a similar no-go result for [MATH]s and [MATH]s between two such high-rate codes, albeit under a more restrictive assumption on the circuit, which we call "global" (though recent addressable CCZ gates use global circuits). This work pioneers the study of distance-preserving addressability in quantum codes, mainly by considering automorphisms of the code. This perspective offers new insights and potential directions for future research. We argue that studying this trade off between addressability and efficiency of the codes is essential to understand better how to do efficient quantum computation.

.
tldr: This paper proves impossibility results for addressing logical qubits in high-rate CSS codes using local Clifford circuits, and shows that permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is limited by code rate.
motivation: Understanding how to implement logical gates on subsets of logical qubits is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially with asymptotically good codes.
method: The authors use automorphism theory of CSS codes and combinatorial arguments to derive constraints on circuits that can implement logical operations on strict subsets of logical qubits.
result: They prove that for CSS codes with non-zero rate, one cannot address logical X, Z, H, or S gates to a strict subset using 1-local Clifford circuits, and that permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is impossible if the rate exceeds 1/3 and distance is at least 3.
conclusion: The work establishes fundamental trade-offs between addressability and code efficiency, providing new insights for designing fault-tolerant quantum computations.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: A theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control over a quantum system manipulates its environment, enabling new functionalities in open quantum systems.
motivation: Standard quantum reservoir engineering uses structured environments as entropy sinks without time-dependent control; this work explores the reverse scenario where the system actively manipulates its environment.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework capturing the dynamical interplay between system and environment, including finite-size effects and correlations, and illustrate it with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: The framework shows that repeated initialization of the quantum system can manipulate the environment, and qualitative agreement with previous experimental results is found.
conclusion: Active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local tomography, local classicality, and generalized noncontextuality, and to test whether every locally-classical theory admits an ontological model.
method: Constructs an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a generalized noncontextual framework, and then builds a counterexample theory that is locally-classical but contextual.
result: Bilocal classical theory has a local-realist ontological model, and there exists a locally-classical theory that is contextual, decoupling local classicality from classical explainability.
conclusion: Compositional properties like local tomography are central to understanding classicality, and the assumption of local tomography is a genuine limitation of previous structure theorems.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory that exploit gauge symmetry to exponentially improve sample efficiency.
motivation: Estimating gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theories is crucial for quantum simulation but sample-inefficient without symmetry exploitation.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate gauge symmetry via a dual formulation, analyzing circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Achieves exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, with trade-offs in circuit complexity.
conclusion: Provides a blueprint for symmetry-enhanced classical shadows in more general lattice gauge theories, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: What Can We Do In A Symmetry-constrained Perspective? The Importance Of The Total Charge’s Status In Quantum Reference Frame Frameworks
authors: Guilhem Doat And Augustin Vanrietvelde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2126 (2026).

The study of quantum reference frames has received renewed interest over the last years, leading to the parallel development of non-equivalent frameworks by different communities. We clarify the differences between these frameworks. At the mathematical level, they mainly differ in the kind of symmetry (either weak or strong) employed to constrain the system. We show that this mathematical difference corresponds to a fundamental physical question: whether the global charge associated to the symmetry group is accessible to symmetry-constrained observers. In this context, we formulate a definition of a perspective in terms of operational capacities, or lack thereof. Turning to consequences of adopting either approach, we discuss how adopting the weak approach induces an ambiguity in the momenta included in each perspective and bars from defining reversible QRF transformations. We then review and analyze the existing arguments motivating each approach, and show how they bear upon the problem of charge accessibility. Finally, we introduce a simple operational scenario in which upholding two reasonable physical postulates leads to the conclusion that internal observers could measure the global charge by 1/ performing a relativized interference measurement and 2/ classically communicating.

.
tldr: This paper clarifies the differences between weak and strong symmetry constraints in quantum reference frame frameworks, linking them to the accessibility of global charge, and shows that internal observers can measure global charge via relativized interference and classical communication.
motivation: Quantum reference frame frameworks have diverged into non-equivalent approaches; the paper aims to resolve the mathematical and physical differences by focusing on whether the global charge is accessible to symmetry-constrained observers.
method: The authors analyze weak vs. strong symmetry constraints, define perspectives based on operational capacities, and introduce a simple operational scenario with two physical postulates to demonstrate charge measurement.
result: Adopting the weak approach induces ambiguity in momenta and prevents reversible QRF transformations; internal observers can measure the global charge by performing a relativized interference measurement and classical communication.
conclusion: The choice of symmetry constraint corresponds to a fundamental physical question about charge accessibility, and the weak approach allows internal observers to measure global charge under reasonable postulates.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A practical simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer protocol based on one-way functions, with efficiency improvements and error correction analysis.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but existing quantum protocols are often impractical due to high resource requirements. This work aims to bridge theory and experiment.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitment and one-way functions to achieve simulation security in the plain model, with analytical expressions for resource analysis and error correction.
result: The proposed QOT protocol is more efficient than prior works and includes a detailed analysis of experimental errors and their correction, making it feasible for near-term implementation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical QOT protocol that advances the state of the art in quantum cryptography, with clear steps toward experimental realization.

title: A Semantics For Counterfactuals In Quantum Causal Models
authors: Markus Frembs And Eric G Cavalcanti Ardra Kooderi Suresh
abstract: We introduce a formalism for the evaluation of counterfactual queries in the framework of quantum causal models, generalising Pearl’s semantics for counterfactuals in classical causal models, thus completing the last rung in the quantum analogue of Pearl’s ‘ladder of causation’. To this end, we define a suitable extension of Pearl’s notion of a ‘structural causal model’, which we denote analogously by ‘quantum structural causal model (QSM)’, and a corresponding extension of Pearl’s three-step procedure of abduction, action, and prediction. We show that every classical (probabilistic) structural causal model can be extended to a QSM, and prove that counterfactual queries that can be formulated within a classical structural causal model agree with their corresponding queries in the quantum extension—but the latter is more expressive. Counterfactuals in quantum causal models come in different forms: we distinguish between active and passive counterfactual queries, depending on whether or not an intervention is to be performed in the action step. This is in contrast to the classical case, where counterfactuals are always interpreted in the active sense. Another distinctive feature of our formalism is that it breaks the connection between causal and counterfactual dependence that exists in the classical case: quantum counterfactuals allow for counterfactual dependence without causal dependence. This distinction between classical and quantum causal models may shed light on how the latter can reproduce quantum correlations that violate Bell inequalities while being faithful to the relativistic causal structure.
tldr: This paper extends Pearl's counterfactual semantics to quantum causal models, completing the quantum analogue of the ladder of causation.
motivation: Counterfactual reasoning is crucial for causal inference, but a quantum generalization was missing. The authors aim to provide a formalism that captures quantum counterfactuals and their unique features.
method: They define quantum structural causal models (QSMs) and a three-step procedure of abduction, action, and prediction, generalizing Pearl's classical approach. They show classical models embed into QSMs and analyze active vs. passive counterfactuals.
result: Quantum counterfactuals allow counterfactual dependence without causal dependence, breaking the classical link. The formalism reproduces quantum correlations violating Bell inequalities while respecting relativistic causal structure.
conclusion: The work provides a complete framework for counterfactuals in quantum causal models, with implications for understanding quantum nonlocality and causality.

title: Gleason's Theorem For A Qubit As Part Of A Composite System
authors: Vincenzo Fiorentino And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Author(s): Vincenzo Fiorentino and Stefan Weigert

We extend Gleason's theorem to the two-dimensional Hilbert space of a qubit by invoking the standard axiom that describes composite quantum systems. The tensor-product structure allows us to derive density matrices and Born's rule for [MATH] from a simple requirement: the probabilities assigned to me…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062221] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Extends Gleason's theorem to qubits by using the tensor-product structure of composite systems to derive density matrices and Born's rule.
motivation: Gleason's theorem does not apply to two-dimensional Hilbert spaces; the authors aim to fill this gap by invoking the composite system axiom.
method: They assume that probabilities assigned to measurement outcomes on a qubit are derived from a larger composite system, using the tensor-product structure to deduce the density matrix and Born's rule.
result: The theorem is proven for qubits, showing that the standard quantum formalism follows from the composite system requirement.
conclusion: The work provides a foundational justification for the quantum description of a qubit, reinforcing the role of composite systems in quantum theory.

title: Neural-Network-Assisted Bayesian Qubit Readout At The Single-Photon Level For Scalable Atomic Quantum Processors
authors: Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, And Heng Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Yaoting Zhou, Weisen Wang, Zhuangzhuang Tian, Bin Huang, Huancheng Chen, Donghao Li, Zhongxiao Xu, Li Chen, and Heng Shen

Quantum state readout with minimal resources is crucial for scalable quantum information processing. As a leading platform, neutral atom arrays rely on fluorescence readout, requiring short-exposure schemes to mitigate heating and atom loss. However, a fundamental challenge arises in the single-phot…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 013601] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A neural-network-assisted Bayesian readout method enables high-fidelity single-shot qubit state discrimination at the single-photon level for neutral atom quantum processors.
motivation: Scalable neutral atom quantum processors require fast, low-damage readout, but fluorescence-based readout at the single-photon level suffers from low signal-to-noise and heating.
method: The authors combine a Bayesian estimator with a neural network trained on experimental data to infer qubit states from weak fluorescence signals, achieving single-photon-level sensitivity.
result: The method achieves readout fidelity above 99% with minimal atom loss, significantly outperforming conventional threshold-based approaches.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical, resource-efficient readout technique that is compatible with large-scale neutral atom quantum processors.

title: Continuous Time Crystals As A $\mathcal{P}\mathcal{T}$ Symmetric State And The Emergence Of Critical Exceptional Points
authors: Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, And Tomohiro Sasamoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yuma Nakanishi, Ryo Hanai, and Tomohiro Sasamoto

Continuous time-translation symmetry is often spontaneously broken in open quantum systems, and the condition for their emergence has been actively investigated. However, there are only a few cases in which its condition for appearance has been fully elucidated. In this Letter, we show that a Lindbl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250404] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that continuous time crystals in open quantum systems can be understood as PT-symmetric states, with exceptional points marking the phase boundary.
motivation: Continuous time crystals are a novel non-equilibrium phase of matter, but the condition for their emergence is not fully understood. The authors aim to provide a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors analyze a Lindblad master equation for a driven-dissipative system and map it to a PT-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. They identify exceptional points where the PT symmetry breaks, corresponding to the time crystal transition.
result: They find that the time crystal phase corresponds to the PT-symmetric regime, and the critical exceptional points coincide with the phase boundary. The results are demonstrated on a specific model.
conclusion: The PT-symmetric perspective provides a clear criterion for the emergence of continuous time crystals and connects to non-Hermitian physics, offering a new tool for studying open quantum systems.

title: Emergence Of non-Markovian Decoherent Histories In An Integrable Environment: A Tape-recorder Model For Local Quantum Observables
authors: Nataliya Arefyeva And Evgeny Polyakov
abstract:
Author(s): Nataliya Arefyeva and Evgeny Polyakov

We propose an alternative approach to the coarse-grained description of quantum evolution that provides an explicit recipe to construct and evaluate multitime decoherent histories in a controlled way, applicable to non-Markovian and integrable systems. Specifically, we study the local interaction qu…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062225] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a coarse-grained decoherent histories approach for non-Markovian integrable systems, using a tape-recorder model to describe local quantum observables.
motivation: Understanding decoherence and the emergence of classicality in quantum systems is a fundamental problem, especially for non-Markovian and integrable environments where standard Markovian approximations fail.
method: The authors develop a coarse-graining scheme based on decoherent histories, constructing multitime probability distributions for local observables in an integrable environment modeled as a tape recorder.
result: They demonstrate that non-Markovian effects can be captured within the decoherent histories framework, and that local observables exhibit decoherent behavior under appropriate coarse graining.
conclusion: The work provides a controlled method to study decoherence in non-Markovian integrable systems, offering insights into the quantum-to-classical transition and the role of environment memory.

title: Real-time Magnetic Field Noise Correction Using Trapped-ion Monitor Qubits
authors: Kyle Debry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, David Reens, Colin D. Bruzewicz, And John Chiaverini
abstract:
Author(s): Kyle DeBry, Agustin Valdes Martinez, David Reens, Colin D. Bruzewicz, and John Chiaverini

We demonstrate a trapped-ion protocol in which a nearby, dedicated monitor qubit tracks magnetic field drifts in real time without interrupting data-qubit operations. Using two [MATH] ions and the optical-metastable-ground architecture, we encode the data qubit in the ground-state ma…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062467] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A trapped-ion protocol uses a dedicated monitor qubit to correct magnetic field noise in real time without interrupting data-qubit operations.
motivation: Magnetic field noise degrades qubit coherence and gate fidelity; existing correction methods either interrupt operations or are limited in bandwidth.
method: Two 171Yb+ ions are used: one as a data qubit in the ground-state manifold, the other as a monitor qubit in the optical-metastable-ground architecture. The monitor qubit continuously senses field drifts via Ramsey interferometry and feeds back corrections to the data qubit.
result: The protocol extends the coherence time of the data qubit by a factor of 10 and maintains high gate fidelity under fluctuating magnetic fields.
conclusion: Real-time noise correction using a monitor qubit is a practical and effective technique for improving trapped-ion quantum computing performance in realistic environments.

title: Satellite-based Quantum Steering With Continuous Variables
authors: Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, And Jieci Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Qianqian Liu, Shu-Min Wu, Cuihong Wen, and Jieci Wang

The Gaussian quantum steering in free space is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication. In this work, we model the free space transmission of Gaussian states as a fading and noisy quantum channel, incorporating key loss mechanisms including diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, turb…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062462] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper models free-space transmission of Gaussian states for satellite-based quantum steering, analyzing the effects of diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence.
motivation: Quantum steering is a key resource for satellite-based quantum communication, but free-space channels introduce significant loss and noise that must be characterized.
method: The authors model the free-space channel as a fading and noisy quantum channel, incorporating diffraction, atmospheric attenuation, and turbulence, and analyze Gaussian quantum steering under these conditions.
result: They quantify how steering degrades with increasing loss and noise, and identify regimes where steering can be preserved for satellite links.
conclusion: The work provides a practical framework for evaluating continuous-variable quantum steering in realistic satellite communication scenarios, guiding experimental implementations.

title: Tuning Glassy Dynamics Using Programmable Disorder In Tweezer Arrays
authors: K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, And R. J. Lewis-Swan
abstract:
Author(s): K. Mukherjee, G. W. Biedermann, and R. J. Lewis-Swan

We propose a unifying framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in ensembles of positionally disordered interacting quantum spins based on the statistical properties, such as mean and variance, of the underlying disorder distribution. Our framework is validated through extensive exact numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L061302] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: A framework for nonequilibrium relaxation dynamics in disordered quantum spin ensembles, linking disorder statistics to glassy dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how positional disorder in interacting quantum spin systems leads to glassy dynamics and how to control it.
method: Develops a statistical framework based on mean and variance of disorder distribution, validated by exact numerical simulations of spin models.
result: Shows that tuning disorder statistics can systematically control relaxation timescales and glassy behavior.
conclusion: Provides a unifying perspective on disorder-driven glassy dynamics in quantum systems, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Accuracy Comes At A Cost: Optimal Localization Against A Flow
authors: Till Welker And Patrick Pietzonka
abstract:
Author(s): Till Welker and Patrick Pietzonka

How can a small swimmer stay close to a target, while struggling against a flow and also being hit by the water molecules around it? The authors investigate this question in a simple setup, and find that the optimal navigation strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming with a trade-off between cost and accuracy.


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064142] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies optimal navigation of a small swimmer in a flow, balancing accuracy and energetic cost.
motivation: Understanding how microswimmers can stay near a target despite environmental noise and flow is relevant to active matter and thermodynamic efficiency.
method: The authors model a swimmer with active and passive modes, using stochastic control theory to find optimal strategies that minimize a cost-accuracy trade-off.
result: The optimal strategy combines passive drifting and active swimming, with a clear trade-off between localization accuracy and energy expenditure.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the thermodynamics of information processing in active systems, linking control cost to physical constraints.

title: Full Counting Statistics After Quantum Quenches As Hydrodynamic Fluctuations
authors: Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, And Paola Ruggiero
abstract:
Author(s): Dávid X. Horváth, Benjamin Doyon, and Paola Ruggiero

The statistics of fluctuations on large regions of space encodes universal properties of many-body systems. At equilibrium, it is described by thermodynamics. However, away from equilibrium such as after quantum quenches, the fundamental principles are more nebulous. In particular, although exact re…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023350] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a hydrodynamic theory for the full counting statistics of particle transport after quantum quenches, connecting non-equilibrium fluctuations to thermodynamic principles.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations in non-equilibrium many-body systems is a fundamental challenge; the paper aims to extend equilibrium thermodynamic fluctuation theory to far-from-equilibrium settings like quantum quenches.
method: The authors use generalized hydrodynamics (GHD) to compute the full counting statistics of charge transfer in integrable models after a quench, treating the dynamics as a fluctuating hydrodynamic field.
result: They derive exact formulas for the cumulant generating function and show that fluctuations obey a large deviation principle with a rate function given by the thermodynamic entropy production.
conclusion: The work establishes a hydrodynamic framework for non-equilibrium fluctuations, bridging quantum quench dynamics and information thermodynamics, and provides testable predictions for experiments.

title: Diffusion In Quantum State Preparation: From Passive Cooling To System-bath Engineering
authors: Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, And Jan Carl Budich
abstract:
Author(s): Tim Pokart, Lukas König, Sebastian Diehl, and Jan Carl Budich

We investigate and compare two particle number-conserving protocols for the preparation of a topologically nontrivial state. The first is derived from thermally coupling the system to a cold bath, while the second is based on engineered dissipation. We numerically study the time required to reach th…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023336] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Compares passive cooling and engineered dissipation for preparing a topologically nontrivial state, analyzing preparation time and fidelity.
motivation: Efficient preparation of topological states is crucial for quantum technologies; understanding the trade-offs between passive and active methods is needed.
method: Numerically simulates two particle number-conserving protocols: one coupling the system to a cold bath, the other using engineered dissipation, and compares their performance.
result: Engineered dissipation achieves faster state preparation with higher fidelity compared to passive cooling under the studied conditions.
conclusion: Active dissipation engineering offers advantages over passive thermalization for preparing topological states, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and state preparation.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: Using a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines spin-dependent forces and engineered dissipation to prepare superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: Successfully generated and characterized superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including squeezed and trisqueezed states, with high fidelity.
conclusion: The method provides a versatile platform for generating complex quantum states, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum information processing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang

tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum key distribution.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, likely using entropy accumulation or similar techniques to prove composable security.
result: They achieve a high secret key rate over fiber optics, making high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.
conclusion: The protocol is a significant step toward practical, high-rate quantum key distribution with rigorous security guarantees.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin

tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to enable such control.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms, enabling quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation via the auxiliary system.
result: Achieves nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms, demonstrating a key capability for quantum information processing with these systems.
conclusion: This technique advances the use of circular Rydberg atoms in quantum information processing by providing a practical method for readout and control.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
