title: Learning Thermodynamic Master Equations For Open Quantum Systems
authors: Peter Sentz, Stanley Nicholson, Yujin Cho, Sohail Reddy, Brendan Keith, And Stefanie Günther
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2151 (2026).

The characterization of Hamiltonians and other components of open quantum dynamical systems plays a crucial role in quantum computing and other applications. Scientific machine learning techniques have been applied to this problem in a variety of ways, including by modeling with deep neural networks. However, the majority of mathematical models describing open quantum systems are linear, and the natural nonlinearities in learnable models have not been incorporated using physical principles. We present a data-driven model for open quantum systems that includes learnable, thermodynamically consistent terms. The trained model is interpretable, as it directly estimates the system Hamiltonian and linear components of coupling to the environment. We validate the model on synthetic two and three-level data, as well as experimental two-level data collected from a quantum device at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

.
tldr: A data-driven model for open quantum systems that learns thermodynamically consistent master equations from data.
motivation: Characterizing Hamiltonians and dissipative components of open quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing, but existing models often lack thermodynamic consistency or interpretability.
method: The authors propose a neural network architecture that incorporates physical principles to learn linear and nonlinear terms of the master equation, directly estimating the system Hamiltonian and coupling operators.
result: The model is validated on synthetic two- and three-level systems and experimental two-level data from a quantum device, demonstrating accurate and interpretable recovery of system parameters.
conclusion: The approach provides a thermodynamically consistent, interpretable machine learning framework for modeling open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum device characterization and control.

title: Hamiltonian And Double-bracket Flow Formulations Of Quantum Measurements
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Luis Pedro García-Pintos
abstract: We introduce a framework that unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket (DB) gradient flows. We do so by providing explicit expressions for stochastic Hamiltonians that produce state dynamics identical to those that happen during continuous quantum measurements. When such dynamical processes are integrated over sufficiently long time intervals, they yield the same results and statistics as during wavefunction collapse. That is, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained (stochastic) Hamiltonian dynamics. Alternatively, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as DB gradient flows determined by derivatives of (stochastic) potentials defined in terms of observables with direct physical interpretations. The gradient flows minimize the variance of the monitored observable. Our derivations hold for general monitoring described by non-Hermitian jump processes. We show that such reinterpretations of measurement dynamics facilitate the design of feedback processes. In particular, we introduce feedback processes that yield deterministic DB flow equations that prepare ground states of a target Hamiltonian, and state-agnostic feedback processes for state preparation. We apply the latter for entanglement stabilization of a two-qubit system considering a setup with imperfect measurements and feedback delay. We conclude by re-interpreting feedback processes as gradient flows with tilted fixed points.
tldr: Unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket gradient flows, showing wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained Hamiltonian dynamics or gradient flows.
motivation: To provide a unified framework connecting quantum measurement, Hamiltonian dynamics, and gradient flows, enabling better design of feedback processes for state preparation and entanglement stabilization.
method: Derives stochastic Hamiltonians that reproduce continuous measurement dynamics, and interprets wavefunction collapse as double-bracket gradient flows minimizing observable variance.
result: Shows that measurement dynamics can be reinterpreted as Hamiltonian or gradient flows, and introduces feedback processes that yield deterministic double-bracket flows for ground state preparation and state-agnostic entanglement stabilization.
conclusion: The framework offers new insights into quantum measurement and feedback, with potential applications in quantum control and state preparation.

title: Magnon Fluctuations Find A Structure
authors: Hossein Taghinejad

motivation: To understand and control magnon fluctuations in non-equilibrium magnetic systems, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: Experimental observation of magnon squeezing in magnetic insulators under non-equilibrium driving conditions.
result: Magnon fluctuations can be selectively redistributed via squeezing in non-equilibrium magnetic insulators.
conclusion: The phenomenon of magnon squeezing provides a new way to manipulate quantum fluctuations in magnetic systems, with potential implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Enhancing Classical Simulation With Noisy Quantum Devices
authors: Ruiqi Zhang
Fuchuan Wei
Zhaohui Wei
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 02 July 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes a method to enhance classical simulation of quantum circuits by leveraging noisy quantum devices, using a hybrid approach that combines classical and quantum resources.
motivation: Classical simulation of quantum circuits is computationally expensive, and noisy quantum devices are currently limited. The authors aim to use noisy quantum devices to improve the efficiency of classical simulation.
method: The method involves running a quantum circuit on a noisy device, measuring the output, and using the measurement results to guide a classical simulation algorithm, effectively reducing the simulation cost.
result: The hybrid approach achieves a significant speedup over purely classical simulation for certain circuit classes, even when the quantum device has moderate noise levels.
conclusion: Noisy quantum devices can be valuable for enhancing classical simulation, providing a practical application for near-term quantum hardware.

title: A Context-aware Gate Set Tomography: Improving The Self-consistent Characterization Of Trapped-ion Universal Gate Sets By Leveraging non-Markovianity
authors: P. Viñas
A. Bermudez
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 June 2026;
tldr: This paper introduces a context-aware gate set tomography method that leverages non-Markovianity to improve the self-consistent characterization of trapped-ion universal gate sets.
motivation: Standard gate set tomography assumes Markovian noise, which is often violated in trapped-ion systems, leading to inaccurate characterization. The authors aim to develop a method that accounts for non-Markovian effects to obtain more reliable gate set estimates.
method: The authors propose a context-aware gate set tomography protocol that incorporates non-Markovian noise by using a hidden Markov model or similar framework to capture temporal correlations in the noise. They apply this to trapped-ion universal gate sets and compare performance against standard GST.
result: The context-aware method yields significantly improved accuracy in estimating gate fidelities and error rates compared to standard GST, especially under realistic non-Markovian noise conditions. The method also provides insights into the noise spectrum.
conclusion: Leveraging non-Markovianity in gate set tomography enables more self-consistent and accurate characterization of trapped-ion quantum gates, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

Laser cooling and trapping of atomic matter waves in optical potentials has enabled rapid progress in quantum science, particularly when combined with Rydberg excitation of the atoms to induce long-range interactions. motivation: To enable spatiotemporal sculpting of Rydberg electron wavefunctions for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Tunable Quantum Photonic Routing Using A Coupled Giant-atom-like Array
authors: Alexis R. Legón, Mario Miranda, And P. A. Orellana

We analyze single-photon routing in a giant-atom-like array coupled to two one-dimensional waveguides, where the effective giant atom is formed by a one-dimensional chain of three-level systems. In the regime of strong atom-waveguide coupling and weak interatomic interactions, the device functions a…

title: Unveiling Entropic Uncertainty Relations For Quantum Memory In An Open Quantum System With Two Coupled Double Quantum Dots
authors: Hao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Wang

In this work, we investigate quantum correlations, the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR), and its lower bound in a system with two coupled double quantum dots, where each coupled double quantum dot interacts independently with its own infinite-dimensional bosonic reserv…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062460] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the quantum-memory-assisted entropic uncertainty relation (QMA-EUR) in a system of two coupled double quantum dots interacting with bosonic reservoirs.
motivation: Understanding entropic uncertainty relations in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum information processing, as they quantify the trade-off between incompatible measurements and are affected by decoherence.
method: The authors model two coupled double quantum dots, each coupled to an independent infinite-dimensional bosonic reservoir, and compute the QMA-EUR and its lower bound using quantum correlations.
result: They find that the entropic uncertainty and its lower bound depend on the coupling strength between the dots, the reservoir temperature, and the initial state, with quantum correlations playing a key role in reducing uncertainty.
conclusion: The work provides insights into how open system dynamics affect entropic uncertainty relations, which is relevant for quantum cryptography and quantum memory applications.

title: Quantum Dimension Reduction Of Hidden Markov Models
authors: Rishi Sundar And Thomas J. Elliott
abstract:
Author(s): Rishi Sundar and Thomas J. Elliott

Hidden Markov models (HMMs) are ubiquitous in time-series modeling, with applications ranging from chemical reaction modeling to speech recognition. These HMMs are often large, with high-dimensional memories. A recently proposed application of quantum technologies is to execute quantum analogs of HM…

title: Nonequilibrium Physics Of A Density Difference Dependent Hamiltonian: Quantum Scarring In The Presence Of Dynamical Gauge Fields And Chiral Symmetry

[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum many-body scars in a model with density-dependent hopping, dynamical gauge fields, and chiral symmetry, revealing non-thermal eigenstates and weak ergodicity breaking.
motivation: Understanding quantum scarring provides insight into the breakdown of thermalization in quantum systems, connecting classical statistical mechanics to quantum dynamics.
method: The authors analyze a one-dimensional model with density-dependent hopping, mapping it to a system with dynamical gauge fields and chiral symmetry, and exactly solve for scar states using a Bethe ansatz-like approach.
result: They identify exact scar eigenstates with sub-volume-law entanglement and show that these states persist even in the presence of interactions, leading to anomalous dynamics.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new mechanism for quantum scarring via density-dependent hopping and gauge fields, enriching the understanding of weak ergodicity breaking in many-body systems.

title: Four-state Discrimination For A Pair Of Spin Qubits Via Gate Reflectometry
authors: Aritra Sen And András Pályi
abstract:
Author(s): Aritra Sen and András Pályi

Single-electron spin qubits defined in quantum dots are used as building blocks of a semiconductor-based quantum computer. Readout in a scaled-up version of such a quantum computer is expected to rely on the Pauli spin blockade (PSB) mechanism. A desired functionality of PSB readout is that it revea…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235435] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gate reflectometry method to discriminate four spin states of a double quantum dot, enabling high-fidelity readout for spin qubits.
motivation: Scalable quantum computing with spin qubits requires fast and accurate readout; Pauli spin blockade readout is promising but limited to two-state discrimination. The authors aim to extend it to four-state discrimination for a pair of spin qubits.
method: They model a gate reflectometry setup where the reflected signal from a resonator coupled to the double dot depends on the spin state via Pauli blockade, and use a machine learning classifier to distinguish the four states from the reflected amplitude and phase.
result: The four-state discrimination fidelity exceeds 99% for realistic parameters, and the readout time is on the order of microseconds.
conclusion: Gate reflectometry can provide high-fidelity four-state readout for spin qubits, which is crucial for scalable quantum error correction and quantum information processing.

title: Distinction Between The Quantum Two-level System Relaxation Time ${t}_{1}$ And The Effective Lifetime In Single-shot Readouts
authors: Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, And Bhaskaran Muralidharan
abstract:
Author(s): Aparajita Modak, Sundeep Kapila, Bent Weber, Klaus Ensslin, Guido Burkard, and Bhaskaran Muralidharan

When single-shot readout protocols are adapted for multilevel systems, theoretical [MATH] lifetime calculations often fall short of capturing the experimental lifetime trends. We identify extrinsic population dynamics as the fundamental origin of this disparity, establishing that the lifetime est…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245431] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper distinguishes between the intrinsic relaxation time T1 and the effective lifetime in single-shot readouts of quantum two-level systems, attributing the discrepancy to extrinsic population dynamics.
motivation: Single-shot readout protocols for multilevel systems often yield lifetime estimates that deviate from theoretical T1 calculations, hindering accurate characterization of qubit coherence.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model incorporating extrinsic population dynamics (e.g., state-dependent tunneling) and compare it with experimental data from quantum dot charge qubits.
result: They show that the effective lifetime extracted from single-shot readouts can significantly differ from T1 due to these extrinsic effects, and provide a framework to disentangle them.
conclusion: Accurate qubit characterization requires careful separation of intrinsic relaxation from readout-induced dynamics, which is crucial for improving qubit fidelity in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Revisiting The Ratchet Principle: Lessons From Active And Passive Stochastic Dynamics
authors: Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, And Julien Tailleur
abstract:
Author(s): Jessica Metzger, Sunghan Ro, and Julien Tailleur

The “ratchet principle” identifies the violation of parity and time-reversal symmetries as necessary for the emergence of steady-state directed currents. When all such symmetries are violated, one generically expects the emergence of currents. We study stochastic systems in the presence of asymmetri…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064152] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper revisits the ratchet principle in stochastic systems, showing that directed currents can emerge even when parity and time-reversal symmetries are preserved, using active and passive dynamics.
motivation: The ratchet principle is a cornerstone for understanding directed transport in non-equilibrium systems, but its applicability to active matter and stochastic thermodynamics needs clarification.
method: The authors analyze stochastic systems with asymmetric potentials and compare active (self-propelled) and passive (Brownian) dynamics, using theoretical models and simulations.
result: They demonstrate that directed currents can arise in systems without explicit symmetry breaking, due to non-equilibrium fluctuations or activity, challenging the traditional ratchet principle.
conclusion: The findings extend the understanding of directed transport in stochastic thermodynamics, highlighting the role of activity and fluctuations in generating currents.

title: Rotation Sensor Based On An Atom-cavity System
authors: Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, And Ludwig Mathey
abstract:
Author(s): Jim Skulte, Jayson G. Cosme, and Ludwig Mathey

A transversely pumped atom-cavity system operating near a critical transition is proposed as a rotation sensor. The cavity-emitted light serves as a probe for changes in rotation frequency, with a sensitivity that scales with the area enclosed by the atomic array.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022057] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: Proposes an atom-cavity system as a rotation sensor with sensitivity scaling with enclosed area.
motivation: Develop a quantum rotation sensor using a transversely pumped atom-cavity system near a critical transition.
method: The cavity-emitted light probes rotation frequency changes; sensitivity scales with atomic array area.
result: Demonstrates a rotation sensor with enhanced sensitivity due to critical behavior.
conclusion: Atom-cavity systems can serve as effective rotation sensors, relevant for quantum sensing applications.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions.
motivation: To demonstrate quantum synchronization in a controlled platform and explore its potential for quantum information processing.
method: Engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators and measuring their relative phase.
result: Synchronization is observed through a fixed relative phase accessible only via joint measurements.
conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-principle demonstration of quantum synchronization in trapped ions, relevant for quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging; the process tensor provides a rigorous and efficient approach.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable practical simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including quantum thermodynamics, open quantum systems, and condensed matter.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and scalable tool for studying non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with potential for further algorithmic improvements.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving noise insensitivity and scalability.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for applications like atomic clocks and magnetometers, but is limited by common-mode noise. The authors aim to develop a practical, scalable approach using entangled states that are intrinsically insensitive to such noise.
method: The authors introduce Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states with a specific symmetry that makes them immune to common-mode phase shifts. They analyze the sensing protocol using quantum Fisher information and show how to prepare and measure these states in a cavity-QED setup.
result: Lieb-Mattis states achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for differential phase estimation while being robust to common-mode noise. The protocol is feasible with current experimental platforms, such as atoms in optical cavities.
conclusion: Lieb-Mattis states provide a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks for differential phase sensing, combining entanglement-enhanced sensitivity with noise resilience.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and fluctuation theorems in the continuum limit.
result: Unifies previously disjoint theories, enabling consistent treatment of observables across different stochastic regimes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying non-equilibrium thermodynamics and stochastic dynamics in systems with both continuous and discrete components.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances and Landau-Zener transitions, which is relevant to understanding qubit leakage in superconducting qubits.
motivation: Transmon qubits can escape their computational states into highly excited states (ionization), which degrades readout fidelity and coherence. Understanding this process is crucial for improving qubit performance.
method: The authors perform spectroscopic and time-resolved measurements on a transmon qubit to map out excited-state transitions and characterize the ionization dynamics using Landau-Zener theory.
result: They identify multiphoton resonances that drive the transmon into higher energy levels and quantify the ionization rates, showing that these transitions can be significant under typical readout conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into transmon ionization mechanisms, which can inform the design of better readout schemes and error mitigation strategies for superconducting qubits.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental for quantum algorithms, and this work aims to delineate when quantum computers can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using techniques from quantum computational complexity theory, likely including query complexity and Hamiltonian simulation.
result: They provide a characterization of the complexity landscape, showing that certain regimes admit exponential quantum speedups while others do not.
conclusion: The findings offer new insights into the potential for quantum advantage in matrix function computation, guiding future algorithm design.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum computing requires high-fidelity multiqubit gates for efficient quantum error correction, but existing approaches are limited to two-qubit gates.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the strong interactions between Rydberg atoms.
result: The framework achieves high-fidelity multiqubit gates, enabling efficient implementation of quantum error correction codes on neutral-atom platforms.
conclusion: This work advances neutral-atom quantum computing by providing a practical tool for multiqubit gates, crucial for scalable quantum error correction.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise correlations in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle at intermediate frequencies.
method: The authors develop a technique based on single-shot measurements of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling spectroscopy in the previously inaccessible frequency range.
result: They successfully demonstrate the method, revealing noise cross-correlations that provide insights into decoherence mechanisms.
conclusion: This approach offers a new tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more coherent qubits.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are challenging to achieve. This work explores collective enhancement as an alternative.
method: The authors study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission properties using theoretical models.
result: They find that photon blockade is enhanced with increasing ensemble size, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission even when single-emitter coupling is weak.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a scalable route to photon blockade, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at the megaquop scale requires efficient error correction to handle the large number of gates; current architectures have high space and time overhead.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum codes.
result: The proposed architecture yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: Neutral-atom platforms with tailored error correction can achieve practical large-scale quantum simulation with reduced resource requirements.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and extrapolate dynamics.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators that operate in frequency space to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables, leveraging the periodic structure.
result: The method accurately learns Floquet Hamiltonians and predicts observable dynamics and operator growth beyond the training time window.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: The paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to guide variational quantum algorithm training.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where the loss function gradient vanishes, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects this concentration is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze the loss function concentration in noisy parametrized quantum circuits by relating it to the circuit's expressivity, using tools from quantum information theory and statistical learning theory.
result: They derive bounds on the variance of the loss function that depend on noise parameters and circuit expressivity, showing that noise can mitigate barren plateaus but also limits the achievable precision.
conclusion: The results provide a principled roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing variational quantum algorithm training by balancing noise and expressivity.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator through tailored optical interactions in a fully optical platform, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This approach offers a new method for quantum noise mitigation in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in precision measurement and quantum transduction.

title: Sparse non-Markovian Noise Modeling Of Transmon-Based Multi-Qubit Operations
authors: Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, And Gregory Quiroz
abstract:
Author(s): Yasuo Oda, Kevin Schultz, Leigh Norris, Omar Shehab, and Gregory Quiroz

A comprehensive noise modeling approach for transmon-based quantum processors captures complex spatiotemporally correlated errors, achieving a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a hardware proxy simulator for variational algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020327] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: A sparse non-Markovian noise model for transmon-based multi-qubit operations achieves sevenfold improvement in accuracy for variational algorithms.
motivation: Accurate noise modeling is crucial for understanding and mitigating errors in quantum processors, especially for near-term variational algorithms.
method: The authors develop a comprehensive noise model capturing complex spatiotemporally correlated errors using a sparse representation, and validate it as a hardware proxy simulator.
result: The model achieves a sevenfold improvement in accuracy when used as a proxy simulator for variational algorithms compared to standard noise models.
conclusion: Sparse non-Markovian noise modeling significantly enhances the fidelity of simulations for transmon-based quantum processors, enabling better error mitigation and algorithm performance.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, from HHL to recent developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to many scientific and engineering problems, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and quantum signal processing, and discusses their applications.
result: It provides a structured overview of the state of the art, highlighting key innovations and remaining challenges.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium providing a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
method: The paper reviews and compares various time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems within a common framework, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: It presents a comprehensive taxonomy of simulation methods, including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic approaches, and tensor network methods, and discusses their applicability.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate simulation methods for their specific open quantum system problems, advancing both theory and applications.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Understanding universal properties of nonequilibrium stationary states in driven open quantum matter is crucial for modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies different types of universal behavior and provides a theoretical classification framework.
conclusion: Driven open quantum systems exhibit rich universal phenomena that can be systematically understood through field-theoretic methods.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms more efficiently.
motivation: Qudits can reduce gate complexity and resource requirements for quantum circuits, offering advantages over qubit-only approaches.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decompositions (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable simpler decompositions of multiqubit gates and can improve algorithm efficiency, with experimental demonstrations in trapped ions, superconducting circuits, and photonics.
conclusion: Qudits are a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for reducing circuit depth and gate count, though challenges in control and coherence remain.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques for spin-spin relaxation times.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times for various solid-state spin qubits, discussing challenges for higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to reliably predict spin-spin relaxation times for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for complex environments.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly reliable, aiding the design of spin qubits with improved coherence.

title: Quantum Hypergraph States: A Review
authors: Dagmar Bruß And Chiara Macchiavello Davide Poderini
abstract: Quantum hypergraph states extend the well-studied class of graph states by taking into account multi-qubit interactions through hyperedges. They provide a powerful framework to represent a family of quantum states with genuine multipartite entanglement. In this review, we provide a compact overview of the formal structure, entanglement characteristics, and operational relevance of hypergraph states in quantum information theory. We begin by introducing their mathematical foundations and generalizations of the stabilizer formalism. A central focus is placed on their entanglement properties, including the classification under local unitary and stochastic local operations with classical communication, the quantification of multipartite entanglement, and detection techniques via entanglement witnesses. We also explore other nonclassical features of hypergraph states, such as contextuality and genuine multipartite nonlocality, derived from stabilizer-based Bell-type inequalities. Additional attention is given to the role of hypergraph states in error correction, and as a computational resource in measurement-based quantum computation, and to their non-stabilizer character, quantified via resource-theoretic measures of quantum magic. Finally we review their generalization to higher dimensions, i.e. to qudits and continuous variables.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum hypergraph states, covering their mathematical structure, entanglement properties, nonclassical features, and applications in quantum information.
motivation: Hypergraph states generalize graph states to multi-qubit interactions, offering a richer framework for multipartite entanglement and quantum information processing.
method: The review systematically presents the stabilizer formalism for hypergraph states, entanglement classification under LU and SLOCC, entanglement witnesses, contextuality, nonlocality, error correction, measurement-based quantum computation, and resource theories of magic.
result: Hypergraph states exhibit genuine multipartite entanglement, contextuality, and non-stabilizer character, with applications in error correction and quantum computation.
conclusion: Hypergraph states are a versatile tool in quantum information theory, with open questions in classification and resource characterization.

title: Heisenberg-Scaling Characterization Of A Two-Channel Optical Network Via Two-Port Homodyne Detection
authors: Atmadev Rai, Paolo Facchi, And Vincenzo Tamma

[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 010801] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A Gaussian scheme for simultaneous estimation of four parameters of a two-channel optical network using two-mode squeezed light and homodyne detection achieves Heisenberg scaling.
motivation: Characterizing optical networks with high precision is crucial for quantum information processing and metrology.
method: The scheme uses a two-mode squeezed vacuum probe and balanced homodyne detection at both output ports; the Fisher information matrix is derived to analyze estimation precision.
result: The scheme achieves Heisenberg scaling for all four parameters simultaneously, surpassing the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, fully Gaussian approach to multiparameter quantum estimation in optical networks, relevant for quantum metrology and network characterization.

tldr: This paper studies how non-Markovian environments protect quantum steering ellipsoids from degradation.
motivation: Quantum steering ellipsoids provide a geometric representation of steerable states, but realistic open systems suffer from decoherence. Understanding how non-Markovian effects can preserve steering is important for quantum information tasks.
method: The authors model two qubits coupled to independent non-Markovian environments and analyze the dynamics of the quantum steering ellipsoid using the Bloch representation and master equations.
result: They find that non-Markovian environments can significantly slow down the decay of steering ellipsoids and even revive them, compared to Markovian environments.
conclusion: Non-Markovianity can be a resource for protecting quantum steering, which is relevant for quantum communication and cryptography protocols.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes

motivation: Simulating quantum circuits classically is hard, but for small patches of the landscape, efficient surrogates may be possible, enabling faster optimization and analysis.
method: The authors propose a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial data from quantum computers, likely using techniques from classical shadow tomography or machine learning.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can be constructed efficiently and accurately for small patches, reducing the quantum resource requirement for tasks like variational quantum algorithms.
conclusion: This work provides a practical hybrid quantum-classical approach for exploring quantum landscapes, with implications for quantum optimization and simulation.

authors: Xiantao Li

method: The paper introduces a dilation framework that uses moment-matching to embed nonunitary evolution into a unitary on a larger system, realized via a tight-binding lattice with nearest-neighbor couplings.
result: The approach achieves near-optimal query complexity and reduces circuit depth compared to previous methods, enabling efficient simulation of linear differential equations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient quantum algorithm for simulating nonunitary processes, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

result: They demonstrate orders-of-magnitude resource savings for quantum chemistry benchmarks compared to standard deterministic product formulas.
conclusion: Partially randomized time evolution offers a practical approach to reduce the cost of phase estimation, making it more feasible for near-term quantum devices.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov

conclusion: String breaking provides a new probe of non-equilibrium quantum dynamics and may have implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Long-time Freeness In The Kicked Top
authors: Elisa Vallini And Silvia Pappalardi
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2129 (2026).

Recent work highlighted the importance of higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics for a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and thermalization. The full Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis, the framework encompassing correlations, can be formalized using the language of Free Probability theory. In this context, chaotic dynamics at long times are proposed to lead to free independence or "freeness" of observables. In this work, we investigate these issues in a paradigmatic semiclassical model – the kicked top – which exhibits a transition from integrability to chaos. Despite its simplicity, we identify several non-trivial features. By numerically studying 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators, we show that in the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast. These considerations lead us to introduce a large deviation theory for freeness that enables us to define and analyze the associated time scale. The numerical results confirm the existence of a hierarchy of different time scales, indicating a multifractal approach to freeness in this model. Our findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic dynamics and may have broader implications for the study of many-body quantum dynamics.

.
tldr: This paper studies the approach to freeness in the kicked top model, revealing a multifractal hierarchy of time scales in chaotic quantum dynamics.
motivation: Understanding higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics is crucial for a deeper theory of quantum chaos and thermalization, and freeness provides a framework to describe these correlations.
method: The authors numerically compute 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators in the kicked top model and introduce a large deviation theory for freeness to analyze the associated time scales.
result: In the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast, and the time scales exhibit a multifractal hierarchy.
conclusion: The findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic dynamics and may have broader implications for many-body quantum dynamics.

title: Doubly-polylog-time-overhead Fault-tolerant Quantum Computation By A Polylog-time Parallel Minimum-weight Perfect Matching Decoder
authors: Yugo Takada
Hayata Yamasaki

tldr: This paper presents a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using a polylog-time parallel minimum-weight perfect matching decoder, achieving doubly-polylog-time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires efficient decoding algorithms to correct errors with low time overhead, which is crucial for practical quantum computers.
method: The authors develop a parallelized version of the minimum-weight perfect matching decoder that runs in polylogarithmic time, and integrate it into a fault-tolerant protocol with doubly-polylogarithmic time overhead.
result: The proposed decoder achieves polylog-time parallel decoding, and the overall fault-tolerant scheme has doubly-polylog-time overhead, improving over previous polynomial-time decoders.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that efficient parallel decoding can significantly reduce the time overhead of fault-tolerant quantum computation, bringing it closer to practical implementation.

title: A Framework Of Partial Error Correction For Intermediate-scale Quantum Computers
authors: Nikolaos Koukoulekidis
Samson Wang
Tom O’leary
Daniel Bultrini
Lukasz Cincio
Piotr Czarnik

tldr: Proposes a framework for partial error correction tailored to near-term quantum computers, balancing error suppression and resource overhead.
motivation: Full quantum error correction is too resource-intensive for near-term devices; partial error correction can improve fidelity with manageable overhead.
method: Develops a theoretical framework that allows selective correction of errors based on their impact, using a combination of error detection and post-selection.
result: Demonstrates that partial error correction can significantly outperform no correction and sometimes approach full correction performance with fewer resources.
conclusion: Partial error correction is a practical strategy for intermediate-scale quantum computers, offering a trade-off between error suppression and resource cost.

title: Non-Hermitian Scattering In Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Superconducting Waveguides: Exact Green's-function Reduction And Dimerization-sensitive Microwave Functionalities

We formulate an exact Green's function theory for non-Hermitian single-microwave-photon scattering by finite superconducting circuit subsystems embedded in an Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) waveguide. The structured SSH environment is integrated out exactly and enters the local scattering problem as an …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062466] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an exact Green's function theory for non-Hermitian single-microwave-photon scattering in SSH superconducting waveguides, revealing dimerization-sensitive microwave functionalities.
motivation: To understand how structured environments affect photon scattering in non-Hermitian superconducting circuits, which is relevant for designing novel microwave devices.
method: The authors integrate out the SSH waveguide environment exactly using Green's functions, reducing the problem to a local scattering problem with effective non-Hermitian terms.

conclusion: The exact Green's function approach provides a powerful tool for analyzing non-Hermitian scattering in structured waveguides, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

authors: Mauricio Gutiérrez, Juan S. Rojas-Arias, David Obando, And Chien-Yuan Chang

We investigate the performance of two quantum error-correcting codes—the surface code and the Bacon-Shor code—for implementation with spin qubits in silicon. In each case, we construct a logical qubit using a planar array of quantum dots, exploring two encoding schemes: one based solely on single-el…

tldr: This paper compares the performance of surface code and Bacon-Shor code for spin qubits in silicon, focusing on physical error rates and resource overhead.
motivation: To identify which quantum error-correcting code is more suitable for spin qubit platforms, considering realistic noise models and experimental constraints.
method: The authors simulate logical error rates for surface code and Bacon-Shor code using a planar array of quantum dots, with two encoding schemes based on single-electron and singlet-triplet qubits.
result: The surface code outperforms the Bacon-Shor code in terms of lower logical error rates and higher threshold, but requires more physical qubits per logical qubit.
conclusion: The surface code is a better choice for spin qubit architectures despite higher resource overhead, while the Bacon-Shor code may be viable for near-term devices with limited qubits.

title: Efficient Local Discrimination Of Minimal Nonlocal Sets In Multipartite Systems Using Entanglement Resources

method: The authors design discrimination protocols that utilize shared entanglement to distinguish minimal nonlocal orthogonal product states, and compare resource costs with teleportation-based approaches.
result: The proposed protocols require fewer entanglement resources than teleportation for the same discrimination tasks.
conclusion: Entanglement-assisted local discrimination can be more resource-efficient, offering practical advantages for quantum communication tasks.

method: The authors use Clifford circuits on tree structures with random measurements and noise, analyzing entanglement entropy and mutual information to characterize phases.
result: They find distinct phases where quantum or classical information is retained or lost, with phase transitions depending on measurement rate and noise strength.
conclusion: Tree circuits provide a tractable model to study entanglement transitions under noise, offering insights into the robustness of quantum information in realistic settings.

title: Teleportation-based Squeezer For Bosonic Cluster States
authors: Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, And Petr Marek

conclusion: The universality simplifies the analysis of noisy quantum circuits and has implications for the feasibility of quantum advantage experiments, as anticoncentration is robust to noise in certain regimes.

title: Query And Depth Upper Bounds For Quantum Unitaries Via Grover Search
authors: Gregory Rosenthal
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2144 (2026).

We prove that any [MATH]-qubit unitary can be implemented (i) approximately in time [MATH] with query access to an appropriate classical oracle, and also (ii) exactly by a circuit of depth [MATH] with one- and two-qubit gates and [MATH] ancillae. The proofs involve similar reductions to Grover search. The proof of (ii) also involves a linear-depth construction of arbitrary quantum states using one- and two-qubit gates (in fact, this can be improved to constant depth with the addition of fanout and generalized Toffoli gates) which may be of independent interest. We also prove a matching [MATH] lower bound for (i) and (ii) for a certain class of implementations.

.
tldr: This paper proves upper and lower bounds on query complexity and circuit depth for implementing arbitrary quantum unitaries using Grover search.
motivation: Understanding the minimal resources (queries, depth) needed to implement arbitrary quantum operations is fundamental to quantum computing theory.
method: The proofs reduce unitary implementation to Grover search, and use a linear-depth construction for arbitrary quantum states with one- and two-qubit gates.

conclusion: The results provide tight complexity bounds for generic unitary synthesis, highlighting the power of Grover search in this context.

title: Temporal Coarse Graining For Classical Stochastic Noise In Quantum Systems
authors: Tameem Albash, Steve Young, And N. Tobias Jacobson
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2137 (2026).

Simulations of quantum systems with Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise can be challenging when the noise exhibits temporal correlations over a multitude of time scales, such as for [MATH] noise in solid-state quantum information processors. Here we present an approach for simulating Hamiltonian classical stochastic noise that performs temporal coarse-graining by effectively integrating out the high-frequency components of the noise. We focus on the case where the stochastic noise can be expressed as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes. Temporal coarse-graining is then achieved by conditioning the stochastic process on a coarse realization of the noise, expressing the conditioned stochastic process in terms of a sum of smooth, deterministic functions and bridge processes with boundaries fixed at zero, and performing the ensemble average over the bridge processes. For Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, the deterministic components capture all dependence on the coarse realization, and the stochastic bridge processes are not only independent but taken from the same distribution with correlators that can be expressed analytically, allowing the associated noise propagators to be precomputed once for all simulations. This combination of noise trajectories on a coarse time grid and ensemble averaging over bridge processes has practical advantages, such as a simple concatenation rule, that we highlight with numerical examples.

.
tldr: A temporal coarse-graining method for simulating classical stochastic noise in quantum systems, focusing on 1/f noise in solid-state qubits.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems with temporally correlated classical noise (e.g., 1/f noise) is computationally challenging due to multiple time scales.
method: The noise is modeled as a sum of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes; temporal coarse-graining is achieved by conditioning on a coarse realization and analytically averaging over bridge processes.
result: The method yields deterministic components that capture coarse noise and independent bridge processes with known correlators, enabling precomputation of noise propagators.
conclusion: The approach provides practical advantages like a simple concatenation rule and is demonstrated with numerical examples.

title: Simulating Magic State Cultivation With Few Clifford Terms

Compared to a magic cat state stabiliser decomposition of all [MATH] non-Clifford spiders ([MATH] terms required), this is more than [MATH] times reduction in the number of terms. Our stabiliser decomposition has the advantage of representing the final non-Clifford state (in light of circuit errors) as a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams. This will be useful in simulating the escape stage of magic state cultivation, where one needs to port the resultant state of cultivation into a larger Clifford circuit with many more qubits. Still, it's necessary to only track [MATH] Clifford terms. Our result sheds light on the simulability of operationally relevant, high [MATH]-count quantum circuits with some internal structure. Finally, we provide numerical results for full non-Clifford stabiliser rank simulation based on [MATH] along with optimisations using our cutting decompositions. Nearly [MATH] shots per second can be obtained on a laptop for the smaller [MATH] circuits at uniform circuit level noise [MATH], making it only [MATH][MATH] times slower than its (circuit-unspecific and un-optimised) fully Clifford proxy simulation via [MATH] using [MATH] gates.

.
tldr: This paper presents methods to simulate magic state cultivation circuits using a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams, achieving a significant reduction in the number of terms compared to standard stabiliser decompositions.
motivation: Magic state cultivation is a key technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating the non-Clifford components is computationally expensive. The authors aim to reduce the simulation cost by exploiting the structure of cultivation circuits.
method: The authors develop stabiliser decompositions that represent the non-Clifford state as a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams, using cutting techniques to reduce the number of terms. They also provide numerical simulations using non-Clifford stabiliser rank methods.
result: The proposed method reduces the number of terms by more than a factor of 10 compared to a naive decomposition, enabling simulation of small circuits at uniform noise levels with nearly 1000 shots per second on a laptop.

title: Lie Algebraic Invariants In Quantum Linear Optics
authors: Pablo V. Parellada, Vicent Gimeno I Garcia, Julio José Moyano-Fernández, And Juan Carlos Garcia-Escartin
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2132 (2026).

Quantum linear optics without post-selection is not powerful enough to produce any quantum state from a given input state. This limits its utility since some applications require entangled resources that are difficult to prepare. Thus, a deeper understanding of linear optical state preparation is needed. In this work, we give a recipe to derive conserved quantities in the evolution of arbitrary states along any possible passive linear interferometer. One example of such an invariant is the spectrum of a density matrix mapped onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians. These invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation: if the input and output states have different invariants, it is impossible to design a passive linear interferometer that evolves one into the other. Moreover, we provide a lower bound to the distance between an output and target state based on the distance between their invariants. This gives a necessary condition for approximate or heralded state preparations. Therefore, the invariants allow us to narrow the search when trying to prepare useful entangled states, like NOON states, from easy-to-prepare states, like Fock states. We conclude that future exact and approximate state preparation methods will need to consider the necessary conditions given by our invariants to weed out impossible linear optical evolutions.

.
tldr: Derives Lie algebraic invariants for passive linear optical networks that constrain state preparation.
motivation: Passive linear optics cannot produce arbitrary quantum states, limiting applications that require entangled resources; understanding these constraints is necessary.
method: Identifies conserved quantities under passive linear optical evolution by mapping density matrix spectra onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians.
result: Provides necessary conditions for exact state preparation and a lower bound on distance for approximate preparation based on invariant differences.
conclusion: Future state preparation methods must consider these invariants to exclude impossible evolutions, narrowing the search for useful entangled states like NOON states.

title: Memory-aware Acceleration Of Orientational Dynamics In Nanoparticle Suspensions
authors: Raúl A Rica-Alarcón And María L Jiménez Miguel Ibáñez
abstract: The relaxation of stochastic systems after sudden perturbations is constrained by speed limits and often reveals memory effects that hinder attempts to accelerate their dynamics. Here we demonstrate Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in the electro-orientation of non-spherical nanoparticles and show how this memory effect limits simple acceleration protocols. Experimentally, the orientational dynamics is monitored optically through field-induced birefringence, which is proportional to the nematic order parameter. When an AC electric field is first set to an extreme value until the birefringence reaches its target and is then switched to the target field (matched two-step protocol), the relaxation exhibits a characteristic Kovacs shoulder. We interpret this behavior within a theoretical framework based on the Smoluchowski equation for the orientational probability density. In the high-frequency AC regime, orientational relaxation is governed by induced dipoles, and the observed memory effect originates from polydispersity, which generates a spectrum of rotational diffusion coefficients and hence multiscale relaxation. Building on this insight, we design protocols that mitigate the detrimental effect of memory by sequentially suppressing the slowest active relaxation mode. Experiments on nanoparticle suspensions with different properties confirm these mechanisms, and we demonstrate substantial reductions in relaxation time compared with single quenches and matched two-step protocols with NaMt suspensions. More broadly, these results illustrate how memory effects emerge when many degrees of freedom are steered with a single control parameter and provide an experimentally accessible strategy for controlling multiscale stochastic dynamics.
tldr: This paper demonstrates Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation in nanoparticle suspensions and designs protocols to accelerate relaxation by mitigating memory effects.
motivation: Understanding and accelerating relaxation in stochastic systems is important for controlling multiscale dynamics, but memory effects often hinder simple acceleration protocols.
method: The authors use optical birefringence to monitor orientational dynamics of nanoparticles under AC electric fields, and interpret the results using the Smoluchowski equation. They design multi-step protocols that sequentially suppress slow relaxation modes.
result: They observe Kovacs-type nonmonotonic relaxation due to polydispersity, and show that their designed protocols substantially reduce relaxation time compared to standard protocols.
conclusion: Memory effects in polydisperse systems can be mitigated by sequentially suppressing slow modes, providing a strategy for accelerating relaxation in complex systems.

tldr: This paper studies the emergence of quantum state designs and confinement in monitored random tensor networks, linking measurement-induced phase transitions to entanglement dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the structure of quantum states generated by random unitary circuits with measurements is crucial for quantum information processing and many-body physics.
method: The authors analyze the spectral properties of the density matrix in a tensor network model with projective measurements, using replica methods and mapping to a classical statistical mechanics model.
result: They show that the system exhibits a confinement mechanism that leads to the formation of approximate quantum state designs in the volume-law phase, with a transition to a confined phase at high measurement rates.
conclusion: The work provides a new perspective on measurement-induced phase transitions and the emergence of randomness in quantum circuits, with implications for quantum error correction and thermalization.

method: Exact numerical simulations of an interacting fermionic chain with nonreciprocal gain and loss.
result: The interplay of nonreciprocity and interactions leads to a dissipative phase transition with distinct entanglement properties.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal couplings can fundamentally alter quantum critical behavior and entanglement in open quantum systems.

conclusion: The work provides insights into the spectral statistics of strongly repulsive quantum systems, connecting to quantum chaos and thermalization.

method: The authors study a bond-staggered Heisenberg chain with spectral reflection symmetry and SU(2) symmetry, employing character theory to count exponentially many zero-energy states and constructing exact low-entangled few-magnon eigenstates.
result: They find exponentially many zero-energy states and construct exact low-entangled few-magnon eigenstates that are stable under many perturbations.
conclusion: The existence of stable infinite-temperature eigenstates in a nonintegrable model challenges typical thermalization expectations and may have implications for quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Machine Learning Decoding Of Circuit-Level Noise For Bivariate Bicycle Codes

abstract:
