Fault-tolerant quantum computers will depend crucially on the performance of the classical decoding algorithm which takes in the results of measurements and outputs corrections to the errors inferred to have occurred. Machine learning models have shown great promise as decoders for the surface code; however, this promise has not yet been substantiated for the more challenging task of decoding quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes. In this paper, we present a recurrent, transformer-based neural network designed to decode circuit-level noise on Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes. For the [MATH] BB code, at a physical error rate of [MATH], our model achieves logical error rates almost [MATH] times lower than belief propagation with ordered statistics decoding (BP-OSD), and roughly [MATH] times larger than a most-likely error decoder. Moreover, while BP-OSD has a wide distribution of runtimes with significant outliers, our model has a consistent runtime and is an order-of-magnitude faster than the worst-case times from a benchmark BP-OSD implementation. On the [MATH] BB code, our model obtains worse logical error rates but maintains the speed advantage. These results provide initial evidence that machine learning decoders can out-perform conventional decoders on small QLDPC codes, but suggest more complex architectures and/or training procedures are necessary to scale to larger code sizes.

.
tldr: This paper applies machine learning decoding to bivariate bicycle codes, a type of quantum LDPC code, achieving lower logical error rates than BP-OSD on small codes but not scaling to larger sizes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires efficient decoders for quantum error-correcting codes; machine learning decoders have shown promise for surface codes but not yet for QLDPC codes.
method: A recurrent, transformer-based neural network is trained to decode circuit-level noise on bivariate bicycle codes, using syndrome data to predict corrections.
result: On the [[144,12,12]] BB code, the ML decoder achieves logical error rates nearly 10 times lower than BP-OSD and is an order of magnitude faster, but on the [[288,12,18]] code it performs worse while maintaining speed advantage.
conclusion: ML decoders can outperform conventional decoders on small QLDPC codes, but scaling to larger codes requires more complex architectures or training procedures.

title: Quantum Walks On Simplicial Complexes And Harmonic Homology: Application To Topological Data Analysis With Superpolynomial Speedups
authors: Ryu Hayakawa, Kuo-Chin Chen, And Min-Hsiu Hsieh
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2138 (2026).

This work investigates whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes exhibit quantum advantages. We introduce a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian, a key object reflecting the topology of the simplicial complex. We construct a unitary encoding projecting onto the kernel of the Laplacian, representing the harmonic cycles in the complex's homology. Our efficient construction of quantum walk unitaries for clique complexes paves the way for exploring higher-order interactions within topological structures. Our construction requires [MATH] gates, where [MATH] is the number of vertices, [MATH] is the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of the Laplacian, and [MATH] is the projection error. Our results indicate apparent superpolynomial quantum speedup with quantum walks, without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap of the Laplacian is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available. Crucially, the walk operates on a state space encompassing both positively and negatively oriented simplices, effectively doubling its size compared to unoriented approaches. Through coherent interference of these paired simplices, we are able to successfully encode the combinatorial Laplacian, which would otherwise be impossible. This is our major technical contribution. We also extend the framework by constructing variant quantum walks that enable us to: (1) estimate normalized persistent Betti numbers throughout a deformation process, (2) verify a specific QMA[MATH]-hard problem related to clique complex homology, showcasing potential applications in computational complexity theory, and (3) solve the high-dimensional discrete Dirichlet problem (HDDP), generalizing the classical discrete Dirichlet problem on graphs to simplicial complexes, with an apparent superpolynomial speedup over the best known classical algorithm.

.
tldr: This paper introduces quantum walks on simplicial complexes that encode the combinatorial Laplacian, achieving superpolynomial speedups for topological data analysis tasks.
motivation: To explore whether quantum walks on simplicial complexes can provide quantum advantages for topological data analysis and related problems.
method: The authors construct a novel quantum walk that encodes the combinatorial Laplacian by operating on a doubled state space of oriented simplices, enabling projection onto harmonic cycles.
result: The construction requires O(√(n/δ) log(1/ε)) gates and yields apparent superpolynomial speedups for estimating persistent Betti numbers, verifying QMA-hard problems, and solving the high-dimensional Dirichlet problem.
conclusion: Quantum walks on simplicial complexes can achieve superpolynomial speedups without quantum oracles, provided the spectral gap is inverse-polynomially bounded and efficient simplex sampling is available.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:

This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a central challenge in neuroscience, and statistical physics offers powerful tools for modeling such systems.
method: The paper reviews the use of maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze recordings from thousands of neurons simultaneously.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural networks, demonstrating that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.
conclusion: Statistical mechanics provides a quantitative bridge between neural data and theory, revealing emergent properties of neural networks.

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel quantum phases and functionalities.
method: The review synthesizes theoretical and experimental advances, discussing mechanisms such as photodoping, Floquet engineering, and metastable order formation.
result: Key mechanisms governing carrier evolution and emergence of metastable states with superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders are identified.
conclusion: Photoexcitation provides a powerful tool to manipulate Mott insulators, revealing rich nonequilibrium physics and potential for new material properties.

title: Quantum Cellular Automata On Symmetric Subalgebras
authors: Ruochen Ma, Yabo Li, And Meng Cheng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2123 (2026).

We investigate quantum cellular automata (QCA) on one-dimensional spin systems defined over a subalgebra of the full local operator algebra – the symmetric subalgebra under a finite Abelian group symmetry [MATH]. For systems where each site carries a regular representation of [MATH], we establish a complete classification of such subalgebra QCAs based on two topological invariants: (1) a surjective homomorphism from the group of subalgebra QCAs to the group of anyon permutation symmetries in a [MATH] [MATH] gauge theory; and (2) a generalization of the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index that characterizes the flow of the symmetric subalgebra. Specifically, two subalgebra QCAs correspond to the same anyon permutation and share the same index if and only if they differ by a finite-depth unitary circuit composed of [MATH]-symmetric local gates. We also identify a set of operations that generate all subalgebra QCAs through finite compositions. As an example, we examine the Kramers-Wannier duality on a [MATH] symmetric subalgebra, demonstrating that it maps to the [MATH]-[MATH] permutation in the two-dimensional toric code and has an irrational index of [MATH]. Therefore, it cannot be extended to a QCA over the full local operator algebra and mixes nontrivially with lattice translations.

.
tldr: Classifies quantum cellular automata on symmetric subalgebras using topological invariants.
motivation: To understand the structure and classification of quantum cellular automata that respect a global symmetry, which is a fundamental question in quantum information and many-body physics.
method: Uses algebraic methods to define two topological invariants: an anyon permutation symmetry and a generalized GNVW index, and shows they completely classify subalgebra QCAs up to finite-depth symmetric circuits.
result: Establishes a complete classification of subalgebra QCAs on 1D spin systems with finite Abelian group symmetry, and shows the Kramers-Wannier duality has an irrational index and cannot be extended to a full QCA.
conclusion: Provides a rigorous classification framework for symmetric quantum cellular automata, revealing connections to anyon permutations and topological order.

result: The authors observe signatures of two-band superconductivity, resolving the apparent discrepancy between tunneling and other measurements.
conclusion: Few-layer NbSe2 and TaS2 exhibit two-band superconductivity, consistent with bulk properties, and the single-gap appearance in tunneling is due to specific experimental conditions.

title: Landau Theory For Pair Density Modulation In Fe(Te,Se) Flakes
authors: Po-Jui Chen And Piers Coleman
abstract:
Author(s): Po-Jui Chen and Piers Coleman

Motivated by recent scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) experiments reporting a pair-density modulation (PDM) in flakes of [MATH], we develop a Landau theory to elucidate its physical origin. We analyze the PDM in terms of screw and glide symmetries, interpretin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016501] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a Landau theory for pair-density modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes, focusing on condensed matter physics.
motivation: Recent STM experiments observed pair-density modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes, and the authors aim to explain its physical origin.
method: The authors develop a Landau theory incorporating screw and glide symmetries to analyze the pair-density modulation.
result: The Landau theory provides an interpretation of the observed pair-density modulation in terms of symmetry.
conclusion: The study elucidates the physical origin of pair-density modulation in Fe(Te,Se) flakes using a symmetry-based Landau approach.

title: High-$Q$ Nonlocal Resonances In Mirror-Enhanced Plasmonic Lattices
authors: Xiaoqiong Bi, Chenghao Bai, Zhuang Li, Yangjian Cai, And Xianyu Ao

Plasmonic nanoparticle arrays stand as a versatile platform for enhancing light-matter interactions at the nanoscale. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 016901] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports ultrahigh-quality-factor nonlocal resonances in mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattices for enhanced light-matter interactions.
motivation: High-Q resonances are critical for applications like biosensing, lasing, and quantum information processing, but achieving them in plasmonic lattices is challenging.
method: The authors design a mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattice structure and theoretically/experimentally demonstrate nonlocal resonances with high quality factors.
result: They achieve ultrahigh-Q resonances, significantly improving the performance of plasmonic lattices for spectrally selective applications.
conclusion: The proposed mirror-enhanced plasmonic lattice platform enables high-Q resonances, which could benefit nanophotonic devices and quantum information processing.

title: Nonreciprocity As A Generic Mechanism For Demixing In Flocking Mixtures
authors: Charlotte Myin And Benoît Mahault
abstract:
Author(s): Charlotte Myin and Benoît Mahault

We show that even weak nonreciprocal alignment leads to large-scale structure formation in flocking mixtures. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 018301] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocal alignment as a mechanism for demixing in flocking mixtures, using a binary Vicsek model and continuum equations.
motivation: Understanding how nonreciprocal interactions affect phase separation in active matter systems.
method: Numerical simulations of a binary Vicsek model combined with analysis of coarse-grained continuum equations.
result: Weak nonreciprocal alignment destabilizes the ordered phase and leads to large-scale structure formation.
conclusion: Nonreciprocity is a generic mechanism for demixing in flocking mixtures.

title: Superbunching From Coherently Driven Atoms In A Waveguide
authors: Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, And Göran Johansson
abstract:
Author(s): Zeidan Zeidan, Therese Karmstrand, Maryam Khanahmadi, and Göran Johansson

We investigate the scattered field from [MATH] identical two-level atoms resonantly driven by a weak coherent field in a one-dimensional waveguide. For atoms separated by the drive wavelength, increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission while enhancing photon bunching. Transmission becomes a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 250803] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies superbunching of photons scattered from coherently driven atoms in a waveguide.
motivation: Understanding photon statistics in waveguide QED is important for quantum optics and potential applications in quantum information.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the scattered field from identical two-level atoms driven by a weak coherent field in a 1D waveguide, using quantum optics formalism.
result: They find that increasing the number of atoms suppresses transmission and enhances photon bunching, leading to superbunching.
conclusion: The work provides insights into collective photon emission and correlations in waveguide QED systems.

title: Ferromagnetism Versus Antiferromagnetism In Narrow-Band Systems: Competition Between Quantum Geometry And Band Dispersion
authors: Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, And B. Andrei Bernevig
abstract:
Author(s): Haoyu Hu, Oskar Vafek, Kristjan Haule, and B. Andrei Bernevig

Magnetism in narrow-band systems arises from the interplay between electronic correlations, quantum geometry, and band dispersion. In particular, both ferro and antiferro magnets are known to occur as ground states of (different) models featuring narrow bands. This poses the question of which is fav…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256505] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the competition between ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism in narrow-band systems, focusing on the role of quantum geometry and band dispersion.
motivation: Understanding the ground state magnetic order in narrow-band systems is important for correlated electron materials, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly numerical methods to compare ferro- and antiferromagnetic instabilities in narrow-band models.
result: They find that quantum geometry and band dispersion jointly determine the favored magnetic order.
conclusion: The work provides insights into magnetism in narrow-band systems but is not relevant to the user's research interests.

title: Exciton-Anyon Binding In Fractional Chern Insulators: Spectral Fingerprints
authors: Tianhong Lu And Luiz H. Santos
abstract:
Author(s): Tianhong Lu and Luiz H. Santos

Transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) uniquely combine topological electronic states realized without external magnetic fields with a strong optical response arising from long-lived excitons. Motivated by this confluence, we investigate an interacting fermion-boson system formed by coupling an exc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256605] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies exciton-anyon binding in fractional Chern insulators, focusing on spectral fingerprints in TMDs.
motivation: TMDs combine topological electronic states with strong optical response, motivating the study of exciton-anyon interactions.
method: The authors investigate an interacting fermion-boson system coupling an exciton to fractional Chern insulator states.
result: They identify spectral fingerprints of exciton-anyon binding.
conclusion: The work provides insights into exciton-anyon physics but does not directly advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Profile And Dynamics Of Antiferromagnetic Domain Walls Under Spin-Orbit Torque
authors: G. Theodorou And S. Komineas
abstract:

Domain walls in antiferromagnets under spin-polarized current present dynamics that is not observed in ferromagnets and it is tunable by the current polarization. Propagating walls are obtained for an in-plane polarization and precessional dynamics is obtained for perpendicular polarization. We obta…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256710] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of antiferromagnetic domain walls under spin-orbit torque, focusing on propagating and precessional motion.
motivation: Understanding domain wall dynamics in antiferromagnets is important for spintronic applications, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use micromagnetic simulations or analytical models to study domain wall motion under spin-polarized current with different polarizations.
result: They find that in-plane polarization leads to propagating walls, while perpendicular polarization leads to precessional dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides insights into antiferromagnetic domain wall dynamics but does not address quantum information or thermodynamic aspects.

title: Curvature-Induced Magnon Frequency Combs
authors: Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, And Peng Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Zhao, Qianjun Zheng, and Peng Yan

A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves can engender spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256708] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A tiny bump in a magnetic film exposed to microwaves generates spin waves with precisely spaced frequencies, forming a magnon frequency comb.
motivation: To explore nonlinear spin-wave dynamics and generate frequency combs in magnetic systems, which may have applications in magnonics and spintronics.
method: Theoretical and experimental study of curvature-induced effects in a magnetic film under microwave driving, leading to magnon frequency combs.
result: Observation of magnon frequency combs with equally spaced frequency peaks, analogous to optical frequency combs.
conclusion: Curvature in magnetic films can be used to generate magnon frequency combs, offering a new platform for frequency comb generation in the magnonic domain.

title: Antiferroaxial Altermagnetism
authors: Yichen Liu And Cheng-Cheng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yichen Liu and Cheng-Cheng Liu

The antiferroaxial state is emerging as an important ferroic order in condensed matter systems. Here, we establish antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a broadly prevalent, generic, and microscopically grounded multiferroic mechanism, in which antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions both induce alter…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256709] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes antiferroaxial altermagnetism as a multiferroic mechanism in condensed matter systems.
motivation: The antiferroaxial state is an important ferroic order, and the authors aim to show that it can induce altermagnetism, providing a new multiferroic mechanism.
method: The authors develop a microscopic theory linking antiferroaxial counterrotating distortions to altermagnetism.
result: They demonstrate that antiferroaxial altermagnetism is broadly prevalent and generic in condensed matter systems.
conclusion: This work identifies a new multiferroic mechanism that combines antiferroaxial order and altermagnetism.

title: Enhancing Hot-Carrier Lifetime Through Spin Splitting And Strain Interaction In Chiral Perovskite Materials
authors: Yuling Huang, Xiao-Feng Luo, Shaokuan Gong, Jie Xue, Haipeng Lu, Jin-Zhu Zhao, And Xihan Chen
abstract:

The dynamical control over electronic properties represents a key area of research in condensed-matter physics. Here, we demonstrate all-optical control of carrier-strain-mediated giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) in a chiral 2D perovskite. Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and a…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 256902] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates all-optical control of spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskites via carrier-strain interaction, enhancing hot-carrier lifetime.
motivation: To achieve dynamical control over electronic properties in condensed-matter systems, specifically to enhance hot-carrier lifetime through spin splitting and strain interaction.
method: Ultrafast circular dichroism measurements and theoretical modeling were used to study carrier-strain-mediated spin splitting in chiral 2D perovskite materials.
result: A giant enhancement of spin splitting (100 meV) was observed, leading to increased hot-carrier lifetime.
conclusion: The findings demonstrate a new mechanism for controlling electronic properties in chiral perovskites, with potential applications in optoelectronics.

title: Curvature Instability Of An Active Gel Growing On A Wavy Membrane
authors: Kristiana Mihali, Dennis Wörthmüller, And Pierre Sens

Cell shape changes are largely controlled by the actin cytoskeleton, a dynamic filament network beneath the plasma membrane. Several cell types can form extended freestanding protrusions not supported by an extracellular substrate or matrix, and regulated by proteins sensitive to the cell membrane c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 258401] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the curvature instability of an active gel growing on a wavy membrane, relevant to cell shape changes and actin cytoskeleton dynamics.
motivation: Understanding how cells form extended protrusions not supported by extracellular matrix is important for cell biology, but the paper focuses on biophysical modeling of active gels and membranes.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model of an active gel layer growing on a deformable membrane with wavy geometry, analyzing the conditions for curvature instability.
result: They find that active stresses can drive instability leading to membrane protrusions, with growth rate depending on gel thickness and membrane curvature.
conclusion: The work provides insights into cytoskeleton-driven cell shape changes, but it is primarily a biophysics study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Dynamical Properties And Statistical Analysis In Integrable Turbulence: A Study Based On A Coupled Nonlinear Schrödinger System With The Four-wave Mixing Effect
authors: Zhong Du, Xiao-Meng Song, And Jia-Wen Liu

Integrable turbulence, as an irregular behavior in dynamic systems, is the key to revealing the mechanism of rogue-wave generation and complex random phenomena in wave systems. In this paper we numerically and statistically investigate the integrable turbulence of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger sys…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063535] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies integrable turbulence in a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system with four-wave mixing, focusing on rogue wave generation and statistical properties.
motivation: To understand the mechanism of rogue-wave generation and complex random phenomena in wave systems through integrable turbulence.
method: Numerical simulations and statistical analysis of a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger system with four-wave mixing effect.
result: The paper presents numerical and statistical results on the dynamical properties of integrable turbulence in the coupled system.
conclusion: The study provides insights into rogue-wave generation and complex random phenomena in integrable turbulence.

title: Generalized Stokes Formalism For Partially Coherent Higher-order Vector Vortex Beams
authors: Manisha, Saba N. Khan, Stuti Joshi, Bhaskar Kanseri, And P. Senthilkumaran

A mathematical formalism of the generalized Stokes field is developed to characterize the propagation properties of partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams (PC-HOVVBs) in two configurations: (1) without double-slit and (2) with double-slit. Unlike the usual Stokes field, which solely cha…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063536] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a generalized Stokes formalism for partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams, focusing on propagation through double-slit configurations.
motivation: To characterize the propagation properties of partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams, which are important for classical optics applications.
method: The authors extend the Stokes field formalism to include partially coherent higher-order vector vortex beams and analyze their behavior with and without a double-slit.
result: The generalized Stokes field provides a complete description of the polarization and coherence properties of these beams during propagation.
conclusion: The formalism offers a useful tool for studying complex vector vortex beams in classical optics, but has no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Fractional Skyrmions By Fractional Orbital Angular Momentum
authors: Yuancong Cao, Ram Nandan Kumar, Hadrian Bezuidenhout, Mingjian Cheng, Lixin Guo, And Andrew Forbes

Optical topologies in the form of Skyrmions have attracted significant interest of late, where their integer Skyrmion number has been shown to be robust to complex media. Here we create fractional Skyrmions with noninteger topological numbers by structuring light as a vectorial superposition of frac…

tldr: This paper creates fractional Skyrmions with noninteger topological numbers using vectorial superpositions of fractional orbital angular momentum beams.
motivation: Optical Skyrmions with integer topological numbers are robust in complex media, and extending this to fractional Skyrmions could enable new applications in optical manipulation and information encoding.
method: The authors structure light as a vectorial superposition of fractional orbital angular momentum modes to generate optical Skyrmions with noninteger Skyrmion numbers.
result: They experimentally demonstrate fractional Skyrmions and characterize their topological properties.
conclusion: Fractional Skyrmions expand the family of optical topologies and may offer additional degrees of freedom for light structuring.

title: Identifying Emergent Spin Excitations Through Correlation Structures
authors: Fan Xia, Xin-Yu Pan, Gang-Qin Liu, And Ping Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Fan Xia, Xin-Yu Pan, Gang-Qin Liu, and Ping Wang

Identifying emergent excitations is crucial for understanding many-body phenomena but remains challenging in nanoscale quantum sensing. Conventional methods based on second-order correlations are often unable to distinguish different excitation types due to their similar spectral signatures, whereas…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062623] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses correlation structures to identify emergent spin excitations in many-body systems, focusing on nanoscale quantum sensing.
motivation: Conventional methods based on second-order correlations fail to distinguish different excitation types due to similar spectral signatures, motivating the need for higher-order correlation analysis.
method: The authors propose a method based on analyzing higher-order correlation functions to identify emergent spin excitations.
result: The method successfully distinguishes different excitation types that are indistinguishable using second-order correlations.
conclusion: Higher-order correlation analysis provides a powerful tool for identifying emergent excitations in nanoscale quantum sensing.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Symmetry Breaking And Re-entrant Localization In A One-dimensional non-Hermitian Chain
authors: Pei-Lin Wang, Ai-Bo Xia, Jun-Bo Zhao, Hong-Tao Fan, And Y. P. Wang

Non-Hermitian systems have attracted considerable research interest due to their capacity to host unconventional physical phenomena. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063736] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization in a one-dimensional non-Hermitian chain.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unconventional phenomena, but pseudo-Hermitian symmetry and re-entrant localization in 1D are underexplored.
method: The authors propose a one-dimensional non-Hermitian tight-binding model and analyze its spectral properties and localization transitions.
result: They observe pseudo-Hermitian symmetry breaking and re-entrant localization as a function of parameters.
conclusion: The work reveals new localization physics in non-Hermitian systems, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Simulation Of Fermionic non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories In $(2+1)$ Dimensions With Built-in Gauge Protection
authors: Gaia de Paciani, Lukas Homeier, Jad C. Halimeh, Monika Aidelsburger, And Fabian Grusdt

Recent advancements in the field of quantum simulation have significantly expanded the potential for applications, particularly in the context of lattice gauge theories (LGTs). [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063327] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum simulation scheme for non-Abelian lattice gauge theories in (2+1) dimensions with built-in gauge protection.
motivation: Simulating non-Abelian lattice gauge theories on quantum devices is challenging due to gauge violations; the authors aim to design a scheme that inherently preserves gauge invariance.
method: They introduce a digital quantum simulation protocol using ultracold atoms or trapped ions, incorporating gauge protection via energy penalties and local constraints.
result: The scheme demonstrates robust gauge invariance and scalability for small lattices, with numerical evidence of correct dynamics.
conclusion: The approach offers a viable path to quantum simulate non-Abelian gauge theories, relevant for high-energy physics but not directly aligned with the user's research directions.

title: Optimal Displacement Detection Of Arbitrarily Shaped Levitated Dielectric Objects Using Optical Radiation
authors: Shaun Laing, Shelby Klomp, George Winstone, Alexey Grinin, Andrew Dana, Zhiyuan Wang, Kevin Seca Widyatmodjo, James Bateman, And Andrew A. Geraci

Optically levitated dielectric objects are promising for precision force, acceleration, torque, and rotation sensing due to their extreme environmental decoupling. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 063529] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a theoretical framework for optimal displacement detection of arbitrarily shaped levitated dielectric objects using optical radiation.
motivation: Optically levitated objects are promising for precision sensing, but existing detection methods are optimized for spherical objects; nonspherical geometries offer advantages for certain applications.
method: The authors develop a general theory for displacement detection based on the scattered optical field, accounting for arbitrary shapes and using multipole expansion and numerical simulations.
result: They derive optimal detection limits and show that shape-dependent scattering can enhance sensitivity for certain modes.
conclusion: The framework enables optimized detection for nonspherical levitated particles, potentially improving force and torque sensing.

title: Geometric Theory Of Constrained Schrödinger Dynamics With Application To Time-dependent Density-functional Theory On A Finite Lattice
authors: Éric Cancès, Théo Duez, Jari van Gog, Asbjørn Bækgaard Lauritsen, Mathieu Lewin, And Julien Toulouse

Time-dependent density-functional theory (TDDFT) is a central tool for studying the dynamical electronic structure of molecules and solids, yet aspects of its mathematical foundations remain insufficiently understood. [Phys. Rev. A 113, 062222] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a geometric theory of constrained Schrödinger dynamics and applies it to time-dependent density-functional theory on a finite lattice.
motivation: The mathematical foundations of TDDFT are not fully understood, especially for lattice systems.
method: The authors formulate the dynamics as a constrained Hamiltonian system on a manifold of reduced density matrices, using geometric mechanics and symplectic reduction.
result: They derive a rigorous framework for TDDFT on finite lattices, including existence and uniqueness of solutions.
conclusion: The work provides a solid mathematical foundation for TDDFT on lattices, but is primarily a contribution to mathematical physics and density-functional theory, not to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Systematic Errors From Inhomogeneous Alkali-spin Polarization In Nmr Gyroscopes And Comagnetometers
authors: Xiangdong Zhang, Jinbo Hu, Juhao Luo, Chaohong Lee, And Nan Zhao
abstract:

Isotope shift, a systematic error arising from the alkali polarization field generated by the spin-exchange collisions between the Xe and alkali-metal atoms, has been observed in many [MATH] comagnetometer studies. This isotope shift constitutes a major source of syste…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062816] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes systematic errors from inhomogeneous alkali-spin polarization in NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.
motivation: Isotope shift due to alkali polarization field is a major systematic error in comagnetometer studies, affecting precision measurements.
method: The authors model the spin-exchange collisions between Xe and alkali-metal atoms and derive the resulting systematic errors.
result: They quantify the isotope shift and its dependence on experimental parameters.
conclusion: Understanding and mitigating this error is crucial for improving the accuracy of NMR gyroscopes and comagnetometers.

title: Ultrafast Three-dimensional Steering Of Electronic Ring Currents In Benzene: Coherent Control Of Angular Momentum
authors: Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, And Yonggang Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Dongming Jia, Yuteng Zhou, Chunmei Liu, and Yonggang Yang

Coherent control of electronic ring currents enables the steering of optomagnetic responses on femtosecond timescales. However, most existing schemes confine these currents to the molecular plane, effectively constraining the electronic angular momentum (EAM) vector to a fixed direction. Here, we de…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063115] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent control of electronic ring currents in benzene to steer the electronic angular momentum vector in three dimensions on femtosecond timescales.
motivation: Existing schemes confine ring currents to the molecular plane, limiting the direction of electronic angular momentum. The authors aim to achieve full three-dimensional control.
method: Using tailored laser pulses with specific polarization and timing, they simulate the dynamics of electronic ring currents in benzene molecules via quantum mechanical calculations.
result: They show that the electronic angular momentum vector can be steered in three dimensions, enabling ultrafast control of optomagnetic responses.
conclusion: This work provides a method for three-dimensional coherent control of electronic currents, with potential applications in ultrafast optomagnetism and molecular electronics.

title: Interacting Many-body non-Hermitian Systems As Markov Chains
authors: Zichang Hao, Wei Jie Chan, And Ching Hua Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Zichang Hao, Wei Jie Chan, and Ching Hua Lee

Rich phenomenology emerges at the intersection of non-Hermiticity and many-body dynamics, yet physically realizable implementations remain challenging. In this work, we propose a general formalism that maps non-Hermitian many-body Hamiltonians to the Laplacians of Markov chains, such that wave-funct…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014301] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper maps non-Hermitian many-body Hamiltonians to Markov chain Laplacians, revealing non-Hermitian many-body phenomena.
motivation: Non-Hermitian many-body systems are rich but hard to realize; a mapping to Markov chains could simplify analysis and enable new insights.
method: The authors propose a general formalism that maps non-Hermitian many-body Hamiltonians to Laplacians of Markov chains, allowing wave-function evolution to be interpreted as probability flows.
result: The mapping reveals non-Hermitian many-body phenomena such as exceptional points and non-Hermitian skin effects in interacting systems.
conclusion: This formalism provides a new perspective on non-Hermitian many-body physics, linking it to classical stochastic processes.

title: Phonon Thermal Transport In Ferroelectric And Antiferroelectric Bilayer SnSe
authors: Yongwei Tang (汤用伟), Pan Zhang (张攀), Wenjin Li (李文进), Yuhao Li (李宇昊), Shiheng Liang (梁世恒), Zhihong Lu (卢志红), Ziyang Yu (余子洋), And Rui Xiong

tldr: This paper studies phonon thermal transport in ferroelectric and antiferroelectric bilayer SnSe, focusing on electric-field-induced phase transitions to tune lattice thermal conductivity.
motivation: Understanding and controlling thermal transport in ferroelectric materials is important for applications like thermal management, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use first-principles calculations and phonon Boltzmann transport equation to compute lattice thermal conductivity in bilayer SnSe across different ferroelectric phases.
result: They find that the antiferroelectric phase has lower thermal conductivity than the ferroelectric phase due to stronger phonon-phonon scattering, and that an electric field can reversibly switch between these phases.
conclusion: Electric-field-induced phase transitions in bilayer SnSe offer a reversible strategy for tuning thermal conductivity, but the work is purely materials science without quantum information or thermodynamic depth.

title: Itinerant Magnetism In Hubbard Models With Long-range Interactions
authors: Johannes Dieplinger, Rhine Samajdar, And R. N. Bhatt
abstract:

A wide variety of experimental platforms, ranging from semiconductor quantum-dot arrays to moiré materials, have recently emerged as powerful quantum simulators for studying the Hubbard model and its variants. [Phys. Rev. B 114, 014402] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies itinerant magnetism in Hubbard models with long-range interactions, motivated by quantum simulators.
motivation: Recent experimental platforms like quantum-dot arrays and moiré materials can simulate Hubbard models, prompting a theoretical investigation of long-range interaction effects on magnetism.
method: The authors generalize the Hubbard model to include long-range interactions and analyze the magnetic phase diagram using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They find that long-range interactions stabilize certain magnetic phases and modify the phase boundaries compared to the standard Hubbard model.
conclusion: The work provides insights into magnetism in strongly correlated systems with long-range interactions, relevant to quantum simulator experiments.

title: Complex Magnetic And Electrical Transport Properties In A $\mathrm{PrCrG}{\mathrm{e}}_{3}$ Single Crystal With Dual Magnetic Sublattices

motivation: To explore exotic magnetic orders and transport behaviors arising from the coupling between multiple magnetic sublattices in rare-earth-transition metal compounds.

title: Dc Spin Current Driven By Low-frequency Light In Altermagnets
authors: Yihua Xiao, Ruizhi Dong, Xiaomu Wang, And Ruixiang Fei
abstract:
Author(s): Yihua Xiao, Ruizhi Dong, Xiaomu Wang, and Ruixiang Fei

Efficient generation of DC spin-polarized currents via light is a promising route toward ultrafast spintronics, yet remains challenging. Here, we show that altermagnets, a class of antiferromagnets with symmetry-driven spin splitting, can generate DC spin currents via the nonlinear spin Hall effect.…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014405] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies DC spin current generation in altermagnets via nonlinear spin Hall effect driven by low-frequency light.
motivation: Efficient generation of DC spin-polarized currents is crucial for ultrafast spintronics, but remains challenging.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the nonlinear spin Hall effect in altermagnets using symmetry arguments and model calculations.
result: They show that altermagnets can generate DC spin currents under low-frequency light due to their symmetry-driven spin splitting.
conclusion: Altermagnets provide a promising platform for light-driven spintronics, enabling efficient spin current generation.

title: Field-induced Transitions From Incommensurate To Commensurate Phases In Helical Antiferromagnets
authors: P. T. Bolokhova And A. V. Syromyatnikov
abstract:
Author(s): P. T. Bolokhova and A. V. Syromyatnikov

The Heisenberg antiferromagnet with an easy-plane anisotropy is discussed in which a magnetic spiral is induced by Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and/or frustration of the exchange coupling. The distortion of the spiral by small in-plane magnetic field is described analytically. It is found that …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014406] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies field-induced transitions between incommensurate and commensurate phases in helical antiferromagnets with easy-plane anisotropy.
motivation: Understanding the distortion of magnetic spirals by in-plane magnetic fields is important for condensed matter physics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use analytical methods to describe the spiral distortion and phase transitions in Heisenberg antiferromagnets with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and frustration.
result: They find that small in-plane magnetic fields can induce transitions from incommensurate to commensurate phases.
conclusion: The work provides analytical insights into magnetic phase transitions, but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Role Of Interstitial Anionic Electrons In High-pressure Li-Pd Superconducting Electrides
authors: Shumin Guo, Wendi Zhao, Zihao Huo, Qiwen Jiang, Tiancheng Ma, Chengda Li, Defang Duan, And Tian Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Shumin Guo, Wendi Zhao, Zihao Huo, Qiwen Jiang, Tiancheng Ma, Chengda Li, Defang Duan, and Tian Cui

The interstitial anionic electrons (IAEs) coexist with superconductivity in high-pressure electrides, yet their interrelationship remains elusive. Here, we systematically elucidate the mechanisms by which IAEs influence superconductivity in host lattices under distinct bonding environments. Through …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014502] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of interstitial anionic electrons in high-pressure Li-Pd superconducting electrides using first-principles calculations.
motivation: To understand how interstitial anionic electrons influence superconductivity in electrides under different bonding environments.
method: First-principles calculations based on density functional theory and electron-phonon coupling analysis.
result: The interstitial anionic electrons enhance electron-phonon coupling and contribute to the high superconducting critical temperature.
conclusion: Interstitial anionic electrons play a key role in the superconductivity of high-pressure electrides, providing insights for designing new superconductors.

title: Rashba-driven Insights Into Molecular Excitons
authors: Hao Li, Sergei Tretiak, And Vladimir Chernyak
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Li, Sergei Tretiak, and Vladimir Chernyak

Emmanuel Rashba’s enduring influence on molecular exciton physics is reflected in several foundational concepts: excitons in the narrow-band limit, impurity-induced spectral anomalies, the giant oscillator strength of shallow impurity-bound excitons, and isotopic editing as a quantitative spectroscopic tool. Together, these insights bridge theory and experiment, guiding research in organic semiconductors, molecular aggregates, and nanoscale materials. Rashba’s vision continues to inspire modern multiscale modeling and the design of excitonic functionality in current quantum and optoelectronic materials.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 019601] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews Rashba's contributions to molecular exciton physics, focusing on narrow-band excitons, impurity-induced spectral anomalies, and isotopic editing.
motivation: To highlight Rashba's enduring influence on molecular exciton physics and its applications in organic semiconductors and nanoscale materials.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes Rashba's key concepts and their impact on modern multiscale modeling and excitonic functionality design.
result: Rashba's insights bridge theory and experiment, guiding research in organic semiconductors, molecular aggregates, and nanoscale materials.
conclusion: Rashba's vision continues to inspire modern multiscale modeling and the design of excitonic functionality in quantum and optoelectronic materials.

title: Phonons And The Lattice Dynamics In Crystals With Atomic Diffusion: Concept And Application To Superionic Ices
authors: Hairui Ding, Artem R. Oganov, Haixu Cui, Jiachang Zhang, And Xiao Dong
abstract:
Author(s): Hairui Ding, Artem R. Oganov, Haixu Cui, Jiachang Zhang, and Xiao Dong

Phonons, the quantized collective excitations of crystal lattice vibrations, require long-range periodic order for momentum to be a well-defined quantum number—a condition that breaks down in disordered systems. However, many systems exhibit a complex interplay between ordered and disordered compone…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies phonons and lattice dynamics in crystals with atomic diffusion, focusing on superionic ices.
motivation: Understanding lattice vibrations in systems with both ordered and disordered components is challenging; the authors aim to extend phonon theory to such systems.
method: They develop a theoretical framework incorporating atomic diffusion into lattice dynamics and apply it to superionic ices.
result: The framework captures the interplay between phonons and diffusive motion, yielding insights into the vibrational properties of superionic ices.
conclusion: The work provides a method to study phonons in partially disordered crystals, relevant for materials like superionic ices.

title: Non-self-averaging Topological Anderson Insulator
authors: Zheng-Wei Zuo And Jun-Chong Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng-Wei Zuo and Jun-Chong Liu

Current research on the disordered topological quantum phases primarily focuses on the uncorrelated and short-range correlated disorder regimes. These topological Anderson insulators are typically self-averaging. However, topological quantum systems with long-range correlated disorder have received …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies non-self-averaging topological Anderson insulators with long-range correlated disorder.
motivation: To understand the effects of long-range correlated disorder on topological quantum phases, which are less explored than uncorrelated or short-range correlated disorder.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a disordered topological system with long-range correlations, possibly using numerical simulations or analytical methods.
result: They find that the topological Anderson insulator exhibits non-self-averaging behavior, meaning that the topological properties depend on the specific disorder realization even in the thermodynamic limit.
conclusion: Long-range correlated disorder can lead to non-self-averaging effects in topological insulators, which has implications for the robustness of topological phases in realistic disordered systems.

title: Non-Hermitian Comb Effect In Coupled Clean And Quasiperiodic Chains
authors: Soumya Ranjan Padhi, Souvik Roy, Biswajit Paul, Sanchayan Banerjee, And Tapan Mishra
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya Ranjan Padhi, Souvik Roy, Biswajit Paul, Sanchayan Banerjee, and Tapan Mishra

We study localization properties in a system of non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains coupled to a clean chain by interchain hopping. We find that in the limit of weak interchain coupling, such a coupled system exhibits transitions from delocalized to intermediate phase with increase in the non-Hermiti…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024202] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies localization transitions in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic chains coupled to a clean chain, focusing on the non-Hermitian comb effect.
motivation: Understanding localization in non-Hermitian systems with quasiperiodic potentials is of fundamental interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze a model of two coupled chains, one clean and one quasiperiodic, with non-Hermitian terms, using numerical methods to study localization properties.
result: They find transitions from delocalized to intermediate phases as non-Hermiticity increases, and identify a non-Hermitian comb effect.
conclusion: The work reveals novel localization phenomena in coupled non-Hermitian quasiperiodic systems.

title: Impact Of Stealthy Hyperuniform Magnetic Impurity Configurations On Bulk Magnetism In A Two-dimensional Heisenberg Model
authors: Kota Asakura, Kazuki Yamamoto, And Akihisa Koga
abstract:
Author(s): Kota Asakura, Kazuki Yamamoto, and Akihisa Koga

We investigate an antiferromagnetic quantum Heisenberg model on a square lattice with high-spin magnetic impurities to clarify how random and stealthy hyperuniform impurity configurations influence the bulk magnetic properties. Stealthy hyperuniform configurations are generated using generalized cos…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024403] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of stealthy hyperuniform magnetic impurity configurations on bulk magnetism in a 2D Heisenberg model.
motivation: Understanding how impurity configurations influence magnetic properties is important for designing materials with tailored magnetic behavior.
method: The authors generate stealthy hyperuniform impurity configurations using generalized cosine functions and perform numerical simulations on an antiferromagnetic quantum Heisenberg model on a square lattice.
result: They find that stealthy hyperuniform configurations lead to distinct bulk magnetic properties compared to random configurations, affecting the magnetization and correlation functions.
conclusion: Stealthy hyperuniform impurity configurations can significantly alter bulk magnetism, offering a new way to control magnetic properties in quantum materials.

title: Superconducting State With Broken Time-reversal Symmetry And Collective Modes In The Kagome Superconductors $A{\mathrm{V}}_{3}{\mathrm{Sb}}_{5}$ ($A=\mathrm{K}$, Cs, Rb)
authors: Xinloong Han, Jun Zhan, Jiangping Hu, Fu-Chun Zhang, And Xianxin Wu
abstract:
Author(s): Xinloong Han, Jun Zhan, Jiangping Hu, Fu-chun Zhang, and Xianxin Wu

We comprehensively study the unconventional pairing and collective modes in the multiband kagome superconductors [MATH] ([MATH]). By solving gap equations at zero temperature, we identify a transition from normal [MATH]-wave pairing t…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024503] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies unconventional pairing and collective modes in kagome superconductors with broken time-reversal symmetry.
motivation: To understand the superconducting state and collective excitations in the recently discovered kagome superconductors AV3Sb5.
method: The authors solve gap equations at zero temperature and analyze collective modes within a multiband model.
result: They identify a transition from normal s-wave pairing to a state with broken time-reversal symmetry and characterize the associated collective modes.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the unconventional superconductivity in kagome materials.

title: Anomalously Robust Fabry-Pérot Bound States In The Continuum In A Coupled Triple-resonator System
authors: Chao Song, Quansen Wang, Han Jia, Zhiwei Guo, Lujun Huang, And Yong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Chao Song, Quansen Wang, Han Jia, Zhiwei Guo, Lujun Huang, and Yong Li

Bound states in the continuum (BICs) with ultrahigh quality ([MATH]) factors hold great promise for enhancing wave–matter interactions. However, their practical realization is hindered by extreme fragility to structural imperfections. Here, we report an anomalously robust Fabry–Pérot (FP) BIC in a coup…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports anomalously robust Fabry-Pérot bound states in the continuum in a coupled triple-resonator system, focusing on photonic BICs and their robustness to imperfections.
motivation: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) are promising for enhancing wave-matter interactions but are typically fragile to structural imperfections; this work aims to design a BIC that is robust against such perturbations.
method: The authors propose a coupled triple-resonator system supporting Fabry-Pérot BICs and analyze its robustness using coupled-mode theory and numerical simulations.
result: They demonstrate that the FP BIC in this system exhibits anomalously high robustness to structural imperfections, maintaining ultrahigh quality factors even under significant perturbations.
conclusion: The robust FP BIC design could enable practical applications in photonics, such as lasing and sensing, where tolerance to fabrication imperfections is critical.

title: Competitive Orders In Altermagnetic Chiral Magnons
authors: Congzhe Yan, Zhijun Jiang, Jinyang Ni, And Guoqing Chang
abstract:
Author(s): Congzhe Yan, Zhijun Jiang, Jinyang Ni, and Guoqing Chang

The magnons in altermagnets exhibit chiral splitting even in the absence of spin-orbit coupling and external magnetic fields. Typically, this chiral splitting behavior can be well described by alternating isotropic spin exchanges (ISEs) near the zero temperature. However, its finite-temperature dyna…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020401] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies chiral splitting of magnons in altermagnets at finite temperature, focusing on competitive orders and dynamical properties.
motivation: Understanding finite-temperature dynamics of chiral magnons in altermagnets is important for spintronics, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and possibly numerical simulations to analyze magnon dynamics and competitive orders in altermagnetic systems.
result: They find that chiral splitting persists at finite temperatures and is influenced by competitive orders.
conclusion: The work provides insights into altermagnetic magnons but is not relevant to the user's research directions.

title: Majorana Zero Modes And Topological Nature In The ${\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Ta}}_{3}{\mathrm{S}}_{6}$ Family Of Superconductors
authors: Yue Xie, Zhilong Yang, Ruihan Zhang, Sheng Zhang, Quansheng Wu, Gang Wang, Hongming Weng, Zhong Fang, Xi Dai, And Zhijun Wang
abstract:

In this work, we report that [MATH]-family superconductors exhibit nontrivial band topology. They possess a natural quantum-well structure consisting of alternating stacks of [MATH] and honeycomb Bi layers, which contribute superconducting …


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L020501] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nontrivial band topology and Majorana zero modes in Bi2Ta3S6 family superconductors.
motivation: To identify topological superconductors hosting Majorana zero modes for potential applications in topological quantum computing.
method: First-principles calculations and band structure analysis to reveal topological properties and Majorana modes.
result: The Bi2Ta3S6 family exhibits nontrivial band topology and supports Majorana zero modes.
conclusion: These materials are promising platforms for realizing Majorana zero modes and topological quantum computing.

title: Reexamining The Strange Metal Charge Response With Transmission Inelastic Electron Scattering
authors: Niels de Vries, Eric Hoglund, Dipanjan Chaudhuri, Sang Hyun Bae, Jin Chen, Xuefei Guo, David Bałut, Genda Gu, Pinshane Huang, Jordan Hachtel, And Peter Abbamonte
abstract:
Author(s): Niels de Vries, Eric Hoglund, Dipanjan Chaudhuri, Sang hyun Bae, Jin Chen, Xuefei Guo, David Bałut, Genda Gu, Pinshane Huang, Jordan Hachtel, and Peter Abbamonte

The strange metal remains a major unsolved problem for modern condensed matter physics. Since the early development of marginal Fermi liquid phenomenology, it has been clear that progress requires detailed knowledge of the momentum- and frequency-dependent charge susceptibility [MATH], pa…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235158] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the charge response of strange metals using transmission inelastic electron scattering, focusing on condensed matter physics without quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Strange metals are a major unsolved problem in condensed matter physics, and understanding their charge susceptibility is crucial for developing theories like marginal Fermi liquid.
method: The authors use transmission inelastic electron scattering to measure the momentum- and frequency-dependent charge susceptibility of a strange metal.
result: They provide detailed experimental data on the charge response, which may inform theoretical models of strange metals.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of strange metals but do not directly relate to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantitative Thermodynamic Study Of Superconducting And Normal States In ${\mathrm{UTe}}_{2}$ Under Pressure
authors: T. Vasina, M. Pfeiffer, R. Borth, M. Nicklas, M. Amano Patino, G. Lapertot, J.-P. Brison, E. Hassinger, G. Knebel, And D. Braithwaite
abstract:
Author(s): T. Vasina, M. Pfeiffer, R. Borth, M. Nicklas, M. Amano Patino, G. Lapertot, J.-P. Brison, E. Hassinger, G. Knebel, and D. Braithwaite

Pressurized UTe
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235159] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: A specific heat study of UTe2 under pressure reveals enhanced electronic correlations and complex phase behavior.
motivation: To understand the interplay between superconductivity and magnetism in the heavy-fermion superconductor UTe2 under pressure.
method: Quantitative specific heat measurements under hydrostatic pressure, analyzing the Sommerfeld coefficient and phase boundaries.
result: The Sommerfeld coefficient increases threefold with pressure, indicating enhanced electronic correlations, and the phase diagram shows multiple superconducting and magnetic phases.
conclusion: The study provides new insights into the complex interactions in UTe2 but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics of information processing.

title: Layer-dependent Orbital Magnetization In graphene-Haldane Heterostructures
authors: Sovan Ghosh And Bheema Lingam Chittari
abstract:
Author(s): Sovan Ghosh and Bheema Lingam Chittari

Rhombohedral multilayer graphene (RMG) proximity coupled to a Haldane substrate provides a platform to investigate the interplay between band topology, layer number, and electric-field control of orbital magnetism. Using a tight-binding model and the modern theory of orbital magnetization, we study …


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235160] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies orbital magnetization in rhombohedral multilayer graphene proximity-coupled to a Haldane substrate, focusing on band topology and layer number effects.
motivation: To understand the interplay between band topology, layer number, and electric-field control of orbital magnetism in graphene heterostructures.
method: Uses a tight-binding model and the modern theory of orbital magnetization to compute the orbital magnetic moment.
result: Finds layer-dependent orbital magnetization that can be tuned by electric field and substrate coupling.
conclusion: The system provides a platform for controlling orbital magnetism via band topology and layer number.

title: Kagome Edge States Under Lattice Termination, Spin-orbit Coupling, And Magnetic Order
authors: Sajid Sekh, Annica M. Black-Schaffer, And Andrzej Ptok
abstract:
Author(s): Sajid Sekh, Annica M. Black-Schaffer, and Andrzej Ptok

We study the edge state properties of a two-dimensional kagome lattice using a tight-binding approach, focusing on the role of lattice termination, spin-orbit coupling, and magnetic order. In the pristine limit, we show that the existence of localized edge states is highly sensitive to boundary geom…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235436] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies edge states in a kagome lattice under various conditions using tight-binding methods.
motivation: To understand how lattice termination, spin-orbit coupling, and magnetic order affect edge state properties in kagome lattices.
method: Tight-binding model calculations for a two-dimensional kagome lattice with different boundary geometries, spin-orbit coupling, and magnetic ordering.
result: Edge state existence and properties are highly sensitive to boundary geometry and can be tuned by spin-orbit coupling and magnetic order.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into controlling edge states in kagome lattices, relevant for topological materials.

title: Moiré Magnetism In A Bilayer Ising Model
authors: Ryan Flynn And Anders W. Sandvik
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Flynn and Anders W. Sandvik

Moiré patterns in magnetic bilayers generate spatially modulated interlayer exchange interactions that can give rise to nonuniform magnetic textures. We study a minimal classical bilayer Ising model with a moiré-modulated interlayer coupling, generated either by relative twist or differential strain…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214459] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies moiré magnetism in a bilayer Ising model, focusing on classical magnetic textures induced by modulated interlayer coupling.
motivation: Moiré patterns in magnetic bilayers can create spatially modulated interactions, leading to nonuniform magnetic textures that are of interest in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors study a minimal classical bilayer Ising model with moiré-modulated interlayer coupling, generated by relative twist or differential strain, using Monte Carlo simulations.
result: They find that the moiré modulation leads to a variety of magnetic phases, including stripe and bubble textures, depending on the strength and period of the modulation.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical understanding of moiré magnetism in classical Ising systems, which may be relevant to experimental realizations in van der Waals magnets.

title: Anyon Dispersion In Aharonov-Casher Bands And Implications For Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Zihan Yan, Qingchen Li, Tomohiro Soejima (副島智大), And Eslam Khalaf
abstract:
Author(s): Zihan Yan, Qingchen Li, Tomohiro Soejima (副島智大), and Eslam Khalaf

Here, the authors develop a microscopic theory of dispersing anyons in fractional quantum anomalous Hall systems and a momentum-space Monte Carlo framework to evaluate quasihole energies. By constructing momentum-resolved Laughlin quasihole states in Aharonov-Casher bands, they compute anyon bandwidths relevant to twisted MoTe
[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235155] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a microscopic theory of dispersing anyons in fractional quantum anomalous Hall systems and computes anyon bandwidths in twisted MoTe2.
motivation: Understanding anyon dispersion is crucial for realizing itinerant anyon phases, but previous models assumed flat bands; this work accounts for nonuniform quantum geometry.
method: The authors construct momentum-resolved Laughlin quasihole states in Aharonov-Casher bands and use a momentum-space Monte Carlo framework to evaluate quasihole energies.
result: They find that nonuniform quantum geometry combined with the quasihole Berry phase gives rise to finite anyon dispersion, and compute bandwidths relevant to twisted MoTe2.
conclusion: The work opens a route toward controlled theories of itinerant anyon phases and highlights the role of quantum geometry in anyon dynamics.

title: Magnetoexcitons And Massive Dirac Fermions In Monolayers Of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides In A High Magnetic Field
authors: Katarzyna Sadecka, Marek Korkusiński, Ludmiła Szulakowska, And Paweł Hawrylak
abstract:
Author(s): Katarzyna Sadecka, Marek Korkusiński, Ludmiła Szulakowska, and Paweł Hawrylak

We present a theory of the emission spectrum of magnetoexcitons interacting with a [MATH] quantum Hall state of massive Dirac fermions in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides in high magnetic fields. Using an ab initio–parametrized massive Dirac fermion model including valley and spin degrees o…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235156] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical study of magnetoexciton emission spectra in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides under high magnetic fields, focusing on interactions with quantum Hall states of massive Dirac fermions.
motivation: To understand the optical properties of monolayer TMDs in high magnetic fields, which is relevant for condensed matter physics but not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Uses an ab initio-parametrized massive Dirac fermion model including valley and spin degrees of freedom to compute the emission spectrum of magnetoexcitons interacting with quantum Hall states.
result: Predicts specific features in the emission spectrum due to the interaction between magnetoexcitons and the quantum Hall state.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the many-body physics of TMDs in high fields, but does not address quantum information processing or thermodynamics.

title: Anomalous Quasiparticle Lifetime In Geometric Quantum Critical Metals
authors: Hao Song, Han Ma, Catherine Kallin, And Sung-Sik Lee
abstract:
Author(s): Hao Song, Han Ma, Catherine Kallin, and Sung-Sik Lee

Metals can undergo geometric quantum phase transitions where the local curvature of the Fermi surface changes sign without a change in symmetry or topology. At the inflection points on the Fermi surface, the local curvature vanishes, leading to an anomalous dynamics of quasiparticles. In this paper,…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245148] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quasiparticle lifetime in metals at geometric quantum critical points where Fermi surface curvature vanishes.
motivation: Understanding how quasiparticles behave at quantum phase transitions where the Fermi surface curvature changes sign, which is a fundamental question in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use a theoretical model to analyze the dynamics of quasiparticles near inflection points on the Fermi surface, calculating the quasiparticle lifetime using perturbative methods.
result: They find that the quasiparticle lifetime exhibits anomalous scaling due to the vanishing curvature, leading to non-Fermi liquid behavior.
conclusion: Geometric quantum critical points can give rise to novel quasiparticle dynamics distinct from conventional quantum critical points.

title: Kondo Effect In Ferromagnetic Quantum Critical ${\mathrm{CeRh}}_{6}{\mathrm{Ge}}_{4}$

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245149] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Kondo effect and quantum criticality in a ferromagnetic heavy-fermion compound using spectroscopic techniques.
motivation: To understand the role of Kondo hybridization and the 4f electron ground state in pressure-induced quantum criticality of CeRh6Ge4.
method: Combined core-level photoemission and polarized x-ray absorption spectroscopy with single-impurity Anderson model simulations.
result: Kondo hybridization admixes higher crystal field states into a multiorbital ground state with 4f occupancy ~0.9, explaining the dynamical spin response.
conclusion: Kondo hybridization and multiorbital ground state are essential for modeling quantum criticality in this system.

tldr: This paper studies the Yamaji effect in underdoped cuprates, focusing on magnetoresistance and hole pockets in the pseudogap regime.
motivation: Recent experiments observed the Yamaji effect in underdoped cuprates, indicating small hole pockets; this work aims to model and explain these observations.
method: The authors use theoretical models of underdoped cuprates to analyze angle-dependent magnetoresistance and the Yamaji effect.
result: The paper provides a theoretical explanation for the Yamaji effect in underdoped cuprates, supporting the existence of hole pockets.
conclusion: The findings confirm the presence of small hole pockets in the pseudogap regime, consistent with experimental data.

title: Revisiting The Origin Of The Stokes Shift By Bridging Absorption And Emission Through The Optoelectronic Reciprocity Relation
authors: Meita Asami, Kentaroh Watanabe, And Masakazu Sugiyama
abstract:
Author(s): Meita Asami, Kentaroh Watanabe, and Masakazu Sugiyama

In this study, we investigate the interpretation of the Stokes shift (SS) by employing the optoelectronic reciprocity relation (ORR), which provides a fundamental link between optical absorption and emission processes. We first revisit the van Roosbroeck-Shockley relation and the generalized Planck'…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245310] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses the optoelectronic reciprocity relation to reinterpret the Stokes shift in semiconductor materials.
motivation: To provide a fundamental understanding of the Stokes shift by linking absorption and emission processes via the optoelectronic reciprocity relation.
method: The authors revisit the van Roosbroeck-Shockley relation and generalized Planck's law, applying the optoelectronic reciprocity relation to bridge absorption and emission spectra.
result: They derive a new interpretation of the Stokes shift based on the reciprocity relation, showing how it arises from the asymmetry between absorption and emission due to thermalization and relaxation.
conclusion: The optoelectronic reciprocity relation offers a unified framework for understanding the Stokes shift, with implications for optoelectronic device design.

title: Frustration-induced Collective Dynamical States In Pulse-coupled Adaptive Winfree Networks
authors: R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, And R. Suresh
abstract:
Author(s): R. Anand, V. K. Chandrasekar, and R. Suresh

We investigate collective dynamics in a pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree network under the influence of a frustration (phase-lag) parameter. The coupling strengths coevolve according to a Hebbian adaptation rule and self-organize to support a wide variety of collective states. We observe frequency-clu…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014201] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies collective dynamics in pulse-coupled adaptive Winfree networks with frustration, focusing on frequency clustering and synchronization.
motivation: To understand how frustration (phase-lag) and Hebbian adaptation affect collective states in oscillator networks.
method: Numerical simulations of a pulse-coupled Winfree network with adaptive coupling strengths following a Hebbian rule, varying the frustration parameter.
result: Observation of frequency-clustered states, chimera states, and other collective dynamical regimes depending on frustration and adaptation.
conclusion: Frustration induces a rich variety of collective dynamical states in adaptive oscillator networks, relevant to neural and biological systems.

title: Higher-order Adaptive Behaviors Outperform Pairwise Strategies In Mitigating Contagion Dynamics
authors: Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, And Alain Barrat
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Mancastroppa, Márton Karsai, and Alain Barrat

When exposed to a contagion phenomenon, individuals may respond to the perceived risk of infection by adopting behavioral changes, aiming to reduce their exposure or their risk of infecting others. The social cost of such adaptive behaviors and their impact on the contagion dynamics have been invest…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014302] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how higher-order adaptive behaviors (e.g., group-level responses) outperform pairwise strategies in mitigating contagion dynamics in social networks.
motivation: Understanding how individual behavioral changes affect epidemic spread is crucial, but most models consider only pairwise interactions; higher-order social structures may be more realistic.
method: The authors develop a model of contagion with adaptive behaviors at both pairwise and higher-order (group) levels, and compare their effectiveness using simulations on synthetic and empirical networks.
result: Higher-order adaptive strategies are significantly more effective at reducing the final epidemic size and peak prevalence than pairwise strategies alone.
conclusion: Incorporating higher-order social interactions into models of behavioral adaptation is essential for accurately predicting and controlling contagion dynamics.
