tldr: This paper studies first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near a wall using numerical simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic attraction and hindered diffusion.
motivation: Understanding how microorganisms encounter surfaces is important for biological and medical applications, but the role of hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion is not fully understood.
method: Numerical simulations of force-dipole microswimmers near a no-slip wall are performed to compute first-passage-time statistics.
result: Wall-induced hindered diffusion delays wall encounters, while active hydrodynamic attraction leads to distinct behaviors for pushers and pullers, including a nonmonotonic dependence on dipole strength.
conclusion: Hydrodynamic interactions and diffusion significantly affect the first-passage times of swimming microorganisms near walls.

tldr: This paper presents a high-stability optical clock based on a continuously ground-state cooled Al+ ion, achieving reduced averaging time without compromising accuracy.
motivation: Single-ion optical clocks have high systematic accuracy but require long averaging times to reach statistical uncertainty; this work aims to reduce averaging time by extending probe duration while mitigating time-dilation shifts.
method: The authors implement continuous ground-state cooling of an Al+ ion and use a novel interrogation scheme to extend probe times, while carefully characterizing and compensating for time-dilation shifts due to ion motion.

title: Tip-enhanced Molecular Fluorescence Microscopy With Atomic-scale Resolution
authors: Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, And Guillaume Schull
abstract:
Author(s): Anna Rosławska, Katharina Kaiser, Sofia Canola, Song Jiang, Fabrice Scheurer, Javier Aizpurua, Tomáš Neuman, and Guillaume Schull

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025007] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: This review discusses tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy achieving atomic-scale resolution using scanning probe techniques.
motivation: To overcome the diffraction limit in optical microscopy and achieve atomic-scale spatial resolution for studying molecular electronic and vibronic properties.
method: Combines scanning probe microscopy with a metallic tip that acts as a nanoscale optical antenna to confine the electromagnetic field at the tip apex.
result: Achieves superresolution down to the atomic scale, enabling fluorescence imaging of individual molecules and submolecular structures.
conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical characterization of molecular systems.

title: Order And Disorder At The Atomic Scale: Microscopy Applied To Semiconductors
authors: Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, And Lorenzo Rigutti
abstract:
Author(s): Enrico Di Russo, Tom Verstijnen, Paul Koenraad, Konstantinos Pantzas, Gilles Patriarche, and Lorenzo Rigutti

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: A review of real-space microscopy techniques for measuring atomic-scale disorder in semiconductors.
motivation: Atomic-scale disorder critically affects semiconductor properties but is difficult to measure; the paper aims to review three real-space techniques that provide direct access to such information.
method: The authors review scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy, emphasizing combined use for a complete picture of defects.
result: The review highlights how these techniques can characterize disorder at the atomic scale in compound semiconductors.
conclusion: Real-space microscopy methods are powerful for understanding atomic-scale disorder, and combining them yields more comprehensive insights.

Author(s): Robin Buschbeck, Mike N. Pionteck, Naomi Herrmann, Michael Rüsing, Susanne C. Kehr, Simone Sanna, and Lukas M. Eng

Raman imaging, based on incoherent spontaneous Raman scattering (SR) or coherent techniques such as broadband coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy (BCARS), is a powerful tool for visualizing local lattice distortions. It can thus be employed, e.g., to identify and visualize ferroelectric (FE) dom…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 034104] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents ab initio modeling and experimental analysis of contrast in broadband coherent anti-Stokes Raman spectroscopy (BCARS) applied to ferroelectric domain walls.
motivation: To understand the contrast mechanisms in BCARS imaging of ferroelectric domain walls, which is important for non-destructive characterization of ferroelectric materials.
method: Combines density functional theory (DFT) calculations of Raman spectra with experimental BCARS measurements on lithium niobate domain walls.
result: The study identifies specific phonon modes that contribute to BCARS contrast and shows that the contrast arises from changes in phonon frequencies and intensities across domain walls.
conclusion: BCARS can effectively visualize ferroelectric domain walls with high contrast, and the contrast is explained by local lattice distortions affecting Raman-active phonons.

title: Interface Effects Of Pb Films On ${\mathrm{TlBiSe}}_{2}$ And ${\mathrm{Bi}}_{2}{\mathrm{Se}}_{3}$ Topological Insulators
authors: Roberto Flammini, Oreste de Luca, Martina Casciaro, Tommaso Caruso, Fabio Biffoli, Daniela Pacilé, Khatira Z. Mehtiyeva, Ziya S. Aliev, Alexey Barinov, Alfonso Policicchio, Anastasia G. We present an experimental investigation of the Pb-induced changes on the electronic structure of selected topological insulators, namely, [MATH] and [MATH]. Using spatially resolved and surface-sensitive techniques, including micro-angle-resolved photo…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045101] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interface effects of lead films on topological insulators TlBiSe2 and Bi2Se3 using surface-sensitive techniques.
motivation: Understanding how metal overlayers modify the electronic structure of topological insulators is important for potential spintronic applications.
method: The authors used micro-angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and other surface-sensitive techniques to probe the electronic structure changes induced by Pb deposition.
result: Pb deposition induces significant modifications to the surface states of the topological insulators, including band bending and shifts in Dirac point energy.
conclusion: The interface effects are substantial and must be considered when designing topological insulator-based devices.

title: Reconstruction Of Residual Kinetic Energy In Inertial-confinement Fusion Implosions At The National Ignition Facility Using Multiple Heterogeneous Data Sources And Neural Networks
authors: J. H. Kunimune, D. T. Casey, B. Kustowski, M. Jones, L. Divol, T. M. Johnson, S. G. Dannhoff, A. Devault, And J. A. Frenje
abstract:
Author(s): J. H. Kunimune, D. T. Casey, B. Kustowski, M. Jones, L. Divol, T. M. Johnson, S. G. Dannhoff, A. DeVault, and J. A. Frenje

Three-dimensional (3D) asymmetries and their associated residual kinetic energy (RKE) are a major performance-degradation mechanism in inertial-confinement fusion (ICF) implosions at the National Ignition Facility (NIF). These asymmetries can be diagnosed with the three neutron imaging systems field…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065213] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses neural networks to reconstruct residual kinetic energy in inertial confinement fusion implosions at the National Ignition Facility.
motivation: Three-dimensional asymmetries and residual kinetic energy degrade performance in inertial confinement fusion; diagnosing these asymmetries is important for improving fusion yields.
method: The authors combine multiple heterogeneous data sources (neutron imaging, etc.) with neural networks to reconstruct the residual kinetic energy.
result: The neural network approach successfully reconstructs residual kinetic energy from experimental data.
conclusion: The method provides a new diagnostic tool for understanding and mitigating performance degradation in ICF implosions.

title: Theory And Simulation Of Turbulence Driven By Momentum Transfer From Material Emitting High-energy Particles
authors: S. E. Kuratov, A. Yu. Mikulin, S. I. Glazyrin, And D. S. Shidlovski
abstract:
Author(s): S. E. Kuratov, A. Yu. Mikulin, S. I. Glazyrin, and D. S. Shidlovski

The development of hydrodynamic instabilities may be significantly affected by the presence of suprathermal high-energy particles (HEPs). These effects are particularly pronounced in high-energy-density plasmas. We develop a single-equation diffusion-type turbulence model that describes the turbulen…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065111] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a turbulence model for high-energy-density plasmas driven by momentum transfer from high-energy particles.
motivation: Understanding hydrodynamic instabilities in high-energy-density plasmas is important for applications like inertial confinement fusion, and high-energy particles can significantly affect turbulence.
method: A single-equation diffusion-type turbulence model is developed to describe the turbulent kinetic energy driven by momentum transfer from suprathermal high-energy particles.
result: The model captures the effect of high-energy particles on turbulence and can be used to simulate instability development in high-energy-density plasmas.
conclusion: The proposed model provides a framework for studying turbulence in plasmas with high-energy particles, relevant to high-energy-density physics.

title: Selective Wave Transmission In Strongly Nonlinear Disordered Granular Chains
authors: João Guilherme Pinto de Freitas, Luis Paulo Silveira Machado, And Surajit Sen
abstract:
Author(s): João Guilherme Pinto de Freitas, Luis Paulo Silveira Machado, and Surajit Sen

Chains of 1000 granules in mutual contact, without precompression, and with random radii that follow a normal distribution are studied numerically. The standard deviation [MATH] controls the disorder level. The chains are subject to (i) a striker impact and (ii) an actuator that imposes band-limited wh…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065426] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave transmission in strongly nonlinear disordered granular chains under impact and band-limited white noise excitation.
motivation: Understanding wave propagation in disordered granular media is important for applications like impact mitigation and energy harvesting.
method: Numerical simulations of 1000-granule chains with random radii following a normal distribution, subjected to striker impact or actuator-imposed band-limited white noise.
result: Selective wave transmission is observed depending on disorder level and excitation type.
conclusion: Disorder in granular chains can be used to control wave transmission properties.

title: Geomimicry: Emergent Dynamics In Earth-mediated Complex Materials
authors: Shravan Pradeep, Emanuela Del Gado, Douglas J. Jerolmack, And Paulo E. Arratia
abstract:
Author(s): Shravan Pradeep, Emanuela Del Gado, Douglas J. Jerolmack, and Paulo E. Arratia

Soils and sediments are soft, amorphous materials with complex microstructures and mechanical properties. They are also building blocks for industrial materials such as concrete. These Earth-mediated materials evolve under prolonged environmental pressures such as mechanical stress, chemical gradien…



[Phys. Rev. E 113, 061002] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the emergent dynamics of Earth-mediated complex materials like soils and sediments under environmental pressures.
motivation: Understanding the evolution of soft, amorphous materials under prolonged mechanical and chemical stress is important for geophysics and industrial applications.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical approaches to characterize microstructural and mechanical changes in these materials.
result: The paper reveals how these materials exhibit complex, emergent behaviors over time.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into the dynamics of Earth-mediated materials but do not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Predicting Instantaneous Friction From Friction Damping Coefficients In Underdamped Sliding
authors: Chengdong Sun, Yi Tao, Zaoqi Duan, Kai Chen, Quan Han, Yajing Kan, Zhonghua Ni, Zhiyong Wei, Yan Zhang, And Yunfei Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Chengdong Sun, Yi Tao, Zaoqi Duan, Kai Chen, Quan Han, Yajing Kan, Zhonghua Ni, Zhiyong Wei, Yan Zhang, and Yunfei Chen

Friction accounts for nearly one-third of global energy consumption. While the coefficient of friction is widely used to quantify energy dissipation in sliding contacts, its strong dependence on sliding velocity limits its effectiveness in predicting instantaneous friction forces and friction-induce…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065508] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies friction in sliding contacts using friction damping coefficients, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Friction accounts for nearly one-third of global energy consumption, and predicting instantaneous friction forces is important for energy efficiency.
method: The authors propose a model to predict instantaneous friction from friction damping coefficients in underdamped sliding systems.
result: The model improves prediction of friction forces compared to using the coefficient of friction alone.
conclusion: The approach offers a more accurate way to quantify energy dissipation in sliding contacts.

title: Ghost Mechanism: An Analytical Model Of Abrupt Learning In Recurrent Networks
authors: Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, And Hidenori Tanaka
abstract:
Author(s): Fatih Dinc, Ege Cirakman, Bariscan Kurtkaya, Mert Yuksekgonul, Yiqi Jiang, Mark J. Schnitzer, and Hidenori Tanaka

This study establishes the ghost mechanism as an underlying mechanism for abrupt learning, whereby the recurrent neural network develops ghost points—transient dynamical bottlenecks—and identifies ways to overcome the training instabilities.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021058] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a ghost mechanism to explain abrupt learning in recurrent neural networks, focusing on dynamical systems and machine learning theory.
motivation: Understanding abrupt learning phenomena in recurrent networks is important for training stability and performance, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop an analytical model of ghost points as transient dynamical bottlenecks in recurrent neural networks.
result: They identify ghost points as a mechanism for abrupt learning and propose ways to overcome training instabilities.
conclusion: The ghost mechanism provides insight into learning dynamics in recurrent networks, but the work is purely in machine learning and dynamical systems.

title: Elastic And Structural Anisotropy In Silica Thin Films For Gravitational-Wave Detectors
authors: Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, And Silvia Corezzi
abstract:
Author(s): Brenda Bracco, Michele Magnozzi, Stefano Colace, Maurizio Canepa, Giulio Favaro, Marco Bazzan, Massimo Granata, David Hofman, Alessandro Di Michele, Laura Silenzi, Gianpietro Cagnoli, Giovanni Carlotti, Paola Sassi, and Silvia Corezzi

Researchers find that silica films in mirror coatings of gravitational-wave detectors have hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment. This discovery informs coating design and deposition and postprocessing strategies aimed at reducing thermal noise.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021036] Published Fri May 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies elastic and structural anisotropy in silica thin films used in gravitational-wave detector mirror coatings, focusing on thermal noise reduction.
motivation: Thermal noise in mirror coatings limits the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors; understanding and mitigating anisotropy in silica films could improve performance.
method: The authors characterize the elastic and structural properties of silica thin films using experimental techniques to detect hidden anisotropy and test the effects of standard heat treatments.
result: They find that silica films exhibit hidden anisotropy that resists standard heat treatment, informing coating design and postprocessing strategies.
conclusion: The findings guide the development of deposition and postprocessing strategies to reduce thermal noise in gravitational-wave detectors.

title: Intertwined Polar, Chiral, And Ferro-Rotational Orders In A Homo-Ferro-Rotational Insulator
authors: Weizhe Zhang, June Ho Yeo, Xiaoyu Guo, Tony Chiang, Nishkarsh Agarwal, John T. Heron, Kai Sun, Junjie Yang, Sang-Wook Cheong, Youngjun Ahn, And Liuyan Zhao
abstract:

Multimodal optical characterization of Ni
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021030] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of intertwined polar, chiral, and ferro-rotational orders in a homo-ferro-rotational insulator using multimodal optical characterization.
motivation: To understand the coupling between different types of ferroic orders (polar, chiral, ferro-rotational) in a single material, which is of interest for fundamental condensed matter physics.
method: Multimodal optical characterization techniques were used to study the material Ni2Mo3O8, identifying the ferro-rotational state and its coupling to polarity and chirality.
result: A uniform ferro-rotational state was identified that couples polarity and chirality, leading to complex mixed-type domain walls.
conclusion: The findings reveal a new type of multiferroic order with intertwined ferroic properties, which may have implications for understanding domain wall physics and designing multifunctional materials.

title: Tracking Ultrafast Ion Diffusion Dynamics In ${\mathrm{AgCrSe}}_{2}$ Superionic Conductor
authors: Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, And Jiaqing He

Author(s): Jianmin Yang, Lin Xie, Mingyuan Hu, Yingpeng Qi, Jun Li, Baohai Jia, Jianghe Feng, Zijing Chen, Michel Bosman, Dao Xiang, and Jiaqing He

Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion in superionic conductors provides a better link to macroscopic properties and high-performance material design.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021024] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally tracks ultrafast ion diffusion dynamics in AgCrSe2 superionic conductor using ultrafast electron diffraction.
motivation: Understanding ion diffusion in superionic conductors is crucial for designing high-performance materials for energy applications.
method: Ultrafast electron diffraction with femtosecond laser pump-probe technique to directly observe ion motion in real time.
result: Direct spatial and temporal characterization of ion diffusion dynamics was achieved, revealing the microscopic mechanism.
conclusion: The work provides a direct link between microscopic ion dynamics and macroscopic properties, aiding material design.

title: Effect Of Glass Stability On The Low Frequency Vibrations Of Vapor Deposited Glasses
authors: I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, And G. Baldi
abstract:
Author(s): I. Festi, E. Alfinelli, D. Bessas, F. Caporaletti, A. I. Chumakov, M. Moratalla, M. A. Ramos, M. Rodríguez-López, C. Rodríguez-Tinoco, J. Rodríguez-Viejo, and G. Baldi

An improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique helps clarify the connections between complex vibrations and the properties of glasses.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021021] Published Tue Apr 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses using inelastic x-ray scattering, focusing on the effect of glass stability.
motivation: Understanding the vibrational properties of glasses is important for their mechanical and thermal behavior, but this work is purely in condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Improved inelastic x-ray scattering technique was used to measure low-frequency vibrations in vapor-deposited glasses of varying stability.
result: The study clarifies how glass stability affects the low-frequency vibrational spectrum.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the structure-dynamics relationship in glasses, but have no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Radiation Forces And Torques In Optics And Acoustics
authors: Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, And Konstantin Y. Bliokh
abstract:
Author(s): Ivan Toftul, Sebastian Golat, Francisco J. Rodríguez-Fortuño, Franco Nori, Yuri Kivshar, and Konstantin Y. Bliokh

This review presents a unified perspective of how local energy, momentum, and spin densities in optical and acoustic wave fields induce forces and torques on particles—a topic that has captivated researchers for centuries. Applications discussed include trapping and manipulation of atoms and nanoparticles by light, sorting of biological cells by the combination of acoustics and microfluidics, and pulling forces that draw particles against the direction of wave propagation.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025002] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: This review unifies the description of radiation forces and torques in optical and acoustic fields, focusing on momentum and spin densities.
motivation: Understanding how wave fields exert forces and torques on particles is fundamental for applications like optical trapping and acoustic manipulation.
method: The authors present a unified theoretical framework based on local energy, momentum, and spin densities in both optical and acoustic wave fields.
result: They show that the same physical principles govern forces and torques in optics and acoustics, enabling cross-disciplinary insights.
conclusion: The unified perspective can guide the design of advanced particle manipulation techniques using light and sound.

title: Pressure Effects On Metals, Alloys, And Compounds Of Transplutonium Elements
authors: Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, And Thomas E. Albrecht
abstract:
Author(s): Tyler W. Hines, Nicholas B. Beck, Kacy N. Mendoza, Joseph M. Sperling, and Thomas E. Albrecht

Materials containing transplutonium elements (the actinides Am–Cm that come after Pu in the periodic table) are important for nuclear power, nuclear waste management, and long-term storage. They also have fascinating properties, with 5
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics and chemistry of transplutonium compounds under high pressure, focusing on their electronic structure and material properties.
motivation: Transplutonium elements are important for nuclear power and waste management, and their 5f electrons exhibit unique localized/itinerant behavior under pressure.
method: The paper is a review summarizing experimental and theoretical studies of transplutonium metals, alloys, and coordination complexes under high pressure.
result: It highlights the challenges and recent progress in understanding the electronic and structural properties of these radioactive materials.
conclusion: The review expands our understanding of transplutonium materials but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Multimessenger Astronomy With Continuous Gravitational Waves And Future Detectors
authors: Benjamin J. Owen
abstract:
Author(s): Benjamin J. Owen

The search for continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars represents a key frontier of gravitational-wave astrophysics, with strong connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics. This Colloquium discusses the detection prospects for these long-lived yet elusive signals in the upcoming generation of gravitational-wave detectors, emphasizing the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations. It also surveys the potential implications of such multimessenger observations for our understanding of the physical and astrophysical processes taking place in the extremely dense environments of their sources.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011002] Published Tue Mar 10, 2026.
tldr: This colloquium discusses the prospects for detecting continuous gravitational waves from rotating neutron stars and their multimessenger implications.
motivation: Continuous gravitational waves from neutron stars are a key frontier in gravitational-wave astrophysics, with connections to electromagnetic astronomy, nuclear astrophysics, and condensed matter physics.
method: The paper reviews detection prospects for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors and emphasizes the importance of simultaneous electromagnetic observations.
result: It surveys potential implications of multimessenger observations for understanding physical processes in dense neutron star environments.
conclusion: Multimessenger astronomy with continuous gravitational waves will enhance our understanding of neutron star physics and astrophysics.

title: Colloquium: Gravitational Waves From Neutrino-driven Core Collapse Supernovae
authors: A. Mezzacappa And M. Zanolin
abstract:
Author(s): A. Mezzacappa and M. Zanolin

The observation of a core collapse supernova explosion of (near-)Galactic origin would constitute a landmark, once-in-a-century event for multimessenger astronomy, eagerly awaited by observers and modelers alike. The detection of gravitational waves, along with photons and neutrinos, from such an event would provide unique insights into the supernova central engine and the physics of the newly forming neutron star. This Colloquium presents the latest progress in core collapse supernova modeling and the associated gravitational wave signal predictions. It also provides an overview of the specific methods of detection and physical parameter estimation that can be implemented for such signals in ground-based laser interferometers, in the context of multimessenger research strategies.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041002] Published Tue Dec 30, 2025.
tldr: This colloquium reviews gravitational wave signals from core collapse supernovae and their detection methods.
motivation: Observing a Galactic core collapse supernova would be a landmark event for multimessenger astronomy, providing insights into the supernova engine and neutron star physics.
method: The paper summarizes recent progress in core collapse supernova modeling and gravitational wave signal predictions, and discusses detection methods in ground-based laser interferometers.
result: The review presents the current state of gravitational wave predictions from supernovae and outlines strategies for detection and parameter estimation.
conclusion: Gravitational wave detection from supernovae, combined with photons and neutrinos, will enable unique multimessenger studies of these events.

title: Neutron Stars And The Dense Matter Equation Of State
authors: Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, And Anna L. Watts
abstract:
Author(s): Katerina Chatziioannou, H. Thankful Cromartie, Stefano Gandolfi, Ingo Tews, David Radice, Andrew W. Steiner, and Anna L. Watts

Neutron stars, the remnants of supernova explosions, are the densest objects in the Universe. A typical neutron star has a mass between one and two solar masses, and a radius of around 12 km. The density at the center of the star is higher than that in atomic nuclei. As a result, the properties of neutron stars provide important information about the behavior of ordinary matter under extreme compression. In recent years, new information about neutron stars has emerged from two sources. The first is the observation of the gravitational-wave signal from the final inspiral of a coalescing binary neutron star. The second is a careful measurement of the x-ray pulse profile of a spinning neutron star. This review discusses these measurements and summarizes how they constrain masses, radii, and central densities. The results are compared to predictions based on calculations of the nuclear equation of state at densities comparable to that in atomic nuclei, which are then extrapolated to higher density. The review ends with an outlook on future observational opportunities.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045007] Published Wed Dec 24, 2025.
tldr: This review discusses how neutron star observations constrain the dense matter equation of state.
motivation: Neutron stars are the densest objects in the Universe, and their properties provide information about matter under extreme compression.
method: The review summarizes constraints from gravitational-wave signals of binary neutron star mergers and x-ray pulse profile measurements, comparing them to nuclear equation of state calculations.
result: The measurements constrain masses, radii, and central densities of neutron stars.
conclusion: Future observations will further refine the equation of state.

title: Prospects For Supersymmetry At High-Luminosity Lhc
authors: Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, And Kairui Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Howard Baer, Vernon Barger, Jessica Bolich, Juhi Dutta, Dakotah Martinez, Shadman Salam, Dibyashree Sengupta, and Kairui Zhang

Supersymmetry remains one of the leading candidates for physics beyond the standard model, offering a compelling framework to address the hierarchy of scales. Its theoretical appeal has inspired decades of intensive model building and experimental searches. Recent results have placed stringent bounds on the supersymmetric parameter space, sharpening the focus on the remaining viable models. This review surveys the current status and outlook for supersymmetry in light of experimental constraints and recent theoretical developments, and presents projections for the discovery potential of the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider across multiple search channels and a variety of well-motivated scenarios.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045001] Published Fri Oct 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the prospects for supersymmetry at the High-Luminosity LHC, focusing on experimental searches and model constraints.
motivation: Supersymmetry is a leading candidate for beyond Standard Model physics, but recent LHC results have constrained its parameter space. The paper aims to survey the current status and future discovery potential.
method: The authors review theoretical models and experimental search channels, and project sensitivities for the High-Luminosity LHC based on current constraints.
result: The paper provides an overview of viable supersymmetric scenarios and estimates of discovery reach across multiple channels.
conclusion: Supersymmetry remains viable but increasingly constrained; the HL-LHC will probe significant remaining parameter space.

title: Solar Fusion Iii: New Data And Theory For Hydrogen-burning Stars
authors: B. Acharya et Al.
abstract:
Author(s): B. Acharya et al.

Approximately 90% of the stars in the Milky Way are on the main sequence, fusing hydrogen into helium through a network of nuclear reactions. This includes the nearest star, our Sun. A precise understanding of hydrogen burning is crucial to predicting its luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology. This review describes the theoretical and experimental work of the last decade that has advanced our understanding of the nuclear physics of hydrogen burning. It describes the plasma and atomic physics that influences the solar environment in which the nuclear reactions take place, as well as the diagnostics probes—including solar neutrinos and helioseismology—that allow us to test our resulting model of the solar interior.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035002] Published Thu Sep 04, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews nuclear physics of hydrogen burning in stars, focusing on solar fusion reactions, plasma physics, and diagnostics like neutrinos and helioseismology.
motivation: Understanding hydrogen burning is crucial for predicting stellar properties such as luminosity, neutrino production, and helioseismology.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental advances over the last decade in nuclear reaction rates, plasma and atomic physics, and solar interior modeling.
result: It summarizes updated nuclear reaction data and improved solar models that better match observations of solar neutrinos and helioseismic data.
conclusion: The review consolidates recent progress in solar fusion physics, providing a benchmark for stellar evolution models and neutrino physics.

title: Nobel Lecture: Physics Is A Point Of View
authors: John J. Hopfield
abstract:
Author(s): John J. Hopfield

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030501] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: Nobel lecture by John Hopfield reflecting on his career and the nature of physics.
motivation: To share personal insights and perspectives on physics as a field of study.
method: Narrative and reflective lecture.
result: No novel research results; a retrospective on past contributions.
conclusion: Physics is a point of view that evolves with new discoveries.

title: Nobel Lecture: Boltzmann Machines
authors: Geoffrey Hinton
abstract:
Author(s): Geoffrey Hinton

The 2024 Nobel Prize for Physics was shared by John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton. This paper is the text of the address given in conjunction with the award.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 030502] Published Mon Aug 25, 2025.
tldr: This is a Nobel lecture on Boltzmann machines, a classical machine learning model, with no direct connection to quantum information theory.
motivation: The lecture presents the development and significance of Boltzmann machines in machine learning.
method: The paper describes the architecture and learning algorithm of Boltzmann machines.
result: Boltzmann machines are a foundational model for unsupervised learning and have influenced deep learning.
conclusion: The work is important for machine learning but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This review summarizes the state of the art in low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions at stellar energies is crucial for stellar burning and nucleosynthesis, but direct measurements are often impossible due to extremely small cross sections.
method: The paper reviews theoretical approaches including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects, and discusses experimental techniques to study these reactions.
result: It provides a comprehensive overview of current theoretical models and experimental methods for low-energy nuclear astrophysics.
conclusion: The field requires continued theoretical and experimental advances to accurately model stellar processes and element formation.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology.

title: The Need For Optoacoustic Microscopy
authors: Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, And Vasilis Ntziachristos
abstract:
Author(s): Ludwig Englert, Dominik Jüstel, and Vasilis Ntziachristos

Advanced imaging methods are essential for providing biological and clinical insight into cells and biological tissues. Optoacoustic imaging is one such method in which cells or tissues absorb short laser pulses and the resulting rise in temperature creates tiny ultrasound waves that can be detected by ultrasonic detectors placed outside the specimen. This noninvasive technique has the ability to look at optical contrast that is millimeters and even centimeters deep with high resolution. This review discusses the basic physics, how the method impacts biological and clinical research, and the latest developments in multimodal microscopy and imaging combining optical and optoacoustic techniques.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015005] Published Tue Mar 04, 2025.

result: Optoacoustic microscopy enables imaging millimeters to centimeters deep with high resolution, providing optical contrast in scattering tissues.
conclusion: Optoacoustic microscopy is a valuable tool for biological and clinical imaging, with ongoing advances in multimodal approaches.

title: Deterministic Initiation Of Inner-shell X-ray Lasers By Two-color Raman Driving
authors: Carles Serrat
abstract: Inner-shell x-ray lasers are conventionally initiated by amplified spontaneous emission (ASE), so that the temporal onset and longitudinal phase of the emitted field are determined by microscopic noise fluctuations. As a result, the early-time dynamics of the laser pulse are intrinsically stochastic. We analyze a regime in which the initial polarization that triggers inner-shell x-ray lasing is imposed deterministically by a resonant two-color Raman drive. Two coherent x-ray fields at angular frequencies and satisfying induce a core–valence coherence at the lasing frequency through an off-resonant Raman coupling mediated by virtual intermediate states. No electromagnetic field is applied at , and population inversion is generated independently by conventional inner-shell photoionization. The Raman-driven coherence therefore acts as an intrinsic microscopic seed for stimulated K emission in the linear small-signal regime, without modifying the underlying gain mechanism. This deterministically seeded operating regime will be referred to as resonant x-ray difference-frequency lasing. Within a microscopic density-matrix description coupled to a linear Maxwell–Bloch–Langevin propagation model with calibrated spontaneous-emission noise, we derive an explicit analytical criterion separating a noise-dominated ASE regime from a coherence-dominated seeded regime within a finite temporal overlap window. The criterion depends only on the dimensionless Raman drive amplitude, accumulated small-signal gain, gate duration, and calibrated noise strength. Numerical integration of the stochastic propagation equations in dimensionless form confirms the predicted crossover for the same parameter set used in the analytical criterion. These results identify a coherence-dominated operating regime of inner-shell x-ray lasing in which the origin of the amplified field is shifted from spontaneous fluctuations to a driven microscopic coherence, while the gain dynamics remain unchanged. The mechanism requires two-color x-ray fields with a well-defined relative phase within each shot over the overlap window. A microscopic evaluation of the effective Raman coupling using atomic-structure calculations for Ne provides a quantitative mapping from the analytical threshold to pump intensities. Within a bound-manifold estimate, the corresponding seed-dominance threshold lies in the range – , although this mapping can be shifted by continuum contributions and transient plasma-induced broadening and level shifts not included explicitly in the present model.
tldr: This paper proposes a deterministic seeding mechanism for inner-shell x-ray lasers using two-color Raman driving, shifting the initiation from noise-dominated ASE to a coherence-dominated regime.
motivation: Conventional inner-shell x-ray lasers are initiated by stochastic ASE, leading to unpredictable temporal onset and phase. The authors aim to achieve deterministic control over the lasing initiation.
method: The authors analyze a regime where a resonant two-color Raman drive induces core-valence coherence at the lasing frequency, acting as a seed. They use a microscopic density-matrix description coupled to a linear Maxwell-Bloch-Langevin propagation model with calibrated noise, deriving an analytical criterion for the crossover from ASE to seeded regime.
result: An explicit analytical criterion is derived that separates noise-dominated ASE from coherence-dominated seeded regime, depending on Raman drive amplitude, gain, gate duration, and noise strength. Numerical simulations confirm the predicted crossover.
conclusion: The mechanism enables deterministic initiation of inner-shell x-ray lasing, shifting the field's origin from spontaneous fluctuations to a driven microscopic coherence, without altering the gain dynamics.

abstract: The contemporary landscape of artificial intelligence (AI) diplomacy in Africa is structurally bound to the continent’s history of science, technology, and innovation (STI) engagement. Colonial-era scientific expeditions sought to catalog geological resources and ecological assets to feed the industrial economies of Western countries, establishing a systemic dependency that relegated Africa to the periphery of the global natural resource trade and other strategic mineral markets. This legacy shaped an international order in which technological advancements across North America, Europe, and East Asia frequently occur through the extraction of African resources, without corresponding technology transfer or local capacity building.

conclusion: Calls for institutionalizing AI diplomacy in Africa to overcome historical imbalances and foster local capacity building.

method: Repeatedly scanning the sky with a large-format digital camera over a decade.
result: A comprehensive movie of the changing universe, cataloging billions of galaxies and transient events.
conclusion: The survey will provide unprecedented data for astronomy and cosmology.

Experimental three-dimensional measurements of the flow field around a free-swimming microalga reveal that microscopic organisms generate unexpected low-Reynolds-number flow phenomena, expanding our understanding of microhydrodynamics with profound biological implications for microbial motility and physiology.

title: High-energy Emission From The Galactic Center
authors: Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, And Régis Terrier
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Goldwurm, Maïca Clavel, Stefano Gabici, and Régis Terrier

In this review, the authors provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view of high-energy emission from the center of our Galaxy. This region contains the closest supermassive black hole to us, which offers the best studied galactic nucleus in the Universe, with its quiescent emission and accretion contrasted by flaring activity. The Galactic Center also hosts diverse compact sources, plasma bubbles, and x-ray chimneys, altogether forming a dense interacting molecular zone—a gigantic powerhouse in the Milky Way.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025006] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: A review of high-energy emission from the Galactic Center, covering astrophysical phenomena such as the supermassive black hole, compact sources, and plasma bubbles.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive multiwavelength overview of the high-energy processes in the Galactic Center, which is the closest and best-studied galactic nucleus.
method: Review of observational data across multiple wavelengths, including X-ray, gamma-ray, and radio, synthesizing results from various instruments and missions.
result: The Galactic Center exhibits a rich variety of high-energy phenomena, including quiescent and flaring emission from Sgr A*, diffuse emission from plasma bubbles and chimneys, and contributions from compact sources.
conclusion: The Galactic Center serves as a unique laboratory for studying high-energy astrophysics and accretion processes around a supermassive black hole.

title: Fundamentals Of Vacuum Breakdown In High-gradient Accelerator Structures
authors: Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, And Yinon Ashkenazy
abstract:
Author(s): Walter Wuensch, Sergio Calatroni, Flyura Djurabekova, Andreas Kyritsakis, and Yinon Ashkenazy

Vacuum breakdown or arcing happens when a very strong electric field causes a metal surface in a vacuum to suddenly form plasma, allowing large electrical currents to flow. Breakdown can damage particle accelerators, fusion reactors, satellites, and x-ray devices, though it is useful in technologies like plasma thrusters. Scientists have studied this unpredictable and fast phenomenon for over a century. Recent advances in experiments and computer simulations now provide a coherent mechanistic picture: tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns. These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025004] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the physics of vacuum breakdown in high-gradient accelerator structures, focusing on the role of surface defects, electrical stress, and plasma formation.
motivation: Vacuum breakdown limits the performance of particle accelerators and other high-power devices; understanding its mechanism is crucial for improving reliability and efficiency.
method: The authors synthesize experimental observations and computer simulations to build a coherent mechanistic picture of the breakdown process.
result: They identify that tiny surface defects, electrical stress, heat, and emitted particles interact in complex ways to trigger breakdowns.
conclusion: These insights could improve high-power technologies and make advanced accelerators more reliable and efficient.

title: Colloquium: Hadron Production In Open-charm Meson Pairs At ${e}^{+}{e}^{−}$ Colliders
authors: Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, And Yuanning Gao
abstract:
Author(s): Xiongfei Wang, Xiang Liu, and Yuanning Gao

Hadron spectroscopy is a frontier of particle physics; searching for new hadrons is crucial for validating the theory of strong interaction (QCD). Investigating how charmonium, a bound state of charm and anticharm quarks, decays and searching for new charmoniumlike states yield valuable insights into strong interaction mechanisms, including quark confinement and gluon binding. Hadrons produced at e− collisions decaying to open-charm meson pairs are a primary source of experimental information for these investigations. This Colloquium reviews current progress from BARBAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments. As BESIII accumulates high-precision data, it has emerged as the leading facility for measuring hadron production in charm-meson pair systems, and recent advances are highlighted.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021001] Published Fri Apr 03, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews hadron production in open-charm meson pairs at e+e- colliders, focusing on charmonium spectroscopy and strong interaction mechanisms.
motivation: Searching for new hadrons and understanding charmonium decays provides insights into quantum chromodynamics, quark confinement, and gluon binding.
method: The paper reviews experimental progress from BABAR, Belle, CLEO-c, and BESIII experiments, highlighting recent high-precision data from BESIII.
result: The review summarizes current knowledge of hadron production in charm-meson pair systems and identifies BESIII as the leading facility for such measurements.
conclusion: Continued experimental studies of open-charm meson pairs are crucial for advancing hadron spectroscopy and testing QCD.

title: Colloquium: Planetary Radar At The Arecibo Observatory
authors: Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, And Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín
abstract:
Author(s): Michael C. Nolan, Lynn M. Carter, and Edgard G. Rivera-Valentín

For more than two decades, the planetary radar installed at the Arecibo Telescope was the most sensitive instrument of its kind, harnessing the penetrating power of radio waves to perform observations of the (sub)surface of planets, moons, and asteroids in the Solar System—providing a unique perspective on those bodies that helped to drive in situ exploration. This Colloquium presents an overview of the scientific legacy of the Arecibo radar system, focusing on the period posterior to the Gregorian Update in the late 1990s until the unexpected demise of the telescope in 2020. After recalling the basics of planetary radar techniques, it reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, our Moon, and the Saturn system, and highlights its essential role in the characterization of a large sample of near-Earth asteroids and comets.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011003] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the scientific legacy of planetary radar observations at the Arecibo Observatory, focusing on Solar System bodies.
motivation: Planetary radar provides unique subsurface and surface information about planets, moons, and asteroids, complementing in situ exploration.
method: The paper summarizes the basics of planetary radar techniques and reviews key Arecibo observations of Mercury, Venus, Mars, the Moon, the Saturn system, and near-Earth asteroids and comets.
result: Arecibo's radar system was the most sensitive of its kind for over two decades, enabling detailed characterization of many Solar System objects.
conclusion: The Arecibo radar system made significant contributions to planetary science, and its loss marks the end of an era for ground-based planetary radar.

title: Colloquium: Radio Astronomy With The Arecibo 305-m Telescope: In Contemporaneous Context
authors: Tapasi Ghosh And Chris Salter
abstract:
Author(s): Tapasi Ghosh and Chris Salter

The Arecibo Observatory, inaugurated in 1963 as the world’s largest single-dish radio telescope, remained at the forefront of astronomy and atmospheric science for more than five decades, until its catastrophic collapse in December 2020. This Colloquium focuses on Arecibo’s enduring legacy in radio astronomy, offering a historical perspective that emphasizes how successive major upgrades of the telescope continuously expanded its observational capabilities and scientific impact. It presents Arecibo’s most influential contributions in topics as diverse as pulsar studies, the mapping of neutral hydrogen (HI) in the Milky Way and other galaxies, the characterization of the interstellar medium, the imaging of extragalactic radio sources with very long baseline interferometry (VLBI), the search for extraterrestrial intelligence (SETI), and being a major contributor to the first-ever detection of a stochastic gravitational-wave background.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011004] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: A historical review of the Arecibo radio telescope's contributions to astronomy and atmospheric science.
motivation: To document the legacy of the Arecibo Observatory and its impact on radio astronomy.
method: Historical narrative and summary of key scientific results from the telescope's operation.
result: Arecibo made major contributions to pulsar studies, HI mapping, VLBI, SETI, and gravitational-wave detection.
conclusion: Arecibo's upgrades and long operation enabled diverse scientific breakthroughs, cementing its legacy.

title: Colloquium: Geospace Pathfinder Science At Arecibo Observatory
authors: J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, And Shikha Raizada
abstract:
Author(s): J. D. Mathews, M. P. Sulzer, and Shikha Raizada

The Arecibo Observatory housed the largest single-aperture radio telescope for approximately 50 years. A major scientific focus was studying the upper atmosphere; its highly sensitive radar facility, combined with lidars, optical sensors, and satellite-based systems, enabled unprecedented studies of ionospheric physics based on incoherent scattering of radio waves off free electrons. After establishing the fundamental concepts and observables of the incoherent scattering radar technique, this Colloquium reviews key advances obtained with the Arecibo suite of instruments in multiple areas of geospace science, including plasma physics, space weather, lidar studies of atomic metals in the ionosphere, and ionosphere-magnetosphere coupling.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011005] Published Tue Mar 31, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews geospace science advances achieved using the Arecibo Observatory's incoherent scatter radar and ancillary instruments.
motivation: To summarize key scientific contributions from the Arecibo Observatory in upper atmospheric and ionospheric physics, highlighting the capabilities of its unique radar facility.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes results from incoherent scatter radar measurements, lidar observations, and satellite data to study ionospheric plasma, space weather, and neutral metal layers.
result: The review covers advances in understanding ionospheric plasma physics, space weather effects, and the coupling between the ionosphere and magnetosphere, enabled by Arecibo's multi-instrument suite.
conclusion: The Arecibo Observatory has been instrumental in advancing geospace science, and its closure leaves a gap in observational capabilities for upper atmospheric research.

title: Colloquium: Convection-cloud Chambers: Experiment And Theory
authors: Steven Krueger And Raymond A. Shaw
abstract:
Author(s): Steven Krueger and Raymond A. Shaw

In warm clouds, drops grow into raindrops through both condensation and collision coalescence, but the observed rapid transition between these mechanisms remains difficult to theoretically explain. The convection-cloud chamber, which reproduces key phenomena such as turbulent fluctuations in droplet concentrations and supersaturation under controlled laboratory conditions, offers a promising approach to addressing this long-standing bottleneck in understanding in cloud physics. This Colloquium reviews the physics underlying the precipitation bottleneck, examines how convection-cloud chambers capture the essential processes, and synthesizes insights from experiments, theory, and computational models that bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 011001] Published Wed Feb 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews convection-cloud chambers as a laboratory tool to study the precipitation bottleneck in warm clouds.
motivation: Understanding the rapid transition from condensation to collision-coalescence in warm clouds is a long-standing problem in cloud physics.
method: The authors review experimental, theoretical, and computational studies of convection-cloud chambers that reproduce key cloud phenomena under controlled conditions.
result: Convection-cloud chambers provide insights into turbulent fluctuations and supersaturation that help explain the precipitation bottleneck.
conclusion: The convection-cloud chamber is a promising approach to bridge laboratory and atmospheric scales for cloud physics research.

title: Colloquium: The Cosmic Dipole Anomaly
authors: Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, And Subir Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Nathan Secrest, Sebastian von Hausegger, Mohamed Rameez, Roya Mohayaee, and Subir Sarkar

The cosmological principle, which states that the Universe must be statistically isotropic and homogeneous on large scales, is a foundational principle of the standard model of cosmology, known as lambda cold dark matter (ΛCDM). The validity of this principle can be tested by assessing the compatibility of a dipole anisotropy in the large-scale distribution of matter with the dipole observed in the cosmic microwave background, interpreted in the ΛCDM model as due to our local peculiar motion. This Colloquium describes the methodology for such a test and presents its outcome based on the analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars, revealing a significant inconsistency between the two dipoles. The authors review these recent findings, as well as potential biases, systematic issues, and alternate interpretations, and discuss how this anomaly could challenge the standard description of our Universe based on the ΛCDM model.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 041001] Published Thu Dec 11, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the cosmic dipole anomaly, a potential challenge to the cosmological principle and ΛCDM model, based on large-scale structure surveys.
motivation: To test the cosmological principle by comparing the dipole anisotropy in the distribution of radio galaxies and quasars with the cosmic microwave background dipole.
method: Analysis of recent large catalogs of radio galaxies and quasars to measure the dipole in the matter distribution and compare it with the CMB dipole.
result: A significant inconsistency is found between the two dipoles, suggesting a possible violation of the cosmological principle.
conclusion: The cosmic dipole anomaly may challenge the standard ΛCDM model, but further investigation of biases and systematics is needed.

title: Astrophysical Tests Of Dark Matter Self-interactions
authors: Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, And Jesús Zavala
abstract:
Author(s): Susmita Adhikari, Arka Banerjee, Kimberly K. Boddy, Francis-Yan Cyr-Racine, Harry Desmond, Cora Dvorkin, Bhuvnesh Jain, Felix Kahlhoefer, Manoj Kaplinghat, Anna Nierenberg, Annika H. G. Peter, Andrew Robertson, Jeremy Sakstein, and Jesús Zavala

Dark sectors, involving new particles that couple very weakly to the standard model ones, play an important role in current model-building efforts in particle physics, as they allow, for example, for new dark matter production and interaction mechanisms. This review focuses on self-interacting dark matter scenarios, their implications on the dynamics and distribution of dark matter halos in the Universe, and the related astrophysical tests and observations, from galaxies to large-scale structures. It is embedded in the framework of the Novel Probes Project, a forum connecting observers and theorists involved in the study of astrophysical tests of dark-sector interactions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045004] Published Mon Dec 08, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews astrophysical tests of dark matter self-interactions, focusing on dark sector models and their implications for dark matter halo dynamics.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter, particularly self-interacting dark matter scenarios, and to connect particle physics models with astrophysical observations.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes results from simulations and observations of dark matter halos across scales from galaxies to large-scale structures.
result: It summarizes current constraints on dark matter self-interaction cross-sections and discusses how future observations can further test these models.
conclusion: Self-interacting dark matter remains a viable candidate, and upcoming astrophysical surveys will provide more stringent tests.

title: Gas Bubble Dynamics
authors: Dominique Legendre And Roberto Zenit
abstract:
Author(s): Dominique Legendre and Roberto Zenit

The motion of gas bubbles in liquids plays a vital role in numerous natural, industrial, and everyday phenomena. Unlike solid particles, gas bubbles are nearly weightless and highly responsive to forces from the surrounding fluid. Their dynamics are affected by added mass acceleration and deformable surfaces, and also by interactions with turbulent flows, other bubbles, and walls, with liquid rheology and surfactants further influencing their behavior. This review examines the intricate behavior of noncondensable gas bubbles, highlighting key advances over the past 20 years. Key topics include turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes, offering insights to enhance modeling and guide future research in two-phase flow systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025001] Published Thu Apr 17, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews the dynamics of gas bubbles in liquids, covering turbulence, non-Newtonian fluids, and electrolytes.
motivation: Understanding gas bubble dynamics is crucial for many natural and industrial processes, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The review synthesizes advances over the past 20 years, focusing on key topics like turbulence and non-Newtonian effects.
result: Key advances in bubble dynamics are highlighted, but no quantum-related results are presented.
conclusion: The paper provides insights for modeling two-phase flows, but is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Wrinkles, Creases, And Cusps In Growing Soft Matter
authors: Martine Ben Amar
abstract:
Author(s): Martine Ben Amar

The buckling of a material surface subject to compression or growth is a ubiquitous phenomenon, arising in materials science contexts such as the swelling of gels as well as in biological contexts such as morphogenesis and embryogenesis. A complete understanding of the creases and sharp cusps that commonly accompany buckling requires nonlinear elasticity theory. [Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015004] Published Mon Feb 24, 2025.

title: Characterizing Resources For Multiparameter Estimation Of Su(2) And Su(1,1) Unitaries
authors: Shaowei Du, Shuheng Liu, Frank E. S. Steinhoff, And Giuseppe Vitagliano
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2130 (2026).

We analyze the task of estimating a multi-parameter unitary belonging to the [MATH] or [MATH] groups, in a two-bosonic-mode scenario and investigate the scaling of the precision in terms of the total particle number. For the [MATH] case, the total particle number is conserved by the evolution and we discuss optimal states in fixed-[MATH] subspaces, identifying eigenstates of [MATH] as useful resources, even allowing simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. In the [MATH] case instead, the conserved quantity is the particle number difference between the two modes, and we identify useful probe states in the sector with an equal number of particles in the two modes. These states are analogous to the [MATH] case and would also allow simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. We then consider the more pragmatic scenario of an estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables, which we restrict to be the first two moments of the generators. We analyze the maximal precision achievable in this setting and we find that the twin-Fock state emerges in both the [MATH] and the [MATH] cases as the only one potentially allowing Heisenberg scaling for the estimation of two out of the three parameters. As a complement, we also consider other probe states with fluctuating number of particles, with measurements restricted to quadratic expressions in the mode operators. In this scenario, simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in multiple parameters seems mostly forbidden, with the only exception being an input two-mode squeezed state for the estimation of a two-parameter [MATH]. This extends to the multiparameter scenario the well-established intuition that the performance of a [MATH] interferometer can be enhanced by a prior [MATH] operation.

title: Propagation And Collisionless Damping Of Topologically-protected Surface Plasma Waves In Non-uniformly Magnetized Plasma Columns
authors: Roopendra Singh Rajawat And Gennady Shvets
abstract: Recent theoretical studies revealed the existence of topologically-protected surface plasma waves (TSPWs) in uniformly magnetized cold plasma columns. Reflections-free propagation of the TSPWs along arbitrarily-shaped plasma boundaries oriented perpendicularly to the magnetic field was shown to be preserved even when their collisionless damping by localized upper-hybrid resonances was accounted for. Here we extend this theory to the realistic case of three-dimensional magnetic field produced by finite-sized magnetic coils. We demonstrate that when TSPWs are launched in the direction of the decreasing magnetic field, they are collisionlessly absorbed within a highly localized (evanescent) region as they propagate away from the magnetic coil. We show that the resulting wave reflection can be negligible—in clear contrast with wave reflection from the corresponding evanescence regions of unmagnetized non-uniform plasmas.
tldr: This paper studies topologically-protected surface plasma waves in non-uniformly magnetized plasma columns, focusing on their propagation and collisionless damping.
motivation: To extend the theory of topologically-protected surface plasma waves from uniformly magnetized to realistic three-dimensional magnetic fields, and to understand their absorption and reflection properties.
method: The authors theoretically analyze wave propagation in a cold plasma column with a non-uniform magnetic field produced by finite-sized coils, using a model that accounts for collisionless damping by upper-hybrid resonances.
result: They find that waves launched in the direction of decreasing magnetic field are collisionlessly absorbed in a localized evanescent region, with negligible reflection, contrasting with unmagnetized non-uniform plasmas.
conclusion: The study demonstrates robust, reflection-free absorption of topologically-protected surface plasma waves in realistic non-uniform magnetic fields, which may have applications in plasma heating or wave manipulation.

title: Search For Decays Of The Higgs Boson Into Pair-produced Pseudoscalar Particles Decaying Into Τ + ...
authors: The ATLAS Collaboration
abstract: A search for a pair of low-mass pseudoscalars that promptly decay into -leptons is presented using 140 fb of proton–proton collision data at TeV centre-of-mass energy recorded with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The result is used to place constraints on exotic decays of the Higgs boson into four -leptons, . This search focuses on events with either one or two -leptons decaying into hadrons and neutrinos, and the remaining three or two -leptons decaying into either electron or muon and neutrinos. No significant excess is observed above the expected Standard Model background and upper limits at the 95% confidence level on are set ranging from 0.06 to 0.23, depending on the mass ranging from 15 to 60 GeV.
tldr: This paper reports an ATLAS search for Higgs boson decays to pseudoscalars decaying to tau leptons, finding no significant excess and setting upper limits.
motivation: To probe exotic decays of the Higgs boson beyond the Standard Model, specifically decays into a pair of pseudoscalar particles that subsequently decay into tau leptons.
method: Analysis of 140 fb^-1 of proton-proton collision data at sqrt(s)=13 TeV recorded by the ATLAS detector, selecting events with one or two hadronically decaying taus and the remaining taus decaying to electrons or muons.
result: No significant excess over Standard Model background is observed; 95% CL upper limits on the branching ratio are set between 0.06 and 0.23 for pseudoscalar masses from 15 to 60 GeV.
conclusion: The search constrains exotic Higgs decays to four tau leptons, but does not fit the user's research interests in quantum information theory, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Causality Of Ultrafast Photoionization From Argon 3 S Usin...
authors: Rezvan Tahouri And Jan Marcus Dahlström
abstract: We study real-time photoionization flux at the Amusia–Cooper minimum (ACM) in argon using ab initio simulations with the relativistic time-dependent configuration-interaction singles (RTDCIS) method in length (LG) and velocity (VG) gauges. A simple analytical model is used to interpret the results, and to construct Wigner delays and Wigner distributions for both gauges and relativistic channels of the photoelectron ( with and ). The two gauges are found to produce qualitatively different ionization dynamics, with LG having positive and VG having negative Wigner delays. The advancement of several femtoseconds, found for Wigner delays in VG, raises some concern for causality when atoms are ionized by attosecond pulses that are shorter than the absolute value of the Wigner delay. Reassuringly, numerical simulations of wave packets with RTDCIS show that the electrons behave in a causal way in both gauges. Weighted delays that take into account the temporal window of excitation (or the bandwidth of the pulses) are constructed from the Wigner distribution to reach agreement between the numerical simulations and our simple wave packet model. Furthermore, a strong effect of spin–orbit coupling of the photoelectron ( ) is reported for ultrafast photoionization dynamics, and Schrödinger kitten and cat states are identified in the Wigner distributions as a result of the ACM. Our work paves the way for a deeper understanding of ultrafast photoionization and the role of causality in systems with strong electron–electron correlation effects.

title: Defect Approach To Giant Graviton Dynamics
authors: Yunfeng Jiang And Xinan Zhou Junding Chen
abstract: We develop a framework of zero dimensional defects for analyzing light–light–heavy–heavy (LLHH) correlators in conformal field theories. We specifically apply this formalism to correlators of giant gravitons in super Yang–Mills to probe the nontrivial physics beyond planarity. By combining this framework with bootstrap techniques, we compute all four-point functions at strong coupling involving two maximal giant gravitons and two supergravitons of arbitrary dimensions. We identify a partially broken, higher-dimensional hidden symmetry—a defect extension of 10d hidden conformal symmetry–present at both strong and weak coupling, which allows these correlators to be packaged into a single generating function. Furthermore, we perform a systematic OPE analysis of the strong-coupling correlators, extracting the complete spectrum of anomalous dimensions for the defect-channel double-particle operators. Finally, we argue that the defect perspective provides the natural nonperturbative description for any LLHH correlator by showing that four-point conformal blocks reduce to defect two-point blocks in the heavy limit.
tldr: This paper develops a defect framework for analyzing LLHH correlators in CFT, applied to giant gravitons in super Yang-Mills, and uncovers hidden symmetries.
motivation: To understand non-planar corrections in AdS/CFT by studying correlators involving heavy operators like giant gravitons.
method: Combines zero-dimensional defect formalism with bootstrap techniques to compute four-point functions at strong coupling.
result: Identifies a partially broken 10d hidden conformal symmetry and extracts the full spectrum of anomalous dimensions for defect-channel operators.
conclusion: The defect perspective provides a natural nonperturbative description for LLHH correlators, with potential applications beyond the specific model.

title: Orthogonal Phase Modulation And Lissajous Mode Decoupling In Light-induced Thermoelastic Spectroscopy For Real-time Multi-component Gas Sensing
authors: Hanxu Ma, Shunda Qiao, Ying He, Haiyue Sun And Yufei Ma
abstract: This paper proposed an optical detection mechanism that utilized orthogonal phase modulation (OPM) and Lissajous mode decoupling within a light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy (LITES) sensor for the first time, enabling real-time multi-component gas sensing. By establishing a two-dimensional forced vibration model of a quartz tuning fork (QTF) under dual-path OPM, it revealed the vibration mode coupling mechanism induced by non-ideal phase and amplitude conditions, thereby providing a theoretical basis and optimization pathway for suppressing channel crosstalk. In the OPM-LITES sensor, two continuous-wave distributed feedback lasers were modulated by sinusoidal waves with the same frequency (f0/2, where f0 is the resonant frequency of the QTF) but a phase difference of 45°. The combined beam, after wavelength division multiplexing, co-excited the self-designed low-frequency QTF. The piezoelectric signal generated by the QTF underwent orthogonal demodulation via a lock-in amplifier (LIA). The concentration information for the two gases was independently retrieved from the decoupled X-component and Y-component of the LIA. Experimental results demonstrated that the OPM-LITES sensor exhibited excellent linear responses to both methane (CH4) and acetylene (C2H2), with average relative systematic errors of 0.54% and 0.79%, and maximum relative errors of 1.72% and 1.38%, respectively. Allan deviation analysis indicated that the minimum detection limits (MDLs) for CH4 and C2H2 reached 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, with normalized noise-equivalent absorption coefficients of 5.09 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2 and 6.18 × 10−9 cm−1·W·Hz−1/2, respectively. This study not only provided a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection but also established a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling and signal processing in spectroscopic sensing.
tldr: This paper presents a novel optical gas sensing technique using orthogonal phase modulation and Lissajous mode decoupling in light-induced thermoelastic spectroscopy for real-time multi-component gas detection.
motivation: Real-time multi-component gas sensing is important for environmental monitoring and industrial safety, but existing methods suffer from channel crosstalk and complexity.
method: Two continuous-wave lasers are modulated with same frequency but 45° phase difference, combined via wavelength division multiplexing, and co-excite a quartz tuning fork. The piezoelectric signal is orthogonally demodulated to retrieve concentration information for two gases independently.
result: The sensor achieves excellent linear responses for methane and acetylene with low systematic errors (0.54% and 0.79%) and detection limits of 0.32 ppm and 0.29 ppm, respectively.
conclusion: The proposed OPM-LITES sensor provides a simple and efficient solution for real-time multi-component gas detection with a novel theoretical framework for mode decoupling.

motivation: Antibiotic resistance is a growing crisis driven by selective pressure; new strategies to kill resistant bacteria without affecting susceptible ones are needed.
